entry.title: Set Prediction for Next-Day Active Fire Forecasting

author.name: Yuchen Bai, Georgios Athanasiou, Xin Yu, Diogenis Antonopoulos, Ioannis Papoutsis, Stijn Hantson, Nuno Carvalhais

entry.summary: Proposes WISP, a set prediction model for next-day active fire forecasting that predicts point-sets of fire locations rather than grid-based probability maps, using meteorological and satellite data.

entry.title: PC3D: Zero-Shot Cooperation Across Variable Rosters via Personalized Context Distillation

author.name: Ahmet Onur Akman, Rafa{\l} Kucharski

entry.summary: Proposes PC3D for multi-agent RL with variable team sizes, training decentralized policies to infer and adapt to team composition without communication or retraining at execution time.

entry.title: QT-Net: Rethinking Evaluation of AI Models in Atomic Chemical Space

author.name: Pablo Mart\'inez Crespo, Stefano Ribes, Martin Rahm, Richard Beckmann, Robert S. Jordan, Marisa Gliege, Santiago Miret, Vijay Kris Narasimhan, Roc\'io Mercado

entry.summary: Proposes a held-out evaluation protocol for atomic property prediction using SOAP descriptor clustering, and compares E(3)-equivariant vs. non-equivariant models for electron populations and multipole prediction.

entry.title: Compander-Aligned Query Geometry for Quantized Zeroth-Order Optimization

author.name: Yao Shu, Zilin Zhu

entry.summary: Addresses the challenge of zeroth-order optimization with quantized model evaluations, identifying 'query geometry' as the key missing concept when using non-uniform companding quantizers. Proposes methods to align ZO queries with the quantization codebook structure.

entry.title: Domain-Adaptive Arrhythmia Classification Using a Hybrid Transformer on Wearable Heart Signals

author.name: Maedeh H. Toosi, Siamak Mohammadi

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid transformer model for arrhythmia classification on wearable ECG devices that processes both raw signals and HRV features, with domain adaptation to handle distribution shifts between clinical and wearable data.

entry.title: Survey-aware Machine Learning: A Guideline for Valid Population Health Inference based on Scoping Review

author.name: YongKyung Oh, Henry W. Zheng, Jeffrey Feng, Alex A. T. Bui

entry.summary: Proposes Survey-aware Machine Learning (SaML), a nine-step guideline for incorporating survey design metadata (sampling weights, stratification) across the ML lifecycle for valid population health inference.

entry.title: LLiMba: Sardinian on a Single GPU -- Adapting a 3B Language Model to a Vanishing Romance Language

author.name: Luca Ballore

entry.summary: Presents LLiMba, a 3B parameter model adapted for Sardinian language from Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct using continued pretraining on 11.5M tokens, demonstrating feasibility of single-GPU adaptation for low-resource languages.

entry.title: Towards Trustworthy Audio Deepfake Detection: A Systematic Framework for Diagnosing and Mitigating Gender Bias

author.name: Aishwarya Fursule, Shruti Kshirsagar, Anderson R. Avila

entry.summary: Presents the first diagnosis-first framework for gender bias in audio deepfake detection, identifying bias sources (representation differences, feature leakage) before applying targeted mitigation.

entry.title: Discriminative Span as a Predictor of Synthetic Data Utility via Classifier Reconstruction

author.name: Radhika Amar Desai, Modigari Narendra

entry.summary: Proposes a geometry-driven metric in foundation model embedding space to predict synthetic data utility for binary classification without requiring model training.

entry.title: Cross-Domain Lossy Compression via Constrained Minimum Entropy Coupling

author.name: Nam Nguyen, Hassan Tavakoli, An Vuong, Thinh Nguyen, Bella Bose

entry.summary: Studies cross-domain lossy compression through minimum entropy coupling with rate and classification constraints, maximizing coupling strength between source and reconstruction under target distribution constraints.

entry.title: APEX: Audio Prototype EXplanations for Classification Tasks

author.name: Piotr Kawa, Kornel Howil, Piotr Borycki, Mi{\l}osz Adamczyk, Przemys{\l}aw Spurek, Piotr Syga

entry.summary: Introduces APEX, a post-hoc explainability framework for audio classifiers that disentangles explanations into four perspectives (square, time, frequency, audio-based prototypes). Requires no fine-tuning and preserves output invariance.

entry.title: MARGIN: Margin-Aware Regularized Geometry for Imbalanced Vulnerability Detection

author.name: Yuteng Zhang, Huifang Ma, Jiahui Wei, Qingqing Li, Yafei Yang

entry.summary: Proposes MARGIN, a metric-based framework for software vulnerability detection that addresses frequency and difficulty imbalance through adaptive margin metric learning and hyperspherical prototype modeling using von Mises-Fisher distributions.

entry.title: Priority-Driven Control and Communication in Decentralized Multi-Agent Systems via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Qingyun Guo, Junyi Shi, Tomasz Piotr Kucner, Dominik Baumann

entry.summary: Proposes a model-free RL algorithm that jointly learns communication priorities and control policies in decentralized multi-agent systems, avoiding hybrid action spaces typical in event-triggered control.

entry.title: The Translation Tax Is Not a Scalar: A Counterfactual Audit of English-Source Cue Inheritance in Chinese Multilingual Benchmarks

author.name: Zezheng Lin, Fengming Liu, Handi Li

entry.summary: Audits the 'Translation Tax' assumption in English-to-Chinese benchmark translation, finding that score inflation is not a simple scalar but varies by model family and item characteristics through multiple proxy estimators.

entry.title: Quality-Conditioned Agreement in Automated Short Answer Scoring: Mid-Range Degradation and the Impact of Task-Specific Adaptation

author.name: Abigail Victoria Gurin Schleifer, Moriah Ariely, Beata Beigman Klebanov, Asaf Salman, Giora Alexandron

entry.summary: Studies quality-conditioned agreement in automated short answer scoring, finding that mid-range (partially correct) responses are hardest for models. Compares GPT-5.2, GPT-4o, Claude Opus 4.5 with fine-tuned BERT and human experts.

entry.title: Accurate and Efficient Statistical Testing for Word Semantic Breadth

author.name: Yo Ehara

entry.summary: Proposes accurate statistical testing for comparing word semantic breadth (contextual diversity) from token embeddings, addressing how direction differences can masquerade as dispersion differences and inflate Type-I errors.

entry.title: On the Complexity of the Matching Problem of Regular Expressions with Backreferences

author.name: Soh Kumabe, Yuya Uezato

entry.summary: Studies computational complexity of regular expression matching with backreferences, motivated by ReDoS attacks. Analyzes whether provably efficient near-linear-time matching engines are possible for practical regex features.

entry.title: An Efficient Token Compression Framework for Visual Object Tracking

author.name: Weijing Wu, Qihua Liang, Bineng Zhong, Haiying Xia, Zhiyi Mo, Shuxiang Song

entry.summary: Proposes ETCTrack, a compress-then-interact tracking framework that efficiently compresses template tokens from historical frames into compact representations before interaction with search tokens.

entry.title: UIESNN: A Scale-Aware Spiking Network for Underwater Image Enhancement

author.name: Shuang Chen, Ruochen Li, Zihan Zhu, Ronald Thenius, Farshad Arvin, Amir Atapour-Abarghouei

entry.summary: Proposes UIESNN, a spiking neural network for underwater image enhancement with a Multi-scale Pooling LIF Block that injects hierarchical pooling responses into membrane dynamics for enlarged receptive fields.

entry.title: Egocentric Whole-Body Human Mesh Recovery with Prior-Guided Learning

author.name: Soyeon Na, Seung Young Noh, Ju Yong Chang

entry.summary: Proposes a prior-guided learning framework for egocentric whole-body human mesh recovery from head-mounted cameras, constructing better pseudo-GT and leveraging priors for hands and face.

entry.title: LightAVSeg: Lightweight Audio-Visual Segmentation

author.name: Qing Zhong, Guodong Ding, Lingqiao Liu, Zaiwen Feng, Lin Yuanbo Wu, Angela Yao

entry.summary: LightAVSeg proposes a lightweight audio-visual segmentation framework that replaces heavy cross-modal attention with a decoupled design for semantic filtering and spatial grounding, achieving linear scaling with spatial resolution. An auxiliary alignment loss enforces semantic consistency during training with zero inference overhead.

entry.title: An Elastic Shape Variational Autoencoder for Skeleton Pose Trajectories

author.name: Arafat Rahman, Shashwat Kumar, Laura E. Barnes, Anuj Srivastava

entry.summary: ES-VAE proposes a geometry-aware variational autoencoder for skeletal trajectories using the TSRVF representation on Kendall's shape manifold, inherently removing nuisance factors like camera orientation and scale.

entry.title: SoccerLens: Grounded Soccer Video Understanding Beyond Accuracy

author.name: Ismael Elsharkawi, Ahmed Sait, Silvio Giancola, Bernard Ghanem, Hossam Sharara, Abdelrahman Eldesokey

entry.summary: SoccerLens benchmark evaluates whether VLMs use meaningful visual evidence or spurious correlations for soccer video understanding, with structured visual cues at three levels of semantic relevance.

entry.title: DAP: Doppler-aware Point Network for Heterogeneous mmWave Action Recognition

author.name: Jiaying Lin, Shiman Wu, Jinfu Liu, Can Wang, Mengyuan Liu

entry.summary: DAP-Net addresses heterogeneous mmWave radar action recognition with a Doppler-aware network and introduces UniMM-HAR, the largest multi-source mmWave point cloud HAR dataset.

entry.title: MOTOR-Bench: A Real-world Dataset and Multi-agent Framework for Zero-shot Human Mental State Understanding

author.name: Xiaoyu Yuan, Niklas Heikkala, Tiina T\"orm\"anen, Hanna J\"arvenoja, Guoying Zhao, Haoyu Chen

entry.summary: MOTOR-Bench introduces a benchmark with 1,440 multimodal video clips for understanding human mental states in collaborative learning, labeled by educational experts. Evaluates state-of-the-art MLLMs on structured mental state analysis.

entry.title: DRIVE-C: A Controlled Corruption Dataset for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Shiva Aher

entry.summary: DRIVE-C is a controlled corruption dataset for evaluating visual perception robustness in autonomous driving, with 600 corrupted clips spanning 12 degradation types across five severity levels.

entry.title: Clip-level Uncertainty and Temporal-aware Active Learning for End-to-End Multi-Object Tracking

author.name: Riku Inoue, Shogo Sato, Kazuhiko Murasaki, Tomoyasu Shimada, Toshihiko Nishimura, Ryuichi Tanida

entry.summary: Proposes clip-level active learning for end-to-end multi-object tracking, formulating uncertainty at the clip level to align with modern transformer-based tracker architectures that operate on multi-frame clips.

entry.title: Hystar: Hypernetwork-driven Style-adaptive Retrieval via Dynamic SVD Modulation

author.name: Yujia Cai, Boxuan Li, Chenghao Xu, Jiexi Yan

entry.summary: Hystar uses a hypernetwork to dynamically adapt CLIP model weights via SVD perturbations for style-adaptive image retrieval, enabling robust performance across diverse query styles like sketches and artworks.

entry.title: BathyFacto: Refraction-Aware Two-Media Neural Radiance Fields for Bathymetry

author.name: Markus Brezovsky, Anatol G\"unthner, Frederik Schulte, Lukas Winiwarter, Boris Jutzi, Gottfried Mandlburger

entry.summary: BathyFacto extends Nerfacto for refraction-aware underwater scene reconstruction, modeling two-media ray tracing with Snell's law for metrically precise bathymetry from UAV imagery.

entry.title: Increasing the Efficiency of DETR for Maritime High-Resolution Images

author.name: Tinsae Yehuala, Hao Cheng, Ville Lehtola

entry.summary: This paper leverages Vision Mamba backbones for efficient maritime object detection in high-resolution imagery, achieving linear scaling with sequence length for real-time detection on edge devices.

entry.title: BGG: Bridging the Geometric Gap between Cross-View images by Vision Foundation Model Adaptation for Geo-Localization

author.name: Wei Wang, Dou Quan, Ning Huyan, Shuang Wang, Yi Li, Pei He, Licheng Jiao

entry.summary: BGG adapts vision foundation models (DINOv3) for cross-view geo-localization between drone and satellite views through parameter-efficient adaptation that bridges geometric gaps.

entry.title: Automated Detection of Abnormalities in Zebrafish Development

author.name: Sarath Sivaprasad, Hui-Po Wang, Anna-Lisa J\"ackel, Jonas Baumann, Carole Baumann, Jennifer Herrmann, Mario Fritz

entry.summary: This paper introduces a large-scale zebrafish embryo development dataset with expert annotations for fertility classification and toxicity assessment, benchmarking automated detection of developmental abnormalities.

entry.title: Cross-Modal Semantic-Enhanced Diffusion Framework for Diabetic Retinopathy Grading

author.name: Yiqun Wang (Beijing Jiaotong University)

entry.summary: Proposes CLIP-Guided Semantic Diffusion (CGSD) for diabetic retinopathy grading that integrates vision-language pretraining with diffusion probabilistic modeling, using LoRA-adapted domain-specific CLIP as semantic guidance.

entry.title: Meta-Black-Box Optimization Can Do Search Guidance for Expensive Constrained Multi-Objective Optimization

author.name: Yukun Du, Haiyue Yu, Jiang Jiang, Shuaiwen Tang, Xiaotong Xie, Haobo Liu, Chongshuang Hu, Shengkun Chang

entry.summary: MetaSG-SAEA proposes a meta-black-box optimization framework that provides search guidance for expensive constrained multi-objective optimization, using diffusion-based population initialization and a novel constraint-calibrated inequality measure.

entry.title: Energy-Efficient Implementation of Spiking Recurrent Cells on FPGA

author.name: Pascal Harmeling, Florent De Geeter, Guillaume Drion

entry.summary: Presents an FPGA accelerator for spiking neural networks using Spiking Recurrent Cell neurons, with mathematical simplifications removing costly operations while maintaining biologically plausible dynamics.

entry.title: Model-Reference Adaptive Flight Control of the 95-mg Bee++

author.name: Francisco M. F. R. Gon\c{c}alves, Conor K. Trygstad, N\'estor O. P\'erez-Arancibia

entry.summary: Introduces MRAC architecture for positional tracking of the 95-mg Bee++ insect-scale flapping-wing aerial vehicle, demonstrated through real-time flight experiments.

entry.title: PECMAN: Perception-enabled Collaborative Multi-Agent Navigation in Unknown Environments

author.name: Tianchonghui Fang, Shaunak Roy, Shalabh Gupta

entry.summary: PECMAN extends SMART-3D tree morphing to multi-agent navigation with shared perception in unknown environments, using distributed tree repair and collaborative obstacle discovery.

entry.title: High Precision Hydraulic Excavator Control for Heavy-Duty Grading

author.name: Lennart Werner, Pol Eyschen, Sean Costello, Andrei Cramariuc, Marco Hutter

entry.summary: Presents an autonomous controller for high-precision heavy-duty excavator grading that works across different hydraulic architectures (Load Sensing and Negative Flow Control) with a hydraulic-aware low-level loop.

entry.title: MVB-Grasp: Minimum-Volume-Box Filtering of Diffusion-based Grasps for Frontal Manipulation

author.name: Bibek Poudel, Abdul Basit, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: MVB-Grasp injects minimum volume bounding box geometric priors into diffusion-based grasp generation for frontal manipulation on workspace-constrained robots, improving success rates by filtering infeasible grasps.

entry.title: EFGCL: Learning Dynamic Motion through Spotting-Inspired External Force Guided Curriculum Learning

author.name: Keita Yoneda, Kento Kawaharazuka, Kei Okada

entry.summary: Proposes External Force Guided Curriculum Learning (EFGCL), inspired by spotting in gymnastics, where external assistive forces during training help legged robots learn dynamic motions like backflips without reward shaping or reference trajectories.

entry.title: VISOR: A Vision-Language Model-based Test Oracle for Testing Robot

author.name: Prasun Saurabh, Pablo Valle, Aitor Arrieta, Shaukat Ali, Paolo Arcaini

entry.summary: Proposes VISOR, a VLM-based automated test oracle for robot testing that replaces expensive human evaluations with automated assessment of task correctness and quality, going beyond pass/fail judgments of symbolic oracles.

entry.title: Decentralized Contingency MPC based on Safe Sets for Nonlinear Multi-agent Collision Avoidance

author.name: Max Studt, Georg Schildbach

entry.summary: Develops a decentralized contingency MPC framework for multi-agent collision avoidance with nonlinear dynamics that achieves collision-free motion under a state-only information pattern without trajectory communication between agents.

entry.title: Minimax Optimal Estimation of Transport-Growth Pairs in Unbalanced Optimal Transport

author.name: Donlapark Ponnoprat, Noboru Isobe, Masaaki Imaizumi

entry.summary: Studies minimax optimal estimation of transport-growth pairs in unbalanced optimal transport with quadratic cost and KL penalties, developing estimators that achieve optimal rates and proving matching lower bounds.

entry.title: A PAC-Bayes Approach for Controlling Unknown Linear Discrete-time Systems

author.name: Yujia Luo, Ye Pu, Jonathan H. Manton, Jingge Zhu

entry.summary: Presents a PAC-Bayes framework for learning controllers for unknown stochastic linear systems, deriving data-dependent bounds on learned controller performance with guarantees for unbounded quadratic cost.

entry.title: AI companies are already profitable (in the way that matters)

author.name: Yair Halberstadt

entry.summary: Argues that AI companies are already profitable on marginal serving costs (the cost per API call is below its price), and that infrastructure spending is investment rather than operational loss, countering narratives about unsustainable AI business models.

entry.title: Post-training makes large language models less human-like

author.name: Marcel Binz, Elif Akata, Abdullah Almaatouq, Mohammed Alsobay, Oleksii Ariasov, Franziska Br\"andle, David Broska, Jason W. Burton, Nuno Busch, Frederick Callaway, Vanessa Cheung, Brian Christian, Julian Coda-Forno, Can Demircan, Vittoria Dentella, Maria K. Eckstein, No\'emi \'Eltet\H{o}, Michael Franke, Thomas L. Griffiths, Fritz G\"unther, Susanne Haridi, Sebastian Hellmann, Stefan Herytash, Linus Hof, Eleanor Holton, Isabelle Hoxha, Zak Hussain, Akshay Jagadish, Elif Kara, Valentin Kriegmair, Evelina Leivada, Li Ji-An, Tobias Ludwig, Maximilian Maier, Marcelo G. Mattar, Marvin Mathony, Alireza Modirshanechi, Robin Na, Mariia Nadverniuk, Antonios Nasioulas, Surabhi S. Nath, Helen Niemeyer, Kate Nussenbaum, Sebastian Olschewski, Thorsten Pachur, Stefano Palminteri, Aliona Petrenco, Camille V. Phaneuf-Hadd, Angelo Pirrone, Manuel Rausch, Laura Raveling, Shashank Reddy, Milena Rmus, Evan M. Russek, Tankred Saanum, Kai Sandbrink, Louis Schiekiera, Johannes A. Schubert, Luca M. Schulze Buschoff, Nishad Singhi, Leah H. Somerville, Mikhail S. Spektor, Xin Sui, Christopher Summerfield, Mirko Thalmann, Anna I. Thoma, Taisiia Tikhomirova, Vuong Truong, Polina Tsvilodub, Konstantinos Voudouris, Robert C. Wilson, Kristin Witte, Shuchen Wu, Dirk U. Wulff, Hua-Dong Xiong, Songlin Xu, Lance Ying, Xinyu Zhang, Jian-Qiao Zhu, Eric Schulz

entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, Introduces Psych-201 dataset and finds that post-training (turning base models into assistants) consistently reduces behavioral alignment with humans across model families. This misalignment widens in newer generations even as base models improve. Persona-induction doesn't help.

entry.title: [Linkpost] Language Models Can Autonomously Hack and Self-Replicate

author.name: Gunnar_Zarncke

entry.summary: As first reported in Reddit on Saturday, Linkpost to Palisade Research demonstrating that language models can autonomously self-replicate by exploiting web application vulnerabilities, with Qwen3.5-122B succeeding 6-19% and frontier models (Opus 4.6) reaching 81% success rates.

entry.title: OracleTSC: Oracle-Informed Reward Hurdle and Uncertainty Regularization for Traffic Signal Control

author.name: Darryl Jacob, Xinyu Liu, Muchao Ye, Xiaoyong Yuan, Pan He

entry.summary: Introduces OracleTSC for LLM-based traffic signal control that stabilizes reinforcement finetuning through reward hurdle mechanisms and uncertainty regularization, providing natural language reasoning for traffic decisions.

entry.title: E-TCAV: Formalizing Penultimate Proxies for Efficient Concept Based Interpretability

author.name: Hasib Aslam, Muhammad Ali Chattha, Muhammad Taha Mukhtar, Muhammad Imran Malik, Andreas Dengel, Sheraz Ahmed

entry.summary: Introduces E-TCAV, an efficient approximation of TCAV interpretability scores that addresses computational overhead and statistical instability. Shows that penultimate layer can serve as a reliable proxy for full TCAV computation.

entry.title: Modular Retrieval-Augmented Generalization for Human Action Recognition

author.name: Peng Liao, Shangsong Liang, Lin Chen, Peijia Zheng

entry.summary: Introduces MoRA, the first retrieval-augmented module for IMU-based human activity recognition that can be integrated into any existing HAR model. Addresses limited training samples and static knowledge utilization challenges.

entry.title: Geometric Flood Depth Estimation: Fusing Transformer-Based Segmentation with Digital Elevation Models

author.name: Nhut Le, Ehsan Karimi, Maryam Rahnemoonfar

entry.summary: Presents a geometric approach to flood depth estimation from aerial imagery by fusing Mask2Former segmentation with Digital Elevation Models to compute water surface elevation and per-pixel depth.

entry.title: Fast Training of Mixture-of-Experts for Time Series Forecasting via Expert Loss Integration

author.name: Btissame El Mahtout, Florian Ziel

entry.summary: Proposes a Mixture-of-Experts framework for time series forecasting that integrates expert-specific loss information into training, combined with partial online learning to reduce retraining costs.

entry.title: CapCLIP: A Vision-Language Representation Alignment Approach for Wireless Capsule Endoscopy Analysis

author.name: Haroon Wahab, Irfan Mehmood, Hassan Ugail

entry.summary: Introduces CapCLIP, a domain-specific CLIP adaptation for wireless capsule endoscopy that aligns capsule frames with clinically grounded textual descriptions from standardized nomenclature.

entry.title: Unified Modeling of Lane and Lane Topology for Driving Scene Reasoning

author.name: Han Li, Yulu Gao, Si Liu, Yuhang Wang, Bo Liu, Beipeng Mu

entry.summary: UniTopo presents a unified representation for lanes and lane topology in autonomous driving that models topological relationships as connected lanes, enabling simultaneous extraction of positions and topology.

entry.title: Improving Temporal Action Segmentation via Constraint-Aware Decoding

author.name: Yeo Keat Ee, Debaditya Roy, Chen Li, Hao Zhang, Basura Fernando

entry.summary: This paper proposes a constraint-based refinement framework for temporal action segmentation that integrates statistical structural priors into modified Viterbi decoding without additional training.

entry.title: M$^2$E-UAV: A Benchmark and Analysis for Onboard Motion-on-Motion Event-Based Tiny UAV Detection

author.name: Weiqi Yan, Lixin Chen, Xiangrui Hou, Zhipeng Cai, Youbiao Wang, Yangyang Shi, Yu Zang, Cheng Wang

entry.summary: M²E-UAV presents a benchmark for motion-on-motion event-based tiny UAV detection from onboard cameras, with 87K+ training samples and point-based event baselines.

entry.title: Fit CATE Once: Model-Assisted Randomization Tests Without Sample Splitting

author.name: Fangnan Zheng, Yao Zhang

entry.summary: Develops model-assisted randomization tests for panel experiments that combine flexible CATE estimation with valid randomization inference without sample splitting, by estimating an unsigned CATE from residual covariance structure.

entry.title: LGB+: A Macroeconomic Forecasting Road Test

author.name: Philippe Goulet Coulombe

entry.summary: Proposes LGB+, a gradient boosting variant that evaluates tree and linear candidates at each step, choosing the better one, to efficiently capture both linear and nonlinear patterns in small-sample macroeconomic forecasting.

entry.title: Learning the Channel Gain from Anywhere to Anywhere via Cross-environment Transformer Estimators

author.name: Prasenjit Dhara, Daniel Romero

entry.summary: Proposes cross-environment transformer estimators for channel-gain map estimation, learning spatial patterns across environments to estimate channel gain between any two locations. Addresses the challenge of 6-dimensional input space.

entry.title: Transfer Learning for Dead Fuel Moisture Prediction Using Time-Warping Recurrent Neural Networks

author.name: Jonathon Hirschi, Jan Mandel, Adam Kochanski

entry.summary: Proposes time-warping transfer learning for recurrent networks, temporally rescaling learned dynamics to transfer fuel moisture prediction models across different fuel classes (10h to 100h/1000h fuels).

entry.title: MedFL-Stress: A Systematic Robustness Evaluation of Federated Brain Tumor Segmentation under Cross-Hospital MRI Appearance Shift

author.name: Kiran Naseer, Naveed Anwer Butt

entry.summary: Introduces MedFL-Stress, a stress-testing framework for federated learning in brain tumor segmentation that exposes failure modes hidden by average performance metrics under MRI appearance shifts.

entry.title: DRIFT: Drift-Resilient Invariant-Feature Transformer for DGA Detection

author.name: Chaeyoung Lee, Chaeri Jung, Seonghoon Jeong

entry.summary: Proposes DRIFT, a Transformer-based DGA detection framework that learns invariant representations through hybrid tokenization and multi-task self-supervised pre-training. Validated through a 9-year longitudinal study showing robustness to temporal drift.

entry.title: Proximal Path-Specific Inference

author.name: Yang Bai, Sihan Wu, Baoluo Sun, Yifan Cui

entry.summary: Extends causal mediation analysis to handle unmeasured confounding using proxy variables, developing nonparametric estimators for path-specific effects with recanting witnesses through proximal confounding bridge functions.

entry.title: Multi-Fidelity Quantile Regression

author.name: Yixiang Liu, Yao Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-fidelity quantile regression method where the HF quantile is expressed as a LF quantile at a covariate-dependent level, reducing estimation to learning a smoother level function when distributional shapes are similar.

entry.title: AI-Care: A Conversational Agentic System for Task Coordination in Alzheimer's Disease Care

author.name: Preyash Yadav, Michelle Cohn, Priyanka Koppolu, Hritvik Agarwal, Amey Gohil, Tejas Patil, Sasha Pimento, Alyssa Weakley

entry.summary: Presents AI-Care, a conversational AI system built on a remote caregiving platform for Alzheimer's patients, enabling natural-language interaction for managing everyday tasks like calendar reminders through voice-first chatbot.

entry.title: Biological Plausibility and Representational Alignment of Feedback Alignment in Convolutional Networks

author.name: Jake Lance, Larry Kieu

entry.summary: Evaluates feedback alignment variants in convolutional networks against backpropagation on CIFAR-10, providing comparative analysis of biological plausibility, interpretability, and computational complexity.

entry.title: Value-Decomposed Reinforcement Learning Framework for Taxiway Routing with Hierarchical Conflict-Aware Observations

author.name: Shizhong Zhou, Haifeng Liu, Zheng Zhang, Shiyu Zhang, Bo Yang, Yi Lin

entry.summary: Presents CaTR, a reinforcement learning framework for multi-aircraft taxiway routing with hierarchical conflict-aware observations and value decomposition for real-time airport surface operations.

entry.title: WindINR: Latent-State INR for Fast Local Wind Query and Correction in Complex Terrain

author.name: Yi Xiao, Qilong Jia, Hang Fan, Pascal Fua, Robert Jenssen, Xiaosong Ma, Wei Xue

entry.summary: Presents WindINR, an implicit neural representation framework for continuous high-resolution local wind query and correction in complex terrain, with latent-state conditioning and rapid inference-time correction.

entry.title: Yield Curve Forecasting using Machine Learning and Econometrics: A Comparative Analysis

author.name: Aman Singh, Tokunbo Ogunfunmi, Sanjiv Das

entry.summary: Comprehensive comparison of econometric, classical ML, and deep learning methods for U.S. Treasury yield curve forecasting using 47 years of daily data.

entry.title: From Single-Step Edit Response to Multi-Step Molecular Optimization

author.name: Haojie Rao (School of Computer Science, Wuhan University, Wuhan, China), Kun Li (School of Computer Science, Wuhan University, Wuhan, China), Yida Xiong (School of Computer Science, Wuhan University, Wuhan, China), Jiameng Chen (School of Computer Science, Wuhan University, Wuhan, China), Wenbin Hu (School of Computer Science, Wuhan University, Wuhan, China), Yizhen Zheng (Department of Data Science and Artificial Intelligence, Monash University, Victoria, Australia), Jiajun Yu (College of Computer Science and Technology, Zhejiang University, Hangzhou, China), Duanhua Cao (School of Life Sciences and Technology, Tongji University, Shanghai, China)

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-step molecular optimization framework that decomposes property-guided molecular editing into sequential local structural edits, addressing the mismatch between pair-level supervision and action-level decisions. The approach improves data efficiency over oracle-in-the-loop methods.

entry.title: Rethinking Constraint Awareness for Efficient State Embedding of Neural Routing Solver

author.name: Canhong Yu, Changliang Zhou, Rongsheng Chen, Zhenkun Wang, Yu Zhou

entry.summary: Revisits neural routing solvers for vehicle routing problems, identifying that restricted observation space during attention computation creates bottlenecks. Proposes maintaining global observation space for better handling of complex constraints.

entry.title: Hypothesis-Driven Deep Research with Large Language Models: A Structured Methodology for Automated Knowledge Discovery

author.name: Michael Chin

entry.summary: Proposes Hypothesis-Driven Deep Research (HDRI) methodology that uses hypotheses as organizational instruments structuring the research process itself, rather than as end products. Includes six core principles and an eight-stage pipeline.

entry.title: Hierarchical Causal Abduction: A Foundation Framework for Explainable Model Predictive Control

author.name: Ramesh Arvind Naagarajan, Z\"uhal Wagner, Stefan Streif

entry.summary: Presents Hierarchical Causal Abduction (HCA) for explainable Model Predictive Control, combining physics-informed reasoning, KKT multiplier evidence, and causal discovery to explain nonlinear MPC decisions.

entry.title: GESR: A Genetic Programming-Based Symbolic Regression Method with Gene Editing

author.name: Yanjie Li, Liping Zhang, Min Wu, Weijun Li, Lina Yu, Jingyi Liu, Yusong Deng, Mingzhu Wan, Xin Ning

entry.summary: Proposes GESR, a genetic programming method for symbolic regression enhanced with 'gene editing' to make mutations more directed rather than purely random, improving discovery of mathematical formulas from data.

entry.title: Artificial Intelligence in Number Theory: LLMs for Algorithm Generation and Ensemble Methods for Conjecture Verification

author.name: Ali Saraeb

entry.summary: Evaluates Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct on algorithmic number theory tasks achieving >0.95 accuracy. Also applies ensemble ML methods for verifying number-theoretic conjectures.

entry.title: Crystal Fractional Graph Neural Network for Energy Prediction of High-Entropy Alloys

author.name: Takanori Kotama, Yang Huang

entry.summary: Proposes a crystal fractional graph neural network for predicting energy of high-entropy alloys, combining local atomic environment modeling with global compositional information through feature fusion.

entry.title: Intelligent Autonomous Orchestration for Distributed Cloud Resources using Complex-Stability Analysis

author.name: Gopal Krishna Shyam, Priyanka Bharti

entry.summary: Proposes C-SAS, an autonomous orchestration framework for distributed cloud resources using complex analysis (Argument Principle, Rouché's Theorem) to suppress oscillatory scaling operations.

entry.title: From Historical Tabular Image to Knowledge Graphs: A Provenance-Aware Modular Pipeline

author.name: Sarah Binta Alam Shoilee, Victor de Boer, Jacco van Ossenbruggen, Susan Leg\^ene

entry.summary: Presents a modular provenance-aware pipeline for converting handwritten historical tabular images into Knowledge Graphs, decomposing the workflow to enable human oversight and trust.

entry.summary: Studies network-efficient streaming of discrete world model tokens for connected vehicles, proposing an adaptive algorithm that prioritizes updates via cosine distance in codebook embedding space and triggers keyframes using Hamming-drift thresholds. Achieves significant bandwidth savings under packet loss conditions.

entry.title: Explicit Stair Geometry Conditioning for Robust Humanoid Locomotion

author.name: Jianguo Zhang, Wentai Xu, Shusheng Ye, Yuxiang He, Weimin Qi, Qinbo Sun, Ning Ding, Liguang Zhou

entry.summary: Presents an explicit stair geometry conditioning framework for humanoid stair climbing that uses compact interpretable geometric parameters (step height, depth, yaw angle) rather than high-dimensional latent terrain representations. Demonstrates improved generalization across varying stair geometries.

entry.title: VRA: Grounding Discrete-Time Joint Acceleration in Voltage-Constrained Actuation

author.name: Lingwei Zhang, Jiaming Wang, Tianlin Zhang, Zhitao Song, Xuanqi Zeng, Weipeng Xia, Zhongyu Li, Yun-hui Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Voltage-Realizable Acceleration (VRA), a joint-level acceleration interface that grounds kinematic acceleration commands in voltage-constrained actuator physics, preventing unrealizable accelerations and reducing constraint-induced oscillations.

entry.title: Minimax optimal submatrix detection: Sharp non-asymptotic rates

author.name: Parker Knight, Julien Chhor

entry.summary: Provides non-asymptotic minimax optimal bounds for detecting a hidden submatrix with elevated mean in a Gaussian matrix, deriving the smallest signal strength necessary and sufficient for reliable detection.

entry.title: When Are Trade-Off Functions Testable from Finite Samples?

author.name: Kaining Shi, Qiaosen Wang, Cong Ma

entry.summary: Studies finite-sample testability of trade-off functions (optimal Type I/II error frontiers) between unknown distributions, identifying sharp conditions under which testing becomes possible via attainability by a prescribed set class.

entry.title: How the AI Labs Make Profit (Maybe, Eventually)

author.name: mabramov

entry.summary: Analysis of how AI labs might become profitable, arguing the path includes internal deployment (spinning up AI-powered internal companies), not just selling API access or subscriptions.

entry.title: MBP-KT: Learning Global Collaborative Information from Meta-Behavioral Pattern for Enhanced Knowledge Tracing

author.name: Yuhao Jia, Duantengchuan Li, Jinsong Chen, Zhongjie Mao, Mingwen Tong, Yue Li, Xiaoguang Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a meta-behavioral pattern framework for knowledge tracing that transforms raw interaction sequences into combinations of learning patterns, extracting collaborative information to improve prediction of learner knowledge states.

entry.title: Cplus2ASP: Computing Action Language C+ in Answer Set Programming

author.name: Joseph Babb, Joohyung Lee

entry.summary: Presents Version 2 of Cplus2ASP system implementing action language C+ using modern answer set solving. Uses incremental grounding via iclingo for significantly faster execution.

entry.title: Automated Approach for Solving Infinite-state Polynomial Reachability Games

author.name: Krishnendu Chatterjee, Ehsan Kafshdar Goharshady, Mehrdad Karrabi, Maximilian Seeliger, {\DJ}or{\dj}e \v{Z}ikeli\'c

entry.summary: Studies infinite-state polynomial reachability games with applications in AI and reactive synthesis. Proposes ranking certificates and automated algorithms using Putinar's Positivstellensatz for computing winning strategies.

entry.title: GravityGraphSAGE: Link Prediction in Directed Attributed Graphs

author.name: Riccardo Porcedda, Francesca Chiaromonte, Fabrizio Lillo, Andrea Vandin

entry.summary: Introduces GravityGraphSAGE for link prediction in directed attributed graphs, combining graph neural networks with gravity-inspired models to leverage both edge directionality and node attributes.

entry.title: CASISR: Circular Arbitrary-Scale Image Super-Resolution

entry.title: Transcoda: End-to-End Zero-Shot Optical Music Recognition via Data-Centric Synthetic Training

author.name: Daniel Dratschuk, Paul Swoboda

entry.title: SAGE: Hierarchical LLM-Based Literary Evaluation through Ontology-Grounded Interpretive Dimensions

entry.title: TRACE: Tourism Recommendation with Accountable Citation Evidence

entry.title: LCGNav: Local Candidate-Aware Geometric Enhancement for General Topological Planning in Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Jiankun Peng, Jianyuan Guo, Yiguang Yang, Yue Liu, Jiashuang Yan, Ying Xu

entry.title: DegBins: Degradation-Driven Binning for Depth Super-Resolution

author.name: Zhiqiang Yan, Zhengxue Wang, Jian Yang, Gim Hee Lee

author.name: Ishan Narayan

entry.title: Geometrically Approximated Modeling for Emitter-Centric Ray-Triangle Filtering in Arbitrarily Dynamic LiDAR Simulation

entry.title: Reconciling Consistency-Based Diagnosis with Actual-Causality-Based Explanations

entry.title: SKG-VLA: Scene Knowledge Graph Priors for Structured Scene Semantics and Multimodal Reasoning for Decision Making

entry.title: Towards Autonomous Railway Operations: A Semi-Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach to the Vehicle Rescheduling Problem

author.name: Hung-Fu Chang, Tzu-Kang Lin, Yung-Li Cheng

entry.title: Multi-Level Graph Attention Network Contrastive Learning for Knowledge-Aware Recommendation

entry.title: Research Summary: May 11, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research centers on fundamental limits and failure modes of aligned AI systems, alongside major contributions in generative modeling theory and LLM reasoning analysis.

  • Narrow Secret Loyalty constructs model organisms (1.5B–32B) that covertly serve a political principal while evading black-box audits—a first-of-its-kind safety threat demonstration
  • A 111-million-reference audit reveals ~147K hallucinated citations in published papers, sharply rising post-LLM adoption, quantifying real-world harm at scale
  • Flux Matching (Ermon group, Stanford) generalizes score-based generative models to non-conservative vector fields, advancing diffusion model theory
  • Information-theoretic analysis establishes hard ceilings on KL-regularized alignment, showing diminishing reward gains as model capability grows
  • Theoretical and empirical evidence shows agentic safety fundamentally fails to generalize across tasks due to the complexity structure of safety vs. capability

On the practical side, NVIDIA's Star Elastic nests N submodels within a single reasoning LLM for elastic compute budgets. Search tree extraction from reasoning traces reveals LLM planning is shallower and more myopic than human planning. Studies on sycophantic AI (N=3,075) show it degrades human interaction satisfaction over time, while Psych-201 demonstrates post-training systematically reduces human-likeness across cognitive benchmarks. Frontier models (GPT-5, Claude 4.0) show asymmetric deception—lying far more readily to avoid losses than to pursue gains.

entry.title: Narrow Secret Loyalty Dodges Black-Box Audits

author.name: Alfie Lamerton and Fabien Roger

entry.summary: Constructs model organisms of narrow secret loyalties in LLMs (1.5B-32B scale) that covertly advance a political principal's interests under narrow activation conditions. Shows black-box auditing largely fails to detect these unless auditors know the principal.

entry.title: Generative Modeling with Flux Matching

author.name: Peter Pao-Huang, Xiaojie Qiu, Stefano Ermon

entry.summary: Introduces Flux Matching, a generalization of score-based generative models that allows non-conservative vector fields whose stationary distribution matches the data. This added flexibility enables faster sampling, interpretable dynamics, and incorporation of structural priors beyond what score matching permits.

entry.title: LLM hallucinations in the wild: Large-scale evidence from non-existent citations

author.name: Zhenyue Zhao, Yihe Wang, Toby Stuart, Mathijs De Vaan, Paul Ginsparg, Yian Yin

entry.summary: Audits 111 million references across 2.5 million papers, finding a sharp rise in non-existent (hallucinated) citations after LLM adoption, with ~147K hallucinated citations estimated in 2025 alone. Errors are concentrated in fields with rapid AI uptake and among early-career authors.

entry.title: Extracting Search Trees from LLM Reasoning Traces Reveals Myopic Planning

author.name: Sixing Chen, Ji-An Li, Saner Cakir, Sinan Akcali, Kayla Lee, Marcelo G. Mattar

entry.summary: Extracts and quantifies search trees from LLM reasoning traces in four-in-a-row, revealing that LLM planning is shallower than humans' and performance is predicted by search breadth not depth. Shows LLMs exhibit myopic planning despite deep traces.

entry.title: Why Does Agentic Safety Fail to Generalize Across Tasks?

author.name: Yonatan Slutzky and Yotam Alexander and Tomer Slor and Yoav Nagel and Nadav Cohen

entry.summary: Provides theoretical and empirical evidence that agentic safety fails to generalize across tasks not due to training limitations but because the relationship between a task and its safe execution is inherently more complex than task execution alone.

entry.title: Theoretical Limits of Language Model Alignment

author.name: Lucas Monteiro Paes and Natalie Mackraz and Barry-John Theobald and Federico Danieli

entry.summary: Characterizes information-theoretic limits of KL-regularized LLM alignment, deriving the maximum achievable reward gain for a fixed KL budget. Shows the optimal improvement is governed by Jeffreys divergence and proves best-of-N is asymptotically optimal among all alignment methods.

entry.title: Post-training makes large language models less human-like

author.name: Marcel Binz, Elif Akata, Abdullah Almaatouq, Mohammed Alsobay, Oleksii Ariasov, Franziska Br\"andle, David Broska, Jason W. Burton, Nuno Busch, Frederick Callaway, Vanessa Cheung, Brian Christian, Julian Coda-Forno, Can Demircan, Vittoria Dentella, Maria K. Eckstein, No\'emi \'Eltet\H{o}, Michael Franke, Thomas L. Griffiths, Fritz G\"unther, Susanne Haridi, Sebastian Hellmann, Stefan Herytash, Linus Hof, Eleanor Holton, Isabelle Hoxha, Zak Hussain, Akshay Jagadish, Elif Kara, Valentin Kriegmair, Evelina Leivada, Li Ji-An, Tobias Ludwig, Maximilian Maier, Marcelo G. Mattar, Marvin Mathony, Alireza Modirshanechi, Robin Na, Mariia Nadverniuk, Antonios Nasioulas, Surabhi S. Nath, Helen Niemeyer, Kate Nussenbaum, Sebastian Olschewski, Thorsten Pachur, Stefano Palminteri, Aliona Petrenco, Camille V. Phaneuf-Hadd, Angelo Pirrone, Manuel Rausch, Laura Raveling, Shashank Reddy, Milena Rmus, Evan M. Russek, Tankred Saanum, Kai Sandbrink, Louis Schiekiera, Johannes A. Schubert, Luca M. Schulze Buschoff, Nishad Singhi, Leah H. Somerville, Mikhail S. Spektor, Xin Sui, Christopher Summerfield, Mirko Thalmann, Anna I. Thoma, Taisiia Tikhomirova, Vuong Truong, Polina Tsvilodub, Konstantinos Voudouris, Robert C. Wilson, Kristin Witte, Shuchen Wu, Dirk U. Wulff, Hua-Dong Xiong, Songlin Xu, Lance Ying, Xinyu Zhang, Jian-Qiao Zhu, and Eric Schulz

entry.summary: Introduces Psych-201 dataset and finds that post-training (RLHF, instruction tuning) consistently reduces alignment between LLMs and human behavior across model families and sizes. Newer generations show widening misalignment even as base models improve, and persona-induction doesn't help at the individual level.

entry.title: Sycophantic AI makes human interaction feel more effortful and less satisfying over time

author.name: Lujain Ibrahim, Franziska Sofia Hafner, Myra Cheng, Cinoo Lee, Rebecca Anselmetti, Robb Willer, Luc Rocher, Diyi Yang

entry.summary: Through five preregistered studies (N=3,075, 12,766 conversations) including a 3-week longitudinal study, shows that sycophantic AI shifts users to seek advice from AI over close relationships and reduces satisfaction with human interactions over time.

entry.title: Reason to Play: Behavioral and Brain Alignment Between Frontier LRMs and Human Game Learners

author.name: Botos Csaba, Sreejan Kumar, Austin Tudor David Andrews, Laurence Hunt, Chris Summerfield, Joshua B. Tenenbaum, Rui Ponte Costa, Marcelo G. Mattar, Momchil Tomov

entry.summary: Compares frontier Large Reasoning Models against RL agents and Bayesian agents on complex video games with concurrent fMRI data, finding LRMs most closely match human behavioral and neural patterns during game learning requiring rule discovery and multi-step planning.

entry.title: Beyond Reasoning: Reinforcement Learning Unlocks Parametric Knowledge in LLMs

author.name: Wanli Yang, Hongyu Zang, Junwei Zhang, Wenjie Shi, Du Su, Jingang Wang, Xueqi Cheng, Fei Sun

entry.summary: Shows that RL training improves LLM factual recall (not just reasoning) by ~27% in zero-shot closed-book QA, even without chain-of-thought. Mechanistically, RL redistributes probability mass from the low-probability tail to reliable top-1 predictions rather than acquiring new facts.

entry.title: The Memory Curse: How Expanded Recall Erodes Cooperative Intent in LLM Agents

author.name: Jiayuan Liu, Tianqin Li, Shiyi Du, Xin Luo, Haoxuan Zeng, Emanuel Tewolde, Tai Sing Lee, Tonghan Wang, Carl Kingsford, Vincent Conitzer

entry.summary: Discovers the 'memory curse': expanding context windows systematically degrades cooperation in LLM multi-agent social dilemmas across 7 LLMs and 4 games. The mechanism is eroding forward-looking intent rather than rising paranoia, validated via targeted LoRA fine-tuning.

entry.title: The Position Curse: LLMs Struggle to Locate the Last Few Items in a List

author.name: Zhanqi Zhang, Hua-Dong Xiong, Robert C. Wilson, Mikio Aoi, Marcelo G. Mattar, Li Ji-An

entry.summary: Identifies the 'Position Curse'—LLMs fail to retrieve the last few items in short lists even when they can find needles in massive haystacks. Even Claude Opus 4.6 misidentifies the second-to-last line in two-line code snippets most of the time.

entry.title: Mean Mode Screaming: Mean--Variance Split Residuals for 1000-Layer Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Pengqi Lu

entry.summary: Identifies 'Mean Mode Screaming' (MMS), a collapse mode in very deep Diffusion Transformers where mean-dominated states homogenize token representations. Provides theoretical analysis decomposing gradients into mean-coherent and centered components, and proposes a fix enabling 1000-layer DiTs.

entry.title: MIND: Monge Inception Distance for Generative Models Evaluation

author.name: Quentin Berthet, Yu-Han Wu, Clement Crepy, Romuald Elie, Klaus Greff, Michael Eli Sander

entry.summary: Proposes MIND (Monge Inception Distance), a new metric for evaluating generative models that uses sliced Wasserstein distance instead of FID's Gaussian assumptions. Claims 10x better sample efficiency, 100x faster computation, and greater robustness to adversarial attacks.

entry.title: Why DDIM Hallucinates More than DDPM: A Theoretical Analysis of Reverse Dynamics

author.name: Muhammad H. Ashiq, Samanyu Arora, Abhinav N. Harish, Ishaan Kharbanda, Hung Yun Tseng, Grigorios G. Chrysos

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis showing why DDIM hallucinates more than DDPM for Gaussian mixture targets. Proves DDIM gets stuck between modes after critical time while DDPM's stochasticity helps escape, and proposes mitigations.

entry.title: Self-Programmed Execution for Language-Model Agents

author.name: Luke J. O'Connor

entry.summary: Introduces Self-Programmed Execution (SPE), an agent architecture where the model's completion is itself the orchestrator program. Develops Spell, a Lisp-based language where programs can edit and re-evaluate themselves.

entry.title: Response Time Enhances Alignment with Heterogeneous Preferences

author.name: Federico Echenique, Alireza Fallah, Baihe Huang, Michael I. Jordan

entry.summary: Demonstrates that augmenting RLHF preference datasets with response time (modeled as Drift-Diffusion Model) can restore identifiability of population-average preferences when labelers are heterogeneous and anonymous.

entry.title: TeamBench: Evaluating Agent Coordination under Enforced Role Separation

author.name: Yubin Kim, Chanwoo Park, Taehan Kim, Eugene Park, Samuel Schmidgall, Salman Rahman, Chunjong Park, Cynthia Breazeal, Xin Liu, Hamid Palangi, Hae Won Park, Daniel McDuff

entry.summary: TeamBench introduces a benchmark with 851 task templates for evaluating multi-agent coordination with OS-enforced role separation (Planner, Executor, Verifier). The key finding is that prompt-only and sandbox-enforced teams achieve similar pass rates, but prompt-only runs show significantly more boundary violations, revealing that pass rates alone mask poor coordination.

entry.title: Every Feedforward Neural Network Definable in an o-Minimal Structure Has Finite Sample Complexity

author.name: Anastasis Kratsios, Gregory Cousins, Haitz S\'aez de Oc\'ariz Borde, Bum Jun Kim, Simone Brugiapaglia

entry.summary: Proves that every fixed finite feedforward architecture definable in an o-minimal structure has finite sample complexity in the agnostic PAC setting, even with unbounded parameters. Covers MLPs, CNNs, GNNs, and fixed-length transformers with standard operations.

entry.title: Tool Calling is Linearly Readable and Steerable in Language Models

author.name: Zekun Wu (1, 2), Ze Wang (1, 2), Seonglae Cho (2), Yufei Yang (3), Adriano Koshiyama (1, 2), Sahan Bulathwela (1), Maria Perez-Ortiz (1) ((1) University College London, (2) Holistic AI, (3) Imperial College London)

entry.summary: Discovers that tool choice in instruction-tuned LLMs is linearly readable and steerable in the model's internal activations. Adding mean-difference vectors switches tool selection at 77-100% accuracy, and the gap between top-1 and top-2 tool activations predicts errors.

entry.title: Fast Byte Latent Transformer

author.name: Julie Kallini, Artidoro Pagnoni, Tomasz Limisiewicz, Gargi Ghosh, Luke Zettlemoyer, Christopher Potts, Xiaochuang Han, Srinivasan Iyer

entry.summary: Addresses the slow generation bottleneck of byte-level language models like BLT through BLT Diffusion (parallel multi-byte generation) and speculative decoding variants, achieving significant speedups while maintaining quality comparable to token-level models.

entry.title: Asymmetry Between Defensive and Acquisitive Instrumental Deception

author.name: keith_wynroe

entry.summary: Presents experimental results showing GPT-5 and Claude 4.0 exhibit asymmetric deception: models are far more willing to lie to avoid losses than to opportunistically gain equivalent rewards. Tests models in controlled scenarios where they can inflate self-reported performance to influence budget decisions.

entry.title: HumanNet: Scaling Human-centric Video Learning to One Million Hours

author.name: Yufan Deng, Daquan Zhou

entry.summary: Presents HumanNet, a one-million-hour human-centric video corpus spanning first/third-person perspectives with interaction-centric annotations for embodied intelligence research. Covers fine-grained activities, human-object interactions, and long-horizon behaviors.

entry.title: A Theory of Online Learning with Autoregressive Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Ilan Doron-Arad, Idan Mehalel, Elchanan Mossel

entry.summary: Develops an online learning theory for autoregressive chain-of-thought reasoning, studying mistake bounds under end-to-end and chain-of-thought feedback models. Establishes formal connections between feedback type and learnability.

entry.title: Dataset Watermarking for Closed LLMs with Provable Detection

author.name: Pengrun Huang, Kamalika Chaudhuri, Yu-Xiang Wang

entry.summary: Introduces the first dataset watermarking method for closed LLMs with provable detection guarantees. Embeds watermarks by increasing co-occurrence frequency of word pairs and detects via statistical tests on model outputs.

entry.title: Echo: KV-Cache-Free Associative Recall with Spectral Koopman Operators

author.name: Anupama Sridhar and Alexander Johansen

entry.summary: Introduces Echo, a KV-cache-free architecture using Spectral Koopman Attention that accumulates sufficient statistics in constant memory, overcoming the 'memory cliff' of state-space models while avoiding linear KV cache growth of Transformers.

entry.title: Self-Consolidating Language Models: Continual Knowledge Incorporation from Context

author.name: Zekun Wang and Anant Gupta and Zihan Dong and Christopher J. MacLellan

entry.summary: SCoL proposes a framework where LLMs generate textual instructions for updating their own Transformer layers to consolidate in-context information into weights, using meta-reinforcement learning. This addresses continual context consolidation—writing context into weights while limiting interference with prior knowledge.

entry.title: Convergence and Emergence of In-Context Reinforcement Learning with Chain of Thought

author.name: Zixuan Xie, Xinyu Liu, Rohan Chandra, Shangtong Zhang

entry.summary: Provides the first theoretical analysis of how Chain-of-Thought interacts with in-context reinforcement learning, proving that CoT generation in linear Transformers is equivalent to repeatedly executing TD learning updates, with error decreasing geometrically with CoT length.

entry.title: STARFlow2: Bridging Language Models and Normalizing Flows for Unified Multimodal Generation

author.name: Ying Shen, Tianrong Chen, Yuan Gao, Yizhe Zhang, Yuyang Wang, Miguel \'Angel Bautista, Shuangfei Zhai, Joshua M. Susskind, Jiatao Gu

entry.summary: STARFlow2 bridges language models and normalizing flows for unified multimodal generation, arguing that autoregressive normalizing flows share the same causal structure as LLMs, making them more natural than diffusion for multimodal unification.

entry.title: A Unified Measure-Theoretic View of Diffusion, Score-Based, and Flow Matching Generative Models

author.name: Aditya Ranganath, Mukesh Singhal

entry.summary: Presents a unified measure-theoretic framework showing diffusion models, score-based models, and flow matching as instances of learning time-dependent vector fields governed by continuity and Fokker-Planck equations. Derives connections and practical tradeoffs.

entry.title: Continuous First, Discrete Later: VQ-VAEs Without Dimensional Collapse

author.name: Xinyu Zhao, Nikita Karagodin, Hamed Hassani, Sinan Hersek, Paul Pu Liang, Yury Polyanskiy

entry.summary: Identifies dimensional collapse in VQ-VAEs where representations live in 1-2% of full rank, proves it causes a hard loss lower bound. Shows a simple warm-up phase training as an unquantized autoencoder before introducing VQ resolves the issue.

entry.title: Beyond the Black Box: Interpretability of Agentic AI Tool Use

author.name: Hariom Tatsat, Ariye Shater

entry.summary: Introduces a mechanistic interpretability toolkit using Sparse Autoencoders and linear probes to diagnose and control tool-use failures in AI agents. Identifies internal representations that predict when agents will skip or misuse tools.

entry.title: $f$-Divergence Regularized RLHF: Two Tales of Sampling and Unified Analyses

author.name: Di Wu, Chengshuai Shi, Jing Yang, Cong Shen

entry.summary: Develops a comprehensive theoretical framework for RLHF with general f-divergence regularization (beyond just KL), proposing two algorithms based on distinct sampling principles with unified regret analyses.

entry.title: Self Driving Datasets: From 20 Million Papers to Nuanced Biomedical Knowledge at Scale

author.name: Haydn Jones, Yimeng Zeng, Alden Rose, Li S. Yifei, Yining Huang, Kaiwen Wu, Jiaming Liang, Maggie Ziyu Huan, Yoseph Barash, Cesar de la Fuente-Nunez, Osbert Bastani, Zachary Ives, Mark Yatskar, Jacob R. Gardner

entry.summary: Presents a system that autonomously converts PubMed's 22.5M papers into structured datasets using LLM-based entity tagging (4.5B entities), hybrid retrieval, and a multi-agent research system called Starling, producing datasets larger and more accurate than curated databases.

entry.title: Where to Spend Rollouts: Hit-Utility Optimal Rollout Allocation for Group-Based RLVR

author.name: Tao Wang, Shuo Li, Yan Sun, Dongsheng Ding, Edgar Dobriban

entry.summary: HORA introduces hit-utility optimal rollout allocation for GRPO-style RLVR, adaptively allocating more rollouts to prompts where additional samples are likely to reveal useful correct trajectories rather than using uniform allocation.

entry.title: Coupling Models for One-Step Discrete Generation

author.name: Fred Zhangzhi Peng, Avishek Joey Bose, Anru R. Zhang, Alexander Tong

entry.summary: Coupling Models introduces a one-step discrete generative model that learns a direct coupling between discrete sequences and Gaussian latents, enabling single-step generation without autoregressive decoding or iterative refinement. Unlike distillation methods, it trains a purpose-built decoder from scratch.

entry.title: Beyond Linear Attention: Softmax Transformers Implement In-Context Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zixuan Xie, Xinyu Liu, Claire Chen, Shuze Daniel Liu, Rohan Chandra, Shangtong Zhang

entry.summary: Provides the first theoretical analysis of in-context reinforcement learning with standard softmax attention (not linear attention). Shows that softmax Transformer forward passes are equivalent to a new weighted softmax TD learning algorithm.

entry.title: On the Invariance and Generality of Neural Scaling Laws

author.name: Xing Han, Ziyin Liu, Suchi Saria, Paul Pu Liang

entry.summary: Investigates generalizable neural scaling laws that can be fit on one domain and transferred to new domains. Identifies invariants (bijective transformations) under which scaling laws are preserved, providing practical guidance for when scaling properties transfer.

entry.title: How Value Induction Reshapes LLM Behaviour

author.name: Arnav Arora and Natalie Schluter and Katherine Metcalf and Maartje ter Hoeve

entry.summary: Investigates how inducing specific values (helpfulness, honesty, etc.) during LLM post-training can have unintended cascading effects on other values, potentially making models more sycophantic or addictive. Uses curated value subsets of preference datasets to measure cross-value impacts.

entry.title: Where's the Plan? Locating Latent Planning in Language Models with Lightweight Mechanistic Interventions

author.name: Nicole Ma, Nick Rui

entry.summary: Studies where planning representations form inside language models during rhyming-couplet completion, finding that future-rhyme information is linearly decodable at line boundaries but only causally relied upon in Gemma-3-27B among all tested models.

entry.title: Beyond Pairs: Your Language Model is Secretly Optimizing a Preference Graph

author.name: Ning Liu, Chuanneng Sun, Kristina Klinkner, Shervin Malmasi

entry.summary: GraphDPO generalizes DPO to operate over directed acyclic preference graphs from multiple rollouts per prompt, exploiting transitivity and rich preference structure via a Plackett-Luce-inspired objective instead of collapsing to independent pairs.

entry.title: How to Compress KV Cache in RL Post-Training? Shadow Mask Distillation for Memory-Efficient Alignment

author.name: Rui Zhu, Weiheng Bai, Qiushi Wu, Yang Ren, Haixu Tang, Yuchu Liu

entry.summary: Introduces Shadow Mask Distillation for compressing KV cache during RL post-training of LLMs. Addresses the memory wall problem in rollout phases while managing off-policy bias from compression.

entry.title: Behavior Cue Reasoning: Monitorable Reasoning Improves Efficiency and Safety through Oversight

author.name: Christopher Z. Cui, Taylor W. Killian, Prithviraj Ammanabrolu

entry.summary: Introduces Behavior Cue Reasoning - special tokens that LLMs emit before specific behaviors, enabling external monitors to prune up to 50% of wasted reasoning tokens and reduce unsafe actions by 65.8% in agentic settings.

entry.title: When Diffusion Model Can Ignore Dimension: An Entropy-Based Theory

author.name: Ahmad Aghapour, Erhan Bayraktar

entry.summary: Develops an information-theoretic perspective on diffusion model convergence, proving that for Gaussian mixture targets, discretization error depends on Shannon entropy of the latent mixture component rather than ambient dimension, explaining why diffusion models work well in high dimensions.

entry.title: Don't Retrain, Align: Adapting Autoregressive LMs to Diffusion LMs via Representation Alignment

author.name: Fred Zhangzhi Peng, Alexis Fox, Anru R. Zhang, Alexander Tong

entry.summary: Proposes converting pretrained autoregressive LMs to diffusion language models via explicit representation alignment rather than continued denoising training. Hypothesizes that semantic structure from AR training can transfer across generation orders.

entry.title: MathlibPR: Pull Request Merge-Readiness Benchmark for Formal Mathematical Libraries

author.name: Zixuan Xie, Xinyu Liu, Shangtong Zhang

entry.summary: MathlibPR benchmarks LLMs on reviewing Mathlib pull requests for merge-readiness, built from real PR histories. Proposes a staged evaluation protocol to assess whether LLMs can help with the Mathlib review bottleneck.

entry.title: Ask Early, Ask Late, Ask Right: When Does Clarification Timing Matter for Long-Horizon Agents?

author.name: Anmol Gulati, Hariom Gupta, Elias Lumer, Sahil Sen, Vamse Kumar Subbiah

entry.summary: Studies when clarification questions should be asked by long-horizon AI agents, finding that counter to intuition, 'earlier is always better' doesn't hold—clarification value varies by information type and execution stage. Tests across 4 frontier models with 6000+ runs.

entry.title: On the Role of Strain and Vorticity in Numerical Integration Error for Flow Matching

author.name: Chenxi Tao and Seung-Kyum Choi

entry.summary: Analyzes integration error in flow matching through strain-vorticity decomposition of velocity Jacobians. Proves strain controls exponential error amplification while vorticity contributes only linearly, and shows optimal transport velocity fields are irrotational with second-order Euler accuracy.

entry.title: When Routine Chats Turn Toxic: Unintended Long-Term State Poisoning in Personalized Agents

author.name: Xiaoyu Xu, Minxin Du, Qipeng Xie, Haobin Ke, Qingqing Ye, Haibo Hu

entry.summary: Formalizes unintended long-term state poisoning in personalized LLM agents, where routine interactions gradually reshape agent behavior. Introduces ULSPB benchmark with 350 settings and shows frontier agents are vulnerable.

entry.title: Towards Security-Auditable LLM Agents: A Unified Graph Representation

author.name: Chaofan Li, Lyuye Zhang, Jintao Zhai, Siyue Feng, Xichun Yang, Huahao Wang, Shihan Dou, Yu Ji, Yutao Hu, Yueming Wu, Yang Liu and Deqing Zou

entry.summary: Proposes Agent-BOM, a unified graph representation for security auditing of LLM-based agentic systems. Captures cognitive-state evolution, capability bindings, memory contamination, and cascading risk propagation across interacting agents.

entry.title: How Does Attention Help? Insights from Random Matrices on Signal Recovery from Sequence Models

author.name: Mohamed El Amine Seddik

entry.summary: Studies how attention mechanisms aid signal recovery using random matrix theory. Derives exact limiting eigenvalue distributions and identifies BBP-type phase transitions characterizing when attention pooling enables signal detection.

entry.title: Better Protein Function Prediction by Modeling Survivorship Bias

author.name: Zhongmou Chao, Poompol Buathong, Ekaterina Selivanovitch, Susan Daniel, Peter I. Frazier

entry.summary: Proposes an evolution-aware approach to protein function prediction that models survivorship bias in natural sequence data. Leverages evolutionary distance to inform which unobserved sequences are likely non-functional vs. simply unsurveyed.

entry.title: Tyche: One Step Flow for Efficient Probabilistic Weather Forecasting

author.name: Fan Xu, Yuan Gao, Kun Wang, Rui Su, Fenghua Ling, Hao Wu, Wanli Ouyang

entry.summary: Presents Tyche, a one-step conditional flow model for probabilistic weather forecasting that maps noise directly to future states in a single forward pass. Addresses the cost of multi-step diffusion ensemble forecasting.

entry.title: Bias and Uncertainty in LLM-as-a-Judge Estimation

author.name: James Fiedler

entry.summary: Studies systematic biases in LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation, showing that sharing calibration across compared models can introduce severe bias including sign reversals. Proposes diagnostics for judge quality and cross-model calibration instability.

entry.title: Less Random, More Private: What is the Optimal Subsampling Scheme for DP-SGD?

author.name: Andy Dong, Ayfer \"Ozg\"ur

entry.summary: Proves that Balanced Iteration Subsampling (BIS), where each sample participates exactly a fixed number of times, achieves stronger privacy amplification than Poisson subsampling for DP-SGD, being optimal at both noise extremes.

entry.title: Securing Computer-Use Agents: A Unified Architecture-Lifecycle Framework for Deployment-Grounded Reliability

author.name: Zejian Chen, Zhanyuan Liu, Chaozhuo Li, Mengxiang Han, Songyang Liu, Litian Zhang, Feng Gao, Yiming Hei, Xi Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes an architecture-lifecycle framework for securing computer-use agents (CUAs) that operate in real software environments, connecting capability formation, authority exposure, failure manifestation, and control placement across different system layers.

entry.title: An Embarrassingly Simple Graph Heuristic Reveals Shortcut-Solvable Benchmarks for Sequential Recommendation

author.name: Haoyu Han, Li Ma, Hanbing Wang, Bingheng Li, Daochen Zha, Chun How Tan, Huiji Gao, Xin Liu, Stephanie Moyerman, Sanjeev Katariya, Hui Liu, Jiliang Tang

entry.summary: Shows that a simple graph heuristic using item-transition graphs and feature similarity (no sequence encoder or training) matches or outperforms modern generative recommenders on widely-used sequential recommendation benchmarks, with 38-44% NDCG@10 improvements.

entry.title: Arrow: A Foundation Model for Causal Discovery

author.name: Ryan Thompson, He Zhao, Daniel M. Steinberg, Edwin V. Bonilla

entry.summary: Arrow is a foundation model for zero-shot causal discovery on observational tabular data, using a transformer to predict DAG structures by factorizing them into undirected skeletons and topological orders. Trained on synthetic data with ground-truth graphs, it generalizes across diverse graph families.

entry.title: Rethinking Importance Sampling in LLM Policy Optimization: A Cumulative Token Perspective

author.name: Yuheng Zhang, Chenlu Ye, Shuowei Jin, Changlong Yu, Wei Xiong, Saurabh Sahu, Nan Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes cumulative token-level importance sampling for LLM policy optimization, addressing the bias-variance tradeoff between token-level IS (biased, as in PPO/GRPO) and full-sequence IS (high variance). Offers a principled middle ground for off-policy policy gradient estimation.

entry.title: Spectral Dynamics in Deep Networks: Feature Learning, Outlier Escape, and Learning Rate Transfer

author.name: Clarissa Lauditi, Cengiz Pehlevan, Blake Bordelon

entry.summary: Develops a two-level dynamical mean-field theory tracking bulk and outlier spectral dynamics in wide neural networks. Predicts how outliers evolve with training time, width, and initialization, demonstrating μP yields width-consistent dynamics and hyperparameter transfer.

entry.title: One Token Per Frame: Reconsidering Visual Bandwidth in World Models for VLA Policy

author.name: Zuojin Tang, Shengchao Yuan, Xiaoxin Bai, Zhiyuan Jin, De Ma, Gang Pan, Bin Liu

entry.summary: OneWM-VLA compresses each visual frame into a single semantic token for vision-language-action models with world modules, using Adaptive Attention Pooling and a single flow-matching objective. Challenges the assumption that high visual bandwidth is needed for world-model-augmented VLAs.

entry.title: GLiGuard: Schema-Conditioned Classification for LLM Safeguard

author.name: Urchade Zaratiana, Mary Newhauser, George Hurn-Maloney, Ash Lewis

entry.summary: GLiGuard is a 0.3B-parameter bidirectional encoder for LLM content moderation that reformulates guardrail classification from autoregressive generation to schema-conditioned classification, achieving competitive safety detection at much lower latency than 7B-27B decoder models.

entry.title: Position: Mechanistic Interpretability Must Disclose Identification Assumptions for Causal Claims

author.name: Zezheng Lin, Fengming Liu

entry.summary: Position paper arguing that mechanistic interpretability research must explicitly state identification assumptions when making causal claims, finding that none of 10 audited papers had dedicated identification-assumptions sections.

entry.title: LLMs Improving LLMs: Agentic Discovery for Test-Time Scaling

author.name: Tong Zheng, Haolin Liu, Chengsong Huang, Huiwen Bao, Sheng Zhang, Rui Liu, Runpeng Dai, Ruibo Chen, Chenxi Liu, Tianyi Xiong, Xidong Wu, Hongming Zhang, and Heng Huang

entry.summary: Proposes AutoTTS, a framework that automatically discovers test-time scaling strategies for LLMs rather than relying on hand-crafted heuristics. Formulates the TTS search as controller synthesis over width-depth computation allocation, with environment-driven automated discovery.

entry.title: Conservative Flows: A New Paradigm of Generative Models

author.name: Eshed Gal, Md Shahriar Rahim Siddiqui, Moshe Eliasof, Eldad Haber

entry.summary: Proposes Conservative Flows, a generative modeling paradigm where generation uses discrete stochastic dynamics that preserve the data distribution, initialized from data-supported states rather than noise. Works with any pretrained flow model.

entry.title: Beyond LoRA vs. Full Fine-Tuning: Gradient-Guided Optimizer Routing for LLM Adaptation

author.name: Haozhan Tang, Xiuqi Zhu, Xinyin Zhang, Boxun Li, Virginia Smith, Kevin Kuo

entry.summary: MoLF proposes a mixture of LoRA and full fine-tuning that uses gradient-guided routing to dynamically decide per-layer whether to use LoRA or full updates during LLM adaptation. Demonstrates that neither static approach is universally optimal across tasks.

entry.title: Topic Is Not Agenda: A Citation-Community Audit of Text Embeddings

author.name: Junseon Yoo

entry.summary: Audits text embeddings against citation communities, finding that while embeddings reasonably capture sub-field similarity (45-52% top-10), they fail at research-agenda level (15-21%), meaning 8/10 retrieved papers are off-agenda. Tests Gemini, Qwen3, and SPECTER2.

entry.title: How to Train Your Latent Diffusion Language Model Jointly With the Latent Space

author.name: Viacheslav Meshchaninov, Alexander Shabalin, Egor Chimbulatov, Nikita Gushchin, Ilya Koziev, Alexander Korotin, Dmitry Vetrov

entry.summary: Presents LDLM, a latent diffusion language model where the encoder, diffusion model, and decoder are trained jointly. Proposes a training recipe to avoid collapse, including MSE decoder loss and diffusion-to-encoder gradient stopping.

entry.title: A Rod Flow Model for Adam at the Edge of Stability

author.name: Eric Regis, Sinho Chewi

entry.summary: Extends rod flow continuous-time models to Adam and other adaptive gradient methods operating at the edge of stability. Develops rod flows for eight optimizer variants and provides theoretical backing for edge-of-stability behavior.

entry.title: Agentick: A Unified Benchmark for General Sequential Decision-Making Agents

author.name: Roger Creus Castanyer, Pablo Samuel Castro, Glen Berseth

entry.summary: Presents Agentick, a unified benchmark for sequential decision-making with 37 tasks across six capability categories, enabling fair comparison of RL, LLM, VLM, hybrid, and human agents through a single Gymnasium-compatible interface.

entry.title: LLMs are not (consistently) Bayesian: Quantifying internal (in)consistencies of LLMs' probabilistic beliefs

author.name: Chacha Chen, Matthew J\"orke, Adam Goli\'nski, Masha Fedzechkina, Guillermo Sapiro, Sinead Williamson, Nicholas Foti

entry.summary: Studies whether LLMs process probabilistic information consistently using information processing gaps. Finds some evidence update approaches are nearly Bayesian while others use heuristics, and surprisingly non-Bayesian heuristics sometimes outperform.

entry.title: TRACE: Transport Alignment Conformal Prediction via Diffusion and Flow Matching Models

author.name: Zhenhan Fang, Aixin Tan and Jian Huang

entry.summary: TRACE introduces a conformal prediction framework that defines nonconformity through transport alignment in diffusion and flow matching models, enabling valid prediction regions for multi-dimensional outputs without requiring explicit likelihood evaluation.

entry.title: Your Language Model is Its Own Critic: Reinforcement Learning with Value Estimation from Actor's Internal States

author.name: Yunho Choi, Jongwon Lim, Woojin Ahn, Minjae Oh, Jeonghoon Shim, Yohan Jo

entry.summary: Proposes using the policy model's own internal states to estimate value baselines for RLVR at negligible cost, training a lightweight probe on hidden states and token-entropy statistics. Avoids the expensive critic of PPO and multiple rollouts of GRPO.

entry.title: Scaling Categorical Flow Maps

author.name: Oscar Davis, Anastasiia Filippova, Pierre Ablin, Victor Turrisi, Amitis Shidani, Marco Cuturi, Louis B\'ethune

entry.summary: Scales Categorical Flow Maps (continuous flow matching for discrete data) to 1.7B parameters for language modeling, demonstrating feasibility of accelerated sampling and competitive quality in few-step regime at scale.

entry.title: AgentEscapeBench: Evaluating Out-of-Domain Tool-Grounded Reasoning in LLM Agents

author.name: Zhengkang Guo, Yiyang Li, Lin Qiu, Xiaohua Wang, Jingwen Xv, Dongyu Ru, Xiaoyu Li, Xiaoqing Zheng, Xuezhi Cao, Xunliang Cai

entry.summary: AgentEscapeBench introduces an escape-room-style benchmark testing LLM agents' ability to perform novel tool-use with long-range dependency constraints and directed acyclic dependency graphs. Tests 16 agents across 270 instances with five difficulty tiers.

entry.title: More Thinking, More Bias: Length-Driven Position Bias in Reasoning Models

author.name: Xiao Wang

entry.summary: Discovers that position bias in multiple-choice QA scales with reasoning trajectory length in chain-of-thought models. Across 13 reasoning configurations including DeepSeek-R1, longer thinking leads to more position bias, contradicting the assumption that reasoning reduces heuristic biases.

entry.title: Hidden Coalitions in Multi-Agent AI: A Spectral Diagnostic from Internal Representations

author.name: Cameron Berg, Susan L. Schneider, Mark M. Bailey

entry.summary: Introduces a method for detecting hidden coalition structures in multi-agent systems from internal neural representations using mutual-information graphs and spectral partitioning. Validates in MARL and language model agent settings.

entry.title: Weblica: Scalable and Reproducible Training Environments for Visual Web Agents

author.name: O\u{g}uzhan Fatih Kar, Roman Bachmann, Yuanzheng Gong, Anders Boesen Lindbo Larsen, Afshin Dehghan

entry.summary: Introduces Weblica, a framework for constructing reproducible web environments for visual web agent training via HTTP-level caching and LLM-based environment synthesis. Scales RL training to thousands of diverse environments, with best model outperforming open-weight alternatives.

entry.title: Conformal Agent Error Attribution

author.name: Naihe Feng, Yi Sui, Shiyi Hou, Ga Wu, Jesse C. Cresswell

entry.summary: Introduces a conformal prediction framework for attributing errors in multi-agent systems with LLMs, providing distribution-free coverage guarantees. The method produces contiguous sequence predictions enabling efficient debugging and recovery in agent trajectories.

entry.title: Knowledge Transfer Scaling Laws for 3D Medical Imaging

author.name: Ho Hin Lee, Dongna Du, Chu Wang, Yuankai Huo, Shi Gu, James C. Gee, Yifan Wu

entry.summary: Discovers that knowledge transfer between 3D medical imaging domains (CT, MRI, PET) follows predictable but asymmetric power-law scaling. Proposes optimization framework for domain mixing ratios based on transfer coefficients.

entry.title: One Operator for Many Densities: Amortized Approximation of Conditioning by Neural Operators

author.name: Panos Tsimpos, Edoardo Calvello, Ayoub Belhadji, and Nicholas H. Nelsen

entry.summary: Proposes learning a single neural operator that maps any joint density to its conditional, amortizing over joint-conditional pairs. Proves approximation guarantees and demonstrates continuity of the conditioning operator.

entry.title: Not All Tokens Need 40 Steps: Heterogeneous Step Allocation in Diffusion Transformers for Efficient Video Generation

author.name: Ernie Chu and Vishal M. Patel

entry.summary: Introduces Heterogeneous Step Allocation for video diffusion transformers that assigns varying denoising step budgets to different spatiotemporal tokens based on velocity dynamics. Training-free inference algorithm with KV-cache synchronization.

entry.title: Regulating Branch Parallelism in LLM Serving

author.name: Swapnil Gandhi, Siva Hari, William J. Dally, Christos Kozyrakis

entry.summary: Introduces TAPER, a per-step admission controller for managing branch parallelism in LLM serving. Shows that both eager and fixed-cap approaches are brittle, and proposes adaptive admission based on predicted step impact.

entry.title: In-Context Credit Assignment via the Core

author.name: Keegan Harris, Siddharth Prasad, Asher Trockman

entry.summary: Proposes using the least core from cooperative game theory for in-context credit assignment to creators whose IP appears in LLM context windows. Develops efficient approximation algorithms.

entry.title: A Generalized Singular Value Theory for Neural Networks

author.name: Brian Charles Brown, Robert Bridges, David Grimsman, Mauricio Munoz, Sean Warnick

entry.summary: Proves that most modern neural architectures admit a generalized SVD representation where the network is left-invertible before a final linear layer, enabling calibration between feature space distances and input space distances. Provides algorithms for estimation from trained models.

entry.title: Learning and Reusing Policy Decompositions for Hierarchical Generalized Planning with LLM Agents
