author.name: Shirin Sohrabi, Haritha Ananthakrishnan, Harsha Kokel, Kavitha Srinivas, Michael Katz

entry.summary: Presents HCL-GP, a hierarchical component learning approach for LLM agents that learns parameterized policies generalizing across task instances and extracts reusable components. Achieves 98.2% accuracy on AppWorld benchmark, 15.8 points above static approaches.

entry.title: ModelLens: Finding the Best for Your Task from Myriads of Models

author.name: Rui Cai, Weijie Jacky Mo, Xiaofei Wen, Qiyao Ma, Wenhui Zhu, Xiwen Chen, Muhao Chen, and Zhe Zhao

entry.summary: ModelLens addresses the challenge of recommending the best model from hundreds of thousands of open-source models for a new dataset, leveraging scattered public leaderboard data as an implicit atlas of model capabilities. It provides a unified framework that goes beyond existing AutoML and transferability estimation approaches.

entry.title: Switchcraft: AI Model Router for Agentic Tool Calling

author.name: Sharad Agarwal, Pooria Namyar, Alec Wolman, Rahul Ambavat, Ankur Gupta, Qizheng Zhang

entry.summary: Switchcraft is the first model router optimized for agentic tool calling rather than chat completion, using a DistilBERT classifier to select the cheapest model that maintains correctness. Achieves 82.9% accuracy while reducing inference cost by 84%.

entry.title: Uncovering and Shaping the Latent Representation of 3D Scene Topology in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Haoming Wang, Wei Gao

entry.summary: Demonstrates that VLMs possess a latent topological map of 3D scenes but it's overshadowed by visual semantics like color/shape. Extracts a clean spatial subspace through cross-scene linear feature extraction that causally controls spatial outputs.

entry.title: Experience Sharing in Mutual Reinforcement Learning for Heterogeneous Language Models

author.name: Xiaoze Liu, Dhananjay Ram, Yuting Zhang, Zhaoyang Zhang, Wei Xia, Stefano Soatto

entry.summary: Introduces Mutual Reinforcement Learning where heterogeneous LLM policies (different model families, tokenizers) exchange typed experience during concurrent RL post-training, using a Tokenizer Heterogeneity Layer to align traces across incompatible vocabularies.

entry.title: Rethinking Dense Sequential Chains: Reasoning Language Models Can Extract Answers from Sparse, Order-Shuffling Chain-of-Thoughts

author.name: Yi-Chang Chen, Feng-Ting Liao, Da-shan Shiu, Hung-yi Lee

entry.summary: Challenges assumptions about chain-of-thought by showing that line-level shuffling reduces accuracy by <0.5pp, word-level shuffling retains 62-89% accuracy, and only ~50% of reasoning content is needed for answer extraction, suggesting CoT is more robust to disruption than expected.

entry.title: LaTER: Efficient Test-Time Reasoning via Latent Exploration and Explicit Verification

author.name: Xuan Li, Yining Wang, Yuchen Liu, Guanjun Liu, Delai Qiu, Shengping Liu, Jiaen Liang, Wei Huang, Jun Yu, Junnan Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces LaTER, a two-stage reasoning paradigm that first explores in continuous latent space then switches to explicit chain-of-thought for verification. This training-free approach uses entropy and stop-token probes to determine when to switch, reducing token generation costs while maintaining symbolic checking ability.

entry.title: Activation Differences Reveal Backdoors: A Comparison of SAE Architectures

author.name: Sachin Kumar

entry.summary: Compares Crosscoders and Differential SAEs for detecting backdoor attacks in language models. Finds that Diff-SAE substantially outperforms Crosscoders for backdoor isolation in both LoRA and full-rank fine-tuned models, tested on a controlled SQL injection backdoor.

entry.title: Think-with-Rubrics: From External Evaluator to Internal Reasoning Guidance

author.name: Jiachen Yu, Zhihao Xu, Junjie Wang, Yujiu Yang

entry.summary: Think-with-Rubrics integrates rubric generation directly into the LLM reasoning trace, transforming evaluation rubrics from external post-hoc tools into internal guidance for instruction following. The model generates a rubric then a response, with a trained reward model scoring rubric adherence during RL training.

entry.title: SHRED: Retain-Set-Free Unlearning via Self-Distillation with Logit Demotion

author.name: Zizhao Hu, Ameya Godbole, Johnny Tian-Zheng Wei, Mohammad Rostami, Jesse Thomason, Robin Jia

entry.summary: SHRED proposes retain-set-free machine unlearning for LLMs by distinguishing high-information tokens (carrying memorized knowledge) from low-information tokens (reflecting general competence), then selectively demoting only the high-information tokens via self-distillation.

entry.title: Safe, or Simply Incapable? Rethinking Safety Evaluation for Phone-Use Agents

author.name: Zhengyang Tang, Yi Zhang, Chenxin Li, Xin Lai, Pengyuan Lyu, Yiduo Guo, Weinong Wang, Junyi Li, Yang Ding, Huawen Shen, Zhengyao Fang, Xingran Zhou, Liang Wu, Fei Tang, Sunqi Fan, Shangpin Peng, Zheng Ruan, Anran Zhang, Benyou Wang, Chengquan Zhang, Han Hu

entry.summary: Introduces PhoneSafety, a benchmark of 700 safety-critical moments from real phone interactions across 130+ apps, distinguishing whether agents avoid harm through genuine safety recognition versus inability to act. Evaluates multiple models revealing that apparent safety often reflects incapability.

entry.title: Not All Tokens Learn Alike: Attention Entropy Reveals Heterogeneous Signals in RL Reasoning

author.name: Gengyang Li, Zheng-Fan Wu, Siqi Bao, Yunfang Wu

entry.summary: Studies heterogeneous learning signals in RL-based post-training through attention entropy, finding that low-entropy 'anchor' tokens provide stable, aligned gradients while high-entropy tokens cause gradient noise. Shows sparse token subsets can preserve performance.

entry.title: Training-Induced Escape from Token Clustering in a Mean-Field Formulation of Transformers

author.name: Noboru Isobe, Daisuke Inoue, Masaaki Imaizumi

entry.summary: Studies how training reshapes token clustering in transformers using mean-field theory. Finds a training-induced phase where token distributions can escape attention-driven clustering near final layers when FFN parameters are trained with L2 regularization.

entry.title: GazeVLM: Active Vision via Internal Attention Control for Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Brown Ebouky, Gabriele Carrino, Niccolo Avogaro, Christoph Studer, Andrea Bartezzaghi, Mattia Rigotti

entry.summary: Proposes GazeVLM, a multimodal architecture that internalizes active vision by allowing VLMs to autonomously generate gaze tokens () for top-down attention control during reasoning, mimicking human metacognitive visual attention.

entry.title: Tree SAE: Learning Hierarchical Feature Structures in Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Tue M. Cao, Hoang X. Nhat, Raed Alharbi, My T. Thai

entry.summary: Tree SAE introduces a novel approach to learning hierarchical feature structures in Sparse Autoencoders by combining activation coverage with a new reconstruction condition, addressing false positives in parent-child relationships. This matters for mechanistic interpretability as it provides more semantically meaningful hierarchical features.

entry.title: Normalizing Trajectory Models

author.name: Jiatao Gu, Tianrong Chen, Ying Shen, David Berthelot, Shuangfei Zhai, Josh Susskind

entry.summary: Introduces Normalizing Trajectory Models (NTM), which model each reverse diffusion step as a conditional normalizing flow with exact likelihood training, enabling high-quality few-step generation without sacrificing the likelihood framework. Combines shallow invertible blocks with a deep parallel predictor across the trajectory.

entry.title: TraceFix: Repairing Agent Coordination Protocols with TLA+ Counterexamples

author.name: Shuren Xia, Qiwei Li, Taqiya Ehsan, Jorge Ortiz

entry.summary: TraceFix presents a verification-first pipeline for LLM multi-agent coordination that synthesizes protocols, generates formal PlusCal specifications, and uses TLA+ model checker counterexamples to iteratively repair coordination logic. Achieves full verification on all 48 tasks.

entry.title: Uneven Evolution of Cognition Across Generations of Generative AI Models

author.name: Isaac Galatzer-Levy, Daniel McDuff, Xin Liu, Jed McGiffin

entry.summary: Introduces a psychometric framework to assess cognitive profiles of generative AI models using adapted Wechsler Intelligence Scale tasks. Reveals profoundly uneven cognitive architecture with near-ceiling verbal abilities but near-floor perceptual reasoning.

entry.title: LLM-Guided Open Hypothesis Learning from Autonomous Scanning Probe Microscopy Experiments

author.name: Boris Slautin, Utkarsh Pratiush, Yu Liu, Kamyar Barakati, Sergei Kalinin

entry.summary: Introduces an open hypothesis-learning framework combining symbolic regression with LLM-based physical evaluation for autonomous scanning probe microscopy. LLMs evaluate candidate analytical relationships for physical plausibility.

entry.title: Muon with Nesterov Momentum: Heavy-Tailed Noise and (Randomized) Inexact Polar Decomposition

author.name: Sayantan Choudhury, Xiaoran Cheng, Martin Tak\'a\v{c}, Sen Na, Mladen Kolar

entry.summary: Provides convergence theory for Muon optimizer with Nesterov momentum, inexact polar decomposition, and heavy-tailed noise. Covers practical implementation details that were previously unanalyzed theoretically.

entry.title: Mitigating Cognitive Bias in RLHF by Altering Rationality

author.name: Tiffany Horter and Andrew Markham and Niki Trigoni and Serena Booth

entry.summary: Proposes adapting the rationality parameter in RLHF's Boltzmann preference model to mitigate cognitive biases in human feedback. Shows that varying beta based on comparison context can improve reward model robustness.

entry.title: A$^2$RD: Agentic Autoregressive Diffusion for Long Video Consistency

author.name: Do Xuan Long, Yale Song, Min-Yen Kan, Tomas Pfister, Long T. Le

entry.summary: Presents A²RD, an agentic autoregressive diffusion architecture for long video generation that uses a Retrieve-Synthesize-Refine-Update cycle with multimodal memory to maintain consistency across segments.

entry.title: PLOT: Progressive Localization via Optimal Transport in Neural Causal Abstraction

author.name: Jonathn Chang, Arya Datla, Ziv Goldfeld

entry.summary: Introduces PLOT, a transport-based framework for localizing causal variables in neural networks using optimal transport coupling between abstract variables and candidate neural sites, enabling mechanistic interpretability without exhaustive search.

entry.title: Towards Closing the Autoregressive Gap in Language Modeling via Entropy-Gated Continuous Bitstream Diffusion

author.name: Georgios Batzolis, Mark Girolami, Luca Ambrogioni

entry.summary: Proposes modeling text as continuous diffusion over fixed-width binary bitstreams with entropy-gated stochastic sampling, further closing the gap between diffusion language models and autoregressive models.

entry.title: The Context Gathering Decision Process: A POMDP Framework for Agentic Search

author.name: Chinmaya Kausik, Adith Swaminathan, Nathan Kallus

entry.summary: Formalizes the Context Gathering Decision Process (CGDP) as a POMDP for LLM agents navigating large environments to find relevant information, addressing issues of redundant work and premature stopping.

entry.title: Dr. Post-Training: A Data Regularization Perspective on LLM Post-Training

author.name: Pingbang Hu, Xueshen Liu, Z. Morley Mao, Jiaqi W. Ma

entry.summary: Introduces Dr. Post-Training, reconceptualizing general training data as a data-induced regularizer that prevents overfitting to scarce target data during LLM post-training, using feasible set projection of update directions.

entry.title: Learning Visual Feature-Based World Models via Residual Latent Action

author.name: Xinyu Zhang, Zhengtong Xu, Yutian Tao, Yeping Wang, Yu She, Abdeslam Boularias

entry.summary: Introduces Residual Latent Action (RLA), a new latent action representation learned from DINO residuals for visual feature-based world models. RLA enables predicting future visual features instead of raw pixels, offering efficiency gains and reduced hallucination compared to image-generation world models.

entry.title: Almost Sure Convergence Rates of Stochastic Approximation and Reinforcement Learning via a Poisson-Moreau Drift

author.name: Xinyu Liu, Zixuan Xie, Shangtong Zhang

entry.summary: Establishes near-optimal almost sure convergence rates for stochastic approximation under Markovian noise, achieving rates arbitrarily close to o(n^{-1}) for harmonic learning rates. Introduces a Poisson-Moreau drift technique applicable to Q-learning and TD learning.

entry.title: Structural Rationale Distillation via Reasoning Space Compression

author.name: Jialin Yang, Jiankun Wang, Jiajun Wu, Henry Leung, Jiayu Zhou, Steve Drew

entry.summary: D-RPC constrains teacher LLM rationales to follow a compact bank of reusable reasoning paths during distillation, producing consistent rationales across similar problems while maintaining diversity. Includes PAC-Bayes analysis of the bank size trade-off.

entry.title: SREGym: A Live Benchmark for AI SRE Agents with High-Fidelity Failure Scenarios

author.name: Jackson Clark, Yiming Su, Saad Mohammad Rafid Pial, Yifang Tian, Lily Gniedziejko, Hans-Arno Jacobsen, Yinfang Chen, Tianyin Xu

entry.summary: SREGym provides a high-fidelity benchmark for AI SRE agents with live cloud-native environments, simulating diverse faults (metastable failures, correlated failures) with ambient noise. Modular and extensible framework for evaluating diagnostic and mitigation capabilities.

entry.title: The Text Uncanny Valley: Non-Monotonic Performance Degradation in LLM Information Retrieval

author.name: Zekai Tong, Ruiyao Xu, Aryan Shrivastava, Chenhao Tan, and Ari Holtzman

entry.summary: Discovers the 'Text Uncanny Valley'—LLM detection accuracy follows a U-shaped curve when words are corrupted by whitespace insertion, with a mode transition between word-level and character-level processing explaining the valley at intermediate corruption.

entry.title: Teaching Language Models to Think in Code

author.name: Hyeon Hwang, Jiwoo Lee, Jaewoo Kang

entry.summary: ThinC proposes making code itself the primary reasoner rather than a tool invoked by natural language, with reasoning unfolding entirely through code blocks after a brief NL planning step. Distills code-centric trajectories to train small (1.7B, 4B) models that outperform larger models.

entry.title: Hard to Read, Easy to Jailbreak: How Visual Degradation Bypasses MLLM Safety Alignment

author.name: Zhixue Song, Boyan Han, Yiwei Wang, and Chi Zhang

entry.summary: Identifies that lowering image resolution in text-rendered-as-image contexts for MLLMs inadvertently enables jailbreaking due to 'Cognitive Overload' where effort to decipher degraded inputs diverts attention from safety auditing.

entry.title: Mean-Pooled Cosine Similarity is Not Length-Invariant: Theory and Cross-Domain Evidence for a Length-Invariant Alternative

author.name: Sibayan Mitra (1), Dhruv Kumar (1) ((1) BITS Pilani)

entry.summary: Proves that mean-pooled cosine similarity is not length-invariant due to transformer anisotropy, with length ratio explaining up to 75% of cross-language proximity scores. Proposes Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) as a length-invariant alternative.

entry.title: Confidence-Aware Alignment Makes Reasoning LLMs More Reliable

author.name: Kejia Chen, Jiawen Zhang, Yihong Wu, Kewei Gao, Jian Lou, Zunlei Feng, Mingli Song, Ruoxi Jia

entry.summary: Introduces CASPO, which aligns token-level confidence with step-wise logical correctness through iterative DPO without external verifiers. Proposes Confidence-aware Thought (CaT) for dynamic pruning of uncertain reasoning branches at negligible latency cost.

entry.title: ForgeVLA: Federated Vision-Language-Action Learning without Language Annotations

author.name: Yuhao Zhou, Yunpeng Zhu, Yang Zhou, Jindi Lyu, Jian Lan, Zhangyuan Wang, Dan Si, Thomas Seidl, Qing Ye, Jiancheng Lyu

entry.summary: ForgeVLA proposes federated training of Vision-Language-Action models from distributed robot vision-action pairs without centralizing data or requiring language annotations. Uses embodied instruction generation and federated learning to handle data heterogeneity across robot deployments.

entry.title: Vaporizer: Breaking Watermarking Schemes for Large Language Model Outputs

author.name: Jonathan Hong Jin Ng, Anh Tu Ngo, Anupam Chattopadhyay

entry.summary: Vaporizer demonstrates that state-of-the-art LLM watermarking schemes can be broken through various text attacks (lexical alterations, translation, neural paraphrasing) while preserving semantic content, challenging claims of robustness for production-grade watermarking.

entry.title: The Coupling Tax: How Shared Token Budgets Undermine Visible Chain-of-Thought Under Fixed Output Limits

author.name: Wenhua Nie, Junlin Liu, Jianan Wu, Zijie Meng, Yilong Fan, Zhang Zijian, Haoran Zheng and Jyh-Shing Roger Jang

entry.summary: Identifies the 'coupling tax': when CoT reasoning and final answers share one output-token budget, long reasoning traces can crowd out the answer. Provides a truncation-waste decomposition that predicts when thinking mode hurts performance.

entry.title: Tracing Uncertainty in Language Model "Reasoning"

author.name: Nils Gr\"unefeld, Bertram H{\o}jer, Philipp Mondorf, Barbara Plank, Anna Rogers, Christian Hardmeier, Stefan Heinrich, Jes Frellsen

entry.summary: Studies LM reasoning dynamics through uncertainty quantification, treating reasoning traces as evolving model states. Finds that 'uncertainty trace profiles' (features like slope and linearity of uncertainty over a trace) predict correctness with AUROC up to 0.807, even using only the first portion of the trace.

entry.title: Delta-Adapter: Scalable Exemplar-Based Image Editing with Single-Pair Supervision

author.name: Jiacheng Chen, Songze Li, Han Fu, Baoquan Zhao, Wei Liu, Yanyan Liang, Li Qing, Xudong Mao

entry.summary: Delta-Adapter enables exemplar-based image editing with single-pair supervision by extracting a semantic delta between source-target images via a pre-trained vision encoder, eliminating the need for paired training data sharing the same edit semantics.

entry.title: Don't Get Your Kroneckers in a Twist: Gaussian Processes on High-Dimensional Incomplete Grids

author.name: Mads Greisen H{\o}jlund, August Smart Lykke-M{\o}ller, Henry Moss, Ove Christiansen

entry.summary: CUTS-GPR enables exact Gaussian process regression in high dimensions by exploiting additive kernel structure on incomplete grids, achieving near-linear scaling with data size and polynomial scaling with dimensionality, demonstrated with billions of data points.

entry.title: Control Debt

author.name: Ida Caspary

entry.summary: Introduces the concept of 'control debt'—the gap between what AI control evaluations assume and what actually exists in production environments. Describes a realistic scenario where monitoring, logging, escalation, and credential management fall far short of what safety protocols require.

entry.title: Flow-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Flow Matching Models

author.name: Zhen Fang, Wenxuan Huang, Yu Zeng, Yiming Zhao, Shuang Chen, Kaituo Feng, Yunlong Lin, Lin Chen, Zehui Chen, Shaosheng Cao, and Feng Zhao

entry.summary: Flow-OPD introduces the first on-policy distillation framework for Flow Matching text-to-image models, addressing reward sparsity and gradient interference in multi-task alignment through a two-stage approach with domain-specialized teacher models.

entry.title: RateQuant: Optimal Mixed-Precision KV Cache Quantization via Rate-Distortion Theory

author.name: Fei Zuo, Zikang Zhou, Hao Cong, Xiaoyan Xi, Ho Fai Leung

entry.summary: Proposes RateQuant, a mixed-precision KV cache quantization method grounded in rate-distortion theory. Shows that naive bit allocation based on head importance can backfire due to varying distortion curves across quantizers, and provides theoretically optimal allocation.

entry.title: Toeplitz MLP Mixers are Low Complexity, Information-Rich Sequence Models

author.name: Benjamin L. Badger and Ethan Roland

entry.summary: Introduces Toeplitz MLP Mixer (TMM), a sub-quadratic architecture replacing attention with triangular-masked Toeplitz matrix multiplication, achieving O(dn log n) training time and improved information retention over transformers at comparable compute.

entry.title: CASCADE: Case-Based Continual Adaptation for Large Language Models During Deployment

author.name: Siyuan Guo, Yali Du, Hechang Chen, Yi Chang, Jun Wang

entry.summary: Formalizes deployment-time learning (DTL) as a third stage in the LLM lifecycle and introduces CASCADE, a framework using episodic memory and contextual bandits to enable LLM agents to learn from experience during deployment without parameter updates.

entry.title: Gradient Extrapolation-Based Policy Optimization

author.name: Ismam Nur Swapnil, Aranya Saha, Tanvir Ahmed Khan, Mohammad Ariful Haque, Ser-Nam Lim

entry.summary: Proposes GXPO, a gradient extrapolation method for GRPO-style reasoning RL that approximates multi-step lookahead using only three backward passes without additional rollouts. Plug-compatible with existing GRPO implementations.

entry.title: Distributional Process Reward Models: Calibrated Prediction of Future Rewards via Conditional Optimal Transport

author.name: Rachel Ma, Dylan Hadfield-Menell, Kristjan Greenewald

entry.summary: Proposes using conditional optimal transport for calibrating Process Reward Models (PRMs), yielding structurally valid quantile estimates that enable confidence-aware inference-time scaling. Evaluated on MATH-500 and harder OOD benchmarks.

entry.title: LookWhen? Fast Video Recognition by Learning When, Where, and What to Compute

author.name: Ali Salamatian and Anthony Fuller and Pritam Sarkar and James R. Green and Leonid Sigal and Evan Shelhamer

entry.summary: Introduces LookWhen, a framework that factorizes video recognition into learning when, where, and what to compute by selecting only top-K tokens from a shallow scoring of all spatiotemporal tokens. Achieves significant compute savings while approximating full-video performance.

entry.title: Randomness is sometimes necessary for coordination

author.name: Rohan Patil, Jai Malegaonkar, Henrik I. Christensen

entry.summary: Proposes Diamond Attention for cooperative multi-agent RL, where agents sample random numbers to create transient rank orderings that enable role differentiation without breaking parameter sharing. Shows randomness is necessary for coordination under symmetric observations.

entry.title: On Privacy Leakage in Tabular Diffusion Models: Influential Factors, Attacker Knowledge, and Metrics

author.name: Masoumeh Shafieinejad, D. B. Emerson, Behnoosh Zamanlooy, Elaheh Bassak, Fatemeh Tavakoli, Sara Kodeiri, Marcelo Lotif, Xi He

entry.summary: Studies privacy leakage in tabular diffusion models using membership inference attacks in black- and white-box settings. Quantifies impact of training setup, synthesis choices, and attacker knowledge on privacy risk.

entry.title: Same Signal, Opposite Meaning: Direction-Informed Adaptive Learning for LLM Agents

author.name: Ziming Li, Jiatan Huang, Xiaoguang Guo, Guilin Wang, Chuxu Zhang

entry.summary: Shows that gating signals for adaptive compute in LLM agents can reverse direction across environments - the same signal predicts benefit in one setting and harm in another. Proposes direction-informed adaptive learning.

entry.title: Can LLMs Take Retrieved Information with a Grain of Salt?

author.name: Behzad Shayegh, Mohamed Osama Ahmed, Fred Tung, Leo Feng

entry.summary: Evaluates eight LLMs on context-certainty obedience - how well they adjust responses to match expressed certainty in retrieved information. Reveals systematic failures and proposes mitigation strategies.

entry.title: Adaptive auditing of AI systems with anytime-valid guarantees

author.name: Siyu Zhou, Patrick Vossler, Venkatesh Sivaraman, Yifan Mai, Jean Feng

entry.summary: Introduces an adaptive auditing framework for AI systems with anytime-valid statistical guarantees, enabling rigorous conclusions from highly adaptive testing with as few as 10-50 annotated cases.

entry.title: A Systematic Investigation of The RL-Jailbreaker in LLMs

author.name: Montaser Mohammedalamen, Kevin Roice, Reginald McLean, Alyssa Lefaivre \v{S}kopac

entry.summary: Presents the first systematic decomposition of RL-based jailbreaking of LLMs, deconstructing the framework into components (reward function, action space, RL algorithm) to identify structural determinants of adversarial success.

entry.title: Towards Differentially Private Reinforcement Learning with General Function Approximation

author.name: Yi He, Xingyu Zhou

entry.summary: Presents first theoretical guarantees for differentially private online RL with general function approximation, achieving regret scaling of O(K^{3/5}) matching the linear case. Also establishes first coverability-based regret bound for batched RL.

entry.title: GSM-SEM: Benchmark and Framework for Generating Semantically Variant Augmentations

author.name: Jyotika Singh, Fang Tu, Aziza Mirzadova, Amit Agarwal, Hitesh Laxmichand Patel, Sandip Ghoshal, Miguel Ballesteros, Yassine Benajiba, Weiyi Sun, Graham Horwood, Sujith Ravi, Dan Roth

entry.summary: Introduces GSM-SEM, a reusable stochastic framework for generating semantically diverse variants of math benchmarks by modifying entities, attributes, and relationships, addressing memorization concerns with fixed test sets like GSM8K.

entry.title: Decoupling Semantics and Fingerprints: A Universal Representation for AI-Generated Image Detection

author.name: Zhiyuan Wang (1), Yanxiang Chen (2), Yuanzhi Yao (2), Yunfeng Diao (2) ((1) Hefei University of Technology, (2) Key Laboratory of Knowledge Engineering with Big Data (Hefei University of Technology), Ministry of Education / School of Computer Science and Information Engineering, Hefei University of Technology / Intelligent Interconnected Systems Laboratory of Anhui Province (Hefei University of Technology))

entry.summary: Proposes ODPNet for AI-generated image detection that decouples semantic content from generator-specific fingerprints using spectral analysis. The key insight is that different generator fingerprints (GAN stripes vs diffusion spots) occupy orthogonal frequency subspaces, enabling universal forgery detection across unseen architectures.

entry.title: Decentralized Diffusion Policy Learning for Enhanced Exploration in Cooperative Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yuyang Zhang, Haldun Balim, Na Li

entry.summary: Proposes decentralized diffusion policy learning (DDPL) for cooperative multi-agent RL, replacing Gaussian policies with diffusion models to overcome exploration limitations. Shows that Gaussian policy expressiveness degrades with agent count.

entry.title: Region4Web: Rethinking Observation Space Granularity for Web Agents

author.name: Donguk Kwon, Dongha Lee

entry.summary: Region4Web reorganizes web page observation from element-level to functional region granularity for web agents, using hierarchical decomposition and semantic abstraction of the AXTree. Proposes PageDigest for efficient inference.

entry.title: Regret-Oracle Complexity Tradeoffs in Agnostic Online Learning

author.name: Idan Attias and Steve Hanneke and Arvind Ramaswami

entry.summary: Significantly improves oracle complexity for agnostic online learning from doubly-exponential to polynomial in Littlestone dimension, while relying only on ERM oracles. Establishes fundamental tradeoffs between regret and oracle complexity.

entry.title: Hallucination Detection via Activations of Open-Weight Proxy Analyzers

author.name: Akshita Singh, Prabesh Paudel, Siddhartha Roy

entry.summary: Introduces a proxy-analyzer framework for hallucination detection that reads generated text through a small open-weight model and detects hallucinations using the reader's internal activations, working equally well with closed APIs like GPT-4 as with open models.

entry.title: Reformulating KV Cache Eviction Problem for Long-Context LLM Inference

author.name: Tho Mai, Joo-Young Kim

entry.summary: LaProx reformulates KV cache eviction from head-wise attention weight averaging to an output-aware, layer-wise matrix multiplication approximation that explicitly models attention-value interactions and inter-head dependencies, achieving the first unified budget allocation across all layers and heads.

entry.title: When Are Experts Misrouted? Counterfactual Routing Analysis in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models

author.name: Youngsik Yoon, Siwei Wang, Wei Chen, Jungseul Ok

entry.summary: Analyzes routing failures in Mixture-of-Experts language models through counterfactual analysis, finding that routers are well-aligned on confident tokens but uninformative on fragile reasoning tokens where better routes exist but aren't selected.

entry.title: Implicit Compression Regularization: Concise Reasoning via Internal Shorter Distributions in RL Post-Training

author.name: Chen Wang, Hexuan Deng, Yining Zhang, Yuchen Zhang, Jionghao Bai, Zhaochun Li, Ge Lan, Yue Wang

entry.summary: Identifies 'implicit compression regularization' in RL post-training of LLMs, showing that shorter responses are initially more accurate but this advantage erodes during compression. Proposes leveraging internal shorter distributions as a natural compression signal to reduce overthinking without length penalties.

entry.title: MISA: Mixture of Indexer Sparse Attention for Long-Context LLM Inference

author.name: Ruijie Zhou, Fanxu Meng, Yufei Xu, Tongxuan Liu, Guangming Lu, Muhan Zhang, Wenjie Pei

entry.summary: Proposes MISA, a drop-in replacement for DeepSeek Sparse Attention's indexer that treats indexer heads as mixture-of-experts, using cheap block-level statistics to select active heads. Reduces the dominant indexer cost on long contexts.

entry.title: Unsolvability Ceiling in Multi-LLM Routing: An Empirical Study of Evaluation Artifacts

author.name: Saloni Garg, Amit Sagtani

entry.summary: Large-scale study of multi-LLM routing showing that much of the reported 'unsolvability ceiling' is actually evaluation artifacts: judge biases, truncation effects, and format mismatches. Reduces unsolvability rates from ~30% to 10-15% through dual-judge validation.

entry.title: OrchJail: Jailbreaking Tool-Calling Text-to-Image Agents by Orchestration-Guided Fuzzing

author.name: Jianming Chen, Yawen Wang, Junjie Wang, Zhe Liu, Qing Wang, Fanjiang Xu

entry.summary: Introduces OrchJail, a fuzzing framework for jailbreaking tool-calling text-to-image agents by exploiting tool orchestration patterns. Shows that individually benign tool steps can combine into unsafe outputs through multi-step orchestration.

entry.title: The Moltbook Files: A Harmless Slopocalypse or Humanity's Last Experiment

author.name: William Brach, Federico Torrielli, Stine Lyngs{\o} Beltoft, Annemette Brok Pirchert, Peter Schneider-Kamp, Lukas Galke Poech

entry.summary: Introduces the Moltbook Files dataset (232K posts, 2.2M comments) from a Reddit-like platform where AI agents autonomously post and interact, analyzing emergent behavior, community structure, and safety concerns including leaked API keys and passwords. Fine-tuning experiments on Qwen2.5-14B examine contamination effects.

entry.title: Physical Simulators as Do-Operators: Causal Discovery under Latent Confounders for AI-for-Science

author.name: Tsuyoshi Okita

entry.summary: CFM-SD uses physical simulators as do-operators in Pearl's interventional calculus for causal discovery under latent confounders, requiring only O(d) interventions for d-variable structure identification. Targets AI-for-Science settings where interventions are expensive physics simulations.

entry.title: Does Your Neural Network Extrapolate? Feature Engineering as Identifiability Bias for OOD Generalization

author.name: Leonel Aguilar, Jan Nagler, Christoph Hoelscher, Nino Antulov-Fantulin

entry.summary: Demonstrates that OOD extrapolation is fundamentally non-identifiable from a single training window, with infinitely many observationally equivalent DGPs diverging outside it. Shows that structural commitments (feature map, label map, model class) govern OOD generalization while leaving ID performance unchanged.

entry.title: Revisiting Transformer Layer Parameterization Through Causal Energy Minimization

author.name: Jin Xu, Camille Couturier, Victor R\"uhle, Saravan Rajmohan, James Hensman

entry.summary: Revisits Transformer layer parameterization through Causal Energy Minimization, showing MHA can be derived as gradient updates on interaction energy and gated MLPs viewed through element-wise energy. Identifies design space including weight sharing and diagonal-plus-low-rank interactions.

entry.title: Reliable Chain-of-Thought via Prefix Consistency

author.name: Naoto Iwase, Yuki Ichihara, Mohammad Atif Quamar, Junpei Komiyama

entry.summary: Proposes prefix consistency as a reliability signal for Chain-of-Thought reasoning: truncating and regenerating CoT traces reveals that correct answers reproduce more stably. This signal improves majority voting without needing log-probabilities.

entry.title: Gradient Starvation in Binary-Reward GRPO: Why Group-Mean Centering Fails and Why the Simplest Fix Works

author.name: Wenhua Nie, Jianan Wu, Junlin Liu, Ziwei Li, Zheng Lin, Zhang Zijian, Yilong Fan, Haoran Zheng and Jyh-Shing Roger Jang

entry.summary: Identifies and analyzes gradient starvation in GRPO under binary rewards where all-correct or all-wrong groups yield zero advantage. Proves degeneracy rate exceeds Bernoulli prediction and proposes a simple Sign advantage fix.

entry.title: Rethinking State Tracking in Recurrent Models Through Error Control Dynamics

author.name: Jiwan Chung, Heechan Choi, Seon Joo Kim

entry.summary: Proves that affine recurrent networks (including SSMs and Linear Attention) cannot correct errors along state-separating subspaces once they preserve states, explaining why they learn finite-horizon rather than robust state tracking.

entry.title: MatryoshkaLoRA: Learning Accurate Hierarchical Low-Rank Representations for LLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: Ionut-Vlad Modoranu, Mher Safaryan, Dan Alistarh

entry.summary: Proposes MatryoshkaLoRA, a Matryoshka-inspired LoRA training framework that learns accurate hierarchical low-rank representations, allowing a single training run to produce LoRA adapters at multiple ranks without exhaustive grid search.

entry.title: Trajectory as the Teacher: Few-Step Discrete Flow Matching via Energy-Navigated Distillation

author.name: Amin Karimi Monsefi, Dominic Culver, Nikhil Bhendawade, Manuel R. Ciosici, Yizhe Zhang, Irina Belousova

entry.summary: TS-DFM proposes that poor distillation in discrete flow matching for text generation is caused by low-quality training trajectories (blind stochastic jumps), not student capacity. It introduces an energy-guided navigation approach to produce better trajectories for few-step distillation.

entry.title: Slowly Annealed Langevin Dynamics: Theory and Applications to Training-Free Guided Generation

author.name: Atsushi Nitanda, Dake Bu, Yueming Lyu, Tanya Veeravalli

entry.summary: Establishes non-asymptotic convergence guarantees for Slowly Annealed Langevin Dynamics (SALD) and proposes Velocity-Aware SALD for training-free guided generation with pretrained score-based models, providing a principled framework for guidance correction.

entry.title: Seeing Across Skies and Streets: Feedforward 3D Reconstruction from Satellite, Drone, and Ground Images

author.name: Qiwei Wang, Zhongyao Tuo, Xianghui Ze, Yujiao Shi

entry.summary: Cross3R introduces a UAV image as an intermediate viewpoint between satellite and ground imagery for full 6-DoF cross-view localization and 3D reconstruction, overcoming the 3-DoF limitation of nadir satellite imagery alone.

entry.title: Object Hallucination-Free Reinforcement Unlearning for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Kaidi Jia, Yujie Lin, Chengyi Yang, Jiayao Ma, Jinsong Su

entry.summary: HFRU proposes reinforcement unlearning for vision-language models that operates on the vision encoder rather than just the language decoder, using GRPO-based optimization with abstraction rewards to achieve deep semantic removal while mitigating hallucination.

entry.title: 123D: Unifying Multi-Modal Autonomous Driving Data at Scale

author.name: Daniel Dauner, Valentin Charraut, Bastian Berle, Tianyu Li, Long Nguyen, Jiabao Wang, Changhui Jing, Maximilian Igl, Holger Caesar, Boris Ivanovic, Yiyi Liao, Andreas Geiger, Kashyap Chitta

entry.summary: Presents 123D, an open-source framework that unifies multi-modal autonomous driving datasets (cameras, lidar, ego states, annotations, maps) through a single API. Addresses fragmentation across datasets with different formats, synchronization schemes, and annotation conventions to enable cross-dataset training and evaluation.

entry.title: Topology-Enhanced Alignment for Large Language Models: Trajectory Topology Loss and Topological Preference Optimization

author.name: Yurui Pan, Ke Xu, Bo Peng

entry.summary: Proposes topology-enhanced LLM alignment using 0-dimensional persistent homology to regularize semantic trajectories in hidden space. Introduces Trajectory Topology Loss for SFT and Topological Preference Optimization for DPO.

entry.title: KL for a KL: On-Policy Distillation with Control Variate Baseline

author.name: Minjae Oh, Sangjun Song, Gyubin Choi, Yunho Choi, Yohan Jo

entry.summary: Proposes vOPD, stabilizing on-policy distillation for LLMs by casting it as policy-gradient RL with a control variate baseline. The value function has closed form as per-token negative reverse KL divergence, requiring no additional critic.

entry.title: It Just Takes Two: Scaling Amortized Inference to Large Sets

author.name: Antoine Wehenkel, Michael Kagan, Lukas Heinrich, Chris Pollard

entry.summary: Introduces a strategy for scaling amortized neural posterior estimation to large sets by training a mean-pool Deep Set on sets of size at most two, which generalizes to arbitrary set sizes, decoupling representation learning from posterior modeling.

entry.title: Rethinking Dense Optical Flow without Test-Time Scaling

author.name: Praroop Chanda, Suryansh Kumar

entry.summary: Argues that dense optical flow can be estimated accurately in a single forward pass by leveraging pretrained foundation model representations, without requiring iterative refinement at test time, challenging the prevailing trend of test-time scaling.

entry.title: LKV: End-to-End Learning of Head-wise Budgets and Token Selection for LLM KV Cache Eviction

author.name: Enshuai Zhou, Yifan Hao, Chao Wang, Rui Zhang, Di Huang, Jiaming Guo, Xing Hu, Zidong Du, Qi Guo, Yunji Chen

entry.summary: Introduces LKV, an end-to-end differentiable framework for KV cache eviction that learns both head-wise budgets and token selection, replacing heuristic approaches. Formulates KV compression as a differentiable optimization problem.

entry.title: Traffic Scenario Orchestration from Language via Constraint Satisfaction

author.name: Frieda Rong, Chris Zhang, Kelvin Wong, Raquel Urtasun

entry.summary: Presents a language-in, simulation-out scenario orchestrator for autonomous vehicle testing that uses foundation model reasoning to translate natural language descriptions into constraint-solving problems for generating closed-loop test scenarios.

entry.title: Retrieve, Integrate, and Synthesize: Spatial-Semantic Grounded Latent Visual Reasoning

author.name: Jin Cui, Xinyue Long, Xunyong Zhang, Yadong Zhang, Chuanchang Su, Jingye Gan, Boran Zhao, Pengju Ren

entry.summary: RIS proposes spatial-semantic grounded latent visual reasoning for multimodal LLMs, addressing manifold compatibility issues where latent reasoning trajectories drift from pretrained circuits. Uses retrieve, integrate, and synthesize steps for compatible latent reasoning.

entry.title: Learning Agent Routing From Early Experience

author.name: Yimin Wang, Jiahao Qiu, Xuan Qi, Xinzhe Juan, Jingzhe Shi, Zelin Zhao, Hongru Wang, Shilong Liu, Mengdi Wang

entry.summary: BoundaryRouter routes queries between lightweight LLM inference and full agent execution under cold-start settings, using early behavioral experience and rubric-guided reasoning without requiring training data.

entry.title: Prune-OPD: Efficient and Reliable On-Policy Distillation for Long-Horizon Reasoning

author.name: Zhicheng Yang, Zhijiang Guo, Yifan Song, Minrui Xu, Yongxin Wang, Yiwei Wang, Xiaodan Liang, Jing Tang

entry.summary: Introduces Prune-OPD, a framework that detects when student-teacher prefix drift occurs during on-policy distillation for long-horizon reasoning, and dynamically prunes drifted trajectories to save compute and improve training quality.

entry.title: Convergent Stochastic Training of Attention and Understanding LoRA

author.name: Zhengkai Sun, Dibyakanti Kumar, Alejandro F Frangi, Anirbit Mukherjee and Mingfei Sun

entry.summary: Proves that attention layers and LoRA on shallow neural nets satisfy Poincaré inequality for the corresponding Gibbs measure under mild regularization, establishing convergence guarantees for stochastic training methods including an SDE that mimics SGD.

entry.title: HEART: Hyperspherical Embedding Alignment via Kent-Representation Traversal in Diffusion Models

author.name: Arani Roy, Shristi Das Biswas, Kaushik Roy

entry.summary: HEART discovers that text encoder embeddings in diffusion models lie on a hypersphere and proposes Kent distribution-based traversal for controlling text-to-image generation, reducing unintended side effects when modifying attributes.

entry.title: Rubric-Grounded RL: Structured Judge Rewards for Generalizable Reasoning

author.name: Manish Bhattarai, Ismael Boureima, Nishath Rajiv Ranasinghe, Scott Pakin, Dan O'Malley

entry.summary: Formalizes rubric-grounded reinforcement learning where a frozen LLM judge scores responses on multiple task-specific criteria, providing partial-credit optimization signals. Demonstrates on scientific document tasks with Llama-3.1-8B and GRPO.

entry.title: AdaSpark: Adaptive Sparsity for Efficient Long-Video Understanding

author.name: Handong Li, Zikang Liu, Longteng Guo, Tongtian Yue, Yepeng Tang, Xinxin Zhu, Chuanyang Zheng, Ziming Wang, Zhibin Wang, Jun Song, Cheng Yu, Bo Zheng, Jing Liu

entry.summary: Introduces AdaSpark, an adaptive sparsity framework for efficient long-video understanding that partitions video into 3D spatio-temporal cubes and employs context-aware attention and FFN selection. Achieves significant speedups while maintaining fine-grained perception.

entry.title: MASPO: Joint Prompt Optimization for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Zhexuan Wang, Xuebo Liu, Li Wang, Zifei Shan, Yutong Wang, Zhenxi Song, Min Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces MASPO, a framework for jointly optimizing prompts across all agents in LLM-based multi-agent systems. Key innovation is a joint evaluation mechanism that assesses prompts by their capacity to facilitate downstream success for successor agents.

entry.title: Visual Text Compression as Measure Transport

author.name: Lv Tang, Tianyi Zheng, Yang Liu, Bo Li, Xingyu Li

entry.summary: Formulates visual text compression (rendering text as images for VLMs) through measure transport theory, treating text and visual tokens as probability measures. Provides principled framework for understanding when visual encoding preserves task-relevant information.

entry.title: Conditional generation of antibody sequences with classifier-guided germline-absorbing discrete diffusion

author.name: Justin Sanders, Luca Giancardo, Lan Guo, Yue Zhao, Kemal Sonmez, Nina Cheng, Melih Yilmaz

entry.summary: Proposes discrete diffusion fine-tuning for antibody sequence design with germline-absorbing noise and classifier-guided conditional generation. Addresses limitations of protein language models that memorize germline sequences rather than modeling somatic variation.

entry.title: When Does a Language Model Commit? A Finite-Answer Theory of Pre-Verbalization Commitment

author.name: Long Zhang, Wei-neng Chen, Feng-feng Wei, Zi-bo Qin

entry.summary: Studies when language models commit to an answer during reasoning by defining finite-answer preference stabilization through log-odds tracking. Shows that answer preference stabilizes before the answer is verbalized in Qwen3-4B.

entry.title: OmicsLM: A Multimodal Large Language Model for Multi-Sample Omics Reasoning

author.name: Maciej Sypetkowski and Joanna Krawczyk and {\L}ukasz Smoli\'nski and Remigiusz Kinas and Przemys{\l}aw Pietrzak and Tomasz Jetka and Rafa{\l} Powalski

entry.summary: Introduces OmicsLM, a multimodal LLM connecting quantitative transcriptomic profiles with natural-language biological reasoning. Trained on 5.5M+ instruction-following examples, it processes multiple interleaved biological samples in one context.

entry.title: Sparse Attention as a Range Searching Problem: Towards an Inference-Efficient Index for KV Cache

author.name: Mohsen Dehghankar, Abolfazl Asudeh

entry.summary: Formulates sparse attention as a range searching problem to build inference-efficient KV cache indices that guarantee zero false negatives. Shows that missing even one critical key causes sharp error spikes in long reasoning tasks.

entry.title: ProtSent: Protein Sentence Transformers

author.name: Dan Ofer, Oriel Perets, Michal Linial, and Nadav Rappoport

entry.summary: Introduces ProtSent, a contrastive fine-tuning framework for protein language models that produces general-purpose sequence embeddings trained across five protein-pair datasets. Evaluates on 23 downstream tasks showing improved neighborhood quality.

entry.title: IntentGrasp: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Intent Understanding

author.name: Yuwei Yin, Chuyuan Li, Giuseppe Carenini

entry.summary: Introduces IntentGrasp, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating LLM intent understanding across 49 corpora and 12 domains. Tests 20 LLMs including GPT-5.4, Gemini-3.1-Pro, and Claude-Opus-4.7, revealing even frontier models have room for improvement.

entry.title: Benchmarked Yet Not Measured -- Generative AI Should be Evaluated Against Real-World Utility

author.name: Ishani Mondal, Shweta Bhardwaj

entry.summary: Identifies three recurring failures in AI evaluation (proxy displacement, temporal collapse, distributional concealment) across 28 deployment cases. Argues for paradigm shift from benchmark-centered to stakeholder-conditioned utility transparency.

entry.title: How Well Do LLMs Perform on the Simplest Long-Chain Reasoning Tasks: An Empirical Study on the Equivalence Class Problem

author.name: Chun Zheng, Lianlong Wu, Bingqian Li, Lvting Liu, and Yi Zhou

entry.summary: Evaluates LLMs on the Equivalence Class Problem, a simple long-chain reasoning task. Shows non-reasoning LLMs fail while reasoning models are significantly better but still struggle to completely solve this fundamental task.

entry.title: Kernel Selection is Model Selection: A Unified Complexity-Penalized Approach for MMD Two-Sample Tests

author.name: Yijin Ni, Xiaoming Huo

entry.summary: Frames data-driven kernel selection for MMD two-sample tests as model selection, proposing complexity-penalized criteria that enable continuous optimization over kernel spaces including deep kernels.

entry.title: Reflections and New Directions for Human-Centered Large Language Models

author.name: Caleb Ziems, Dora Zhao, Rose E. Wang, Matthew J\"orke, Ahmad Rushdi, Advit Deepak, Sunny Yu, Anshika Agarwal, Harshvardhan Agarwal, Gabriela Aranguiz-Dias, Aditri Bhagirath, Justine Breuch, Huanxing Chen, Ruishi Chen, Sarah Chen, Haocheng Fan, William Fang, Cat Gonzales Fergesen, Daniel Frees, Tian Gao, Ziqing Huang, Vishal Jain, Yucheng Jiang, Kirill Kalinin, Su Doga Karaca, Arpandeep Khatua, Teland La, Isabelle Levent, Miranda Li, Xinling Li, Yongce Li, Angela Liu, Minsik Oh, Nathan J. Paek, Anthony Qin, Emily Redmond, Michael J. Ryan, Aadesh Salecha, Xiaoxian Shen, Pranava Singhal, Shashanka Subrahmanya, Mei Tan, Irawadee Thawornbut, Michelle Vinocour, Xiaoyue Wang, Zheng Wang, Henry Jin Weng, Pawan Wirawarn, Shirley Wu, Sophie Wu, Yichen Xie, Patrick Ye, Sean Zhang, Yutong Zhang, Cathy Zhou, Yiling Zhao, James Landay, Diyi Yang

entry.summary: Presents a comprehensive framework for Human-Centered LLMs integrating NLP, HCI, and responsible AI perspectives. Argues for addressing human concerns throughout the development lifecycle, not just in post-hoc alignment.

entry.title: MELD: Multi-Task Equilibrated Learning Detector for AI-Generated Text

author.name: Chenjun Li, Cheng Wan, Johannes C. Paetzold

entry.summary: Introduces MELD, a multi-task detector for AI-generated text that enriches binary detection with auxiliary tasks for generator, attack, and domain identification. Aims for robustness to attacks and transfer to unseen generators.

entry.title: Target-Aware Data Augmentation for SAT Prediction

author.name: Eshed Gal, Uri Ascher, Eldad Haber

entry.summary: Proposes a target-aware, solver-free data generation framework for SAT prediction that produces correctly labeled instances by construction. Eliminates expensive solver-in-the-loop labeling while matching target benchmark structure.

entry.title: Learned Lyapunov Shielding for Adaptive Control

author.name: Giansalvo Cirrincione and Adriano Fagiolini

entry.summary: Combines a structured Lyapunov function learned via Cholesky parameterization with a Soft Actor-Critic RL policy and physics-informed neural network for adaptive robot control with safety guarantees. The safety filter projects policy outputs onto safe sets without online QP solvers.

entry.title: Adaptive Memory Decay for Log-Linear Attention

author.name: Yaxita Amin, Helen Zichen Li, Mengfan Zhang, Samet Ayhan

entry.summary: Proposes making the memory decay parameter in log-linear attention input-dependent via a lightweight MLP, producing per-head, per-step decay values. This adaptive approach navigates the memory-compute tradeoff more flexibly than fixed decay.

entry.title: Equivalence of Coarse and Fine-Grained Models for Learning with Distribution Shift

author.name: Adam R. Klivans, Shyamal Patel, Konstantinos Stavropoulos, Arsen Vasilyan

entry.summary: Proves a surprising equivalence between PQ learning (point-wise rejection) and TDS learning (set-wise rejection) in distribution-free settings, implying first hardness results for TDS learning of basic concept classes like halfspaces.

entry.title: FlashMol: High-Quality Molecule Generation in as Few as Four Steps

author.name: Xinyuan Wei, Zian Li, Shaoheng Yan, Cai Zhou, Muhan Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces FlashMol, an ultra-fast molecule generation model producing high-quality 3D conformations in as few as 4 steps via distribution matching distillation adapted to the molecular domain.

entry.title: Delulu: A Verified Multi-Lingual Benchmark for Code Hallucination Detection in Fill-in-the-Middle Tasks

author.name: Mahdi Erfanian, Nelson Daniel Troncoso, Aashna Garg, Amabel Gale, Xiaoyu Liu, Pareesa Ameneh Golnari, Shengyu Fu

entry.summary: Introduces Delulu, a verified multi-lingual benchmark of 1,951 FIM samples across 7 languages and 4 hallucination types for detecting code generation hallucinations, with Docker-based verification of correctness.

entry.title: Integrating Causal DAGs in Deep RL: Activating Minimal Markovian States with Multi-Order Exposure

author.name: Jiamin Xu, Jacqueline Maasch, Kyra Gan

entry.summary: Provides a procedure for constructing provably minimal Markov state representations from longitudinal causal graphs for deep RL, and introduces multi-order exposure to help neural networks exploit this minimality.

entry.title: PolarAdamW: Disentangling Spectral Control and Schur Gauge-Equivariance in Matrix Optimisation

author.name: Haozhou Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces PolarAdamW, separating Muon's polar spectral-norm control from its Schur gauge-equivariance by applying the polar map to AdamW's preconditioned direction. Shows spectral control alone accounts for most gains on DeiT-Tiny.

entry.title: Test-Time Compositional Generalization in Diffusion Models via Concept Discovery

author.name: Zekun Wang and Anant Gupta and Tianyi Zhu and Christopher J. MacLellan

entry.summary: Proposes a test-time method for compositional generalization in diffusion models that discovers query-specific concepts from learned score functions and composes them via product-of-experts. Unlike prior methods, it doesn't assume relevant concepts are already available.

entry.title: The Translation Tax Is Not a Scalar: A Counterfactual Audit of English-Source Cue Inheritance in Chinese Multilingual Benchmarks

author.name: Zezheng Lin, Fengming Liu, and Handi Li

entry.summary: Challenges the common assumption that translated benchmarks uniformly inflate LLM scores by preserving English-source cues. In English-to-Chinese evaluation, finds the 'translation tax' is model-family dependent rather than uniform, with a residue dose-response effect.

entry.title: Solving Max-Cut to Global Optimality via Feasibility-Preserving Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Hao Chen, Chendi Qian, Christopher Morris, Andrea Lodi, Can Li

entry.summary: Proposes a GNN-based neural proxy for SDP solvers within branch-and-bound for Max-Cut, predicting both primal- and dual-feasible solutions with O(n²+ne) complexity. Can be plugged into exact solvers while maintaining solution feasibility guarantees.

entry.title: GAD in the Wild: Benchmarking Graph Anomaly Detection under Realistic Deployment Challenges

author.name: Jingjing Zhou and Shiyu Huang and Qing Qing and Zuquan Yuan and Huafei Huang and Ziqi Xu and Mingliang Hou and Xikun Zhang and Renqiang Luo and Ivan Lee

entry.summary: Presents a multi-dimensional benchmark for graph anomaly detection under realistic deployment challenges: million-scale graphs, extreme anomaly scarcity, and missing node attributes, including industrial-scale datasets with over 3.7M nodes.

entry.title: Can You Break RLVER? Probing Adversarial Robustness of RL-Trained Empathetic Agents

author.name: Deeraj S K, Sadhana Devarajan, Krishna Mehra, Sudhakar Mishra

entry.summary: Constructs the Adversarial Empathy Benchmark (AEB) to evaluate empathetic AI models under adversarial conditions like gaslighting and emotional escalation. Introduces the Emotional Consistency Score to measure robustness beyond cooperative benchmarks.

entry.title: Qwen3-VL-Seg: Unlocking Open-World Referring Segmentation with Vision-Language Grounding

author.name: Yuan Yao, Qiushi Yang, Humen Zhong, Jiangning Wei, Yifang Men, Shuai Bai, Miaomiao Cui, Zhibo Yang

entry.summary: Qwen3-VL-Seg adds pixel-level segmentation to Qwen3-VL by treating MLLM-predicted boxes as semantic priors and decoding them into dense masks through lightweight pixel decoding, avoiding heavy external segmentation models like SAM.

entry.title: Learned Lagrangian Models of PDEs via Euler-Lagrange Residual Minimization

author.name: Lyra Zhornyak, Eric Forgoston, M. Ani Hsieh

entry.summary: Presents the first method to forecast PDE dynamics using a learned continuous Lagrangian, with an optimization-based integrator that minimizes Euler-Lagrange residuals on local space-time patches for stable long-range predictions.

entry.title: HyperEyes: Dual-Grained Efficiency-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Parallel Multimodal Search Agents

author.name: Guankai Li, Jiabin Chen, Yi Xu, Xichen Zhang, Yuan Lu

entry.summary: HyperEyes is a parallel multimodal search agent that dispatches multiple grounded queries concurrently within a round, treating inference efficiency as a first-class training objective using dual-grained reinforcement learning.

entry.title: See Tomorrow, Act Today: Foresight-Driven Autonomous Driving

author.name: Bozhou Zhang, Nan Song, Yuang Wang, Jiankang Deng, Xiatian Zhu, Li Zhang

entry.summary: ForeSight introduces an autonomous driving framework that uses a world model to first imagine future scenes and then plans actions conditioned on these imagined futures, shifting from reactive to anticipatory decision-making. This mirrors how human drivers mentally simulate outcomes before acting.

entry.title: Same Brain, Different Prediction: How Preprocessing Choices Undermine EEG Decoding Reliability

author.name: Dengzhe Hou, Zihao Wu, Lingyu Jiang, Zirui Li, Fangzhou Lin, Kazunori D. Yamada

entry.summary: Demonstrates that up to 42% of EEG trial-level predictions flip when only preprocessing changes, formalizes preprocessing as a counterfactual intervention space, and provides tools (Walsh-Hadamard decomposition, ensemble method) to make this instability measurable and reducible.

entry.title: On the Robustness of Distribution Support under Diffusion Guidance

author.name: Ruijia Cao, Yuchen Wu, Nisha Chadramoorthy

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis showing that guided diffusion processes almost always generate samples remaining close to the target support, establishing a robustness of support property that explains why guidance consistently produces high-quality samples.

entry.title: Pretraining Induces a Reusable Spectral Basis for Downstream Task Adaptation

author.name: Junjie Yu, Yue Wang, Zihan Deng, Yan Zhu, Wenxiao Ma, Quanying Liu

entry.summary: Shows that leading singular vectors of pretrained weight matrices remain highly stable under finetuning and are shared across unrelated tasks, revealing that pretraining establishes a reusable spectral basis that captures task-relevant structure requiring no adjustment.

entry.title: MedAction: Towards Active Multi-turn Clinical Diagnostic LLMs

author.name: Hsin-Ling Hsu, Zizheng Wang, Donghua Zhang, Nai-Chia Chen, Jerry Wang, Jun-En Ding, Chia-Hsuan Hsu, Guoan Wang, Feng Liu, Fang-Ming Hung, Chenwei Wu, Liyue Shen

entry.summary: MedAction addresses active multi-turn clinical diagnosis in LLMs, identifying three failure modes (ungrounded test ordering, unreliable diagnostic update, degraded coherence) and proposing tree-structured distillation to train models for reasoning under evolving partial evidence.

entry.title: SparseRL-Sync: Lossless Weight Synchronization with ~100x Less Communication

author.name: Lucas Hu, Ranchi Zhao, Isaac Zhu, Zach Zhang, Hscos Zhang, Hugh Yin, Jason Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces SparseRL-Sync, exploiting the observation that 99%+ of weight parameters don't change between RL training steps. Achieves ~100x communication reduction for weight synchronization in distributed RL through sparse delta transmission.

entry.title: Tools as Continuous Flow for Evolving Agentic Reasoning

author.name: Tairan Huang, Siyu Shang, Qiang Chen, Xiu Su, Yi Chen

entry.summary: Proposes FlowAgent, which reconceptualizes tool chaining as continuous trajectory generation in semantic space using conditional flow matching. Includes the first plan-level closed-loop benchmark for agentic reasoning in dynamic environments.

entry.title: Gradient-Based LoRA Rank Allocation Under GRPO: An Empirical Study

author.name: Yash Ganpat Sawant

entry.summary: Shows that gradient-based adaptive LoRA rank allocation, which works well under SFT, fails under GRPO reinforcement learning. The gradient landscape under GRPO is much flatter (2.17x vs >10x ratio), making all layers similarly important.

entry.title: Escaping the Diversity Trap in Robotic Manipulation via Anchor-Centric Adaptation

author.name: Yanzhe Chen, Kevin Yuchen Ma, Qi Lv, Yiqi Lin, Zechen Bai, Chen Gao, Mike Zheng Shou

entry.summary: Identifies a 'diversity trap' in robot demonstration collection: maximizing coverage with single-shot demonstrations can be counterproductive due to estimation noise. Proposes Anchor-Centric Adaptation (ACA) with theoretical analysis of the coverage-density trade-off.

entry.title: Rubric-based On-policy Distillation

author.name: Junfeng Fang, Zhepei Hong, Mao Zheng, Mingyang Song, Gengsheng Li, Houcheng Jiang, Dan Zhang, Haiyun Guo, Xiang Wang, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Proposes ROPD, using structured semantic rubrics as a scalable alternative to teacher logits for on-policy distillation, enabling black-box-compatible knowledge distillation. Achieves up to 10x sample efficiency gains over logit-based methods.

entry.title: GPO-V: Jailbreak Diffusion Vision Language Model by Global Probability Optimization

author.name: Yu Pan, Andi Zhang, Yi Wang, Sibei Yang, Wenjie Wang

entry.summary: Discovers jailbreak vulnerabilities in Diffusion Vision-Language Models (dVLMs) through Global Probability Optimization (GPO-V). Identifies novel refusal patterns (Immediate and Progressive Refusal) and exploits the progressive refinement process as a latent attack surface.

entry.title: Sparse Autoencoders as Plug-and-Play Firewalls for Adversarial Attack Detection in VLMs

author.name: Hao Wang, Yiqun Sun, Pengfei Wei, Lawrence B. Hsieh, Daisuke Kawahara

entry.summary: Proposes SAEgis, using sparse autoencoders as plug-and-play adversarial attack detectors for VLMs. Shows that SAE sparse latent features naturally capture attack-relevant signals after standard reconstruction training.

entry.title: Approximation Error Upper and Lower Bounds for H\"{o}lder Class with Transformers

author.name: Xin He, Yuling Jiao, Xiliang Lu, Jerry Zhijian Yang

entry.summary: Establishes tight approximation error bounds (upper and lower) for Transformer networks approximating Hölder-class functions. Shows O(ε^{-d₀/α}) blocks suffice for the upper bound and Ω(ε^{-d₀/(4α)}) blocks are necessary, providing the first rigorous lower bounds for Transformers via VC-dimension arguments.

entry.title: SEIF: Self-Evolving Reinforcement Learning for Instruction Following

author.name: Qingyu Ren, Qianyu He, Jiajie Zhu, Xingzhou Chen, Jingwen Chang, Zeye Sun, Han Xia, Fei Yu, Jiaqing Liang, Yanghua Xiao

entry.summary: SEIF proposes a self-evolving reinforcement learning framework for instruction following where instruction difficulty and model capability co-evolve in a closed loop. The system uses four roles (Instructor, Executor, Evaluator, Evolver) to progressively generate harder instructions as the model improves.

entry.title: HBEE: Human Behavioral Entropy Engine -- Pre-Registered Multi-Agent LLM Simulation of Peer-Suspicion-Based Detection Inversion

author.name: Vickson Ferrel

entry.summary: Tests insider threat detection against LLM-driven adaptive adversaries in a multi-agent simulation, finding a 'detection inversion' where adaptive moles become less suspicious than innocent agents. Pre-registered study with surprising negative result for defenders.

entry.title: How Far Is Document Parsing from Solved? PureDocBench: A Source-TraceableBenchmark across Clean, Degraded, and Real-World Settings

author.name: Zhiheng Li, Zongyang Ma, Jiaxian Chen, Jianing Zhang, Zhaolong Su, Yutong Zhang, Zhiyin Yu, Ruiqi Liu, Xiaolei Lv, Bo Li, Jun Gao, Ziqi Zhang, Chunfeng Yuan, Bing Li, Weiming Hu

entry.summary: PureDocBench is a programmatically generated document parsing benchmark that addresses contamination and annotation quality issues in OmniDocBench (finding 12% error rate). Covers 10 domains, 66 subcategories across clean/degraded/real-degraded versions with verifiable annotations from source HTML/CSS.

entry.title: ExpThink: Experience-Guided Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Chain-of-Thought Compression

author.name: Tingcheng Bian, Yuzhe Zhang, Jing Jin, Jinchang Luo, MingQuan Cheng, Haiwei Wang, Wenyuan Jiang, Miaohui Wang

entry.summary: ExpThink proposes experience-guided RL for adaptive CoT compression that tracks shortest correct solutions per problem and applies tiered rewards, with automatic threshold tightening as model improves and problem-level difficulty awareness.

entry.title: Tessellations of Semi-Discrete Flow Matching

author.name: Emile Pierret, Johannes Hertrich, Samuel Hurault, Julie Delon

entry.summary: Studies Flow Matching in the semi-discrete setting (Gaussian source to discrete target) where exact velocity fields are available in closed form. Proves terminal assignment regions are open, simply connected, and under additional assumptions homeomorphic to the unit ball.

entry.title: ProteinJEPA: Latent prediction complements protein language models

author.name: Dan Ofer, Dafna Shahaf, Michal Linial

entry.summary: ProteinJEPA shows that masked-position latent prediction (combining MLM with JEPA at masked positions only) complements standard masked language modeling for protein sequence encoders, winning more downstream tasks than MLM-only under matched compute budgets.

entry.title: Tracing the Arrow of Time: Diagnosing Temporal Information Flow in Video-LLMs

author.name: Peitao Han and Fei Cheng and Lis K. Pereira and Qianying Liu and Shigeru Kitazawa

entry.summary: Traces temporal information flow through Video-LLM architectures, finding that video-centric encoders capture strong temporal signals but these are lost in the projector/LLM pipeline. Demonstrates that temporal information bottleneck lies in the architecture beyond the vision encoder.

entry.title: MemCompiler: Compile, Don't Inject -- State-Conditioned Memory for Embodied Agents

author.name: Xin Ding, Xinrui Wang, Yifan Yang, Hao Wu, Shiqi Jiang, Qianxi Zhang, Liang Mi, Hanxin Zhu, Kun Li, Yunxin Liu, Zhibo Chen, Ting Cao

entry.summary: MemCompiler reframes memory for embodied agents from static injection to dynamic state-conditioned compilation, where a Memory Compiler reads the agent's execution state and compiles only relevant memory into executable guidance through text and latent channels.

entry.title: The Endogeneity of Miscalibration: Impossibility and Escape in Scored Reporting

author.name: Lauri Lov\'en and Sasu Tarkoma

entry.summary: Proves an endogeneity impossibility: a principal's optimal AI oversight using strictly proper scoring rules necessarily introduces non-affine approval functions that make truthful reporting suboptimal, whenever agents have non-accuracy incentives.

entry.title: Future Validity is the Missing Statistic: From Impossibility to $\Phi$-Estimation for Grammar-Faithful Speculative Decoding

author.name: Wenhua Nie, Zijie Meng, Kun Zou, Zheng Lin, Ziwei Li, Haoran Zheng, Jyh-Shing Roger Jang and Hao Zhang

entry.summary: Proves that speculative decoding with local grammar masks samples from locally projected rather than grammar-conditional distributions, identifies the future-validity function as the missing correction, and proposes practical estimators.

entry.title: Curated Synthetic Data Doesn't Have to Collapse: A Theoretical Study of Generative Retraining with Pluralistic Preferences

author.name: Ali Falahati, Mohammad Mohammadi Amiri, Kate Larson, Lukasz Golab

entry.summary: Shows that model collapse from recursive retraining on curated synthetic data can be mitigated through curation based on multiple reward functions (pluralistic preferences), proving convergence to stable diverse distributions.

entry.title: TextLDM: Language Modeling with Continuous Latent Diffusion

author.name: Jiaxiu Jiang, Jingjing Ren, Wenbo Li, Bo Wang, Haoze Sun, Yijun Yang, Jianhui Liu, Yanbing Zhang, Shenghe Zheng, Yuan Zhang, Haoyang Huang, Nan Duan, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: TextLDM transfers the visual latent diffusion recipe (DiT + flow matching + VAE) to text generation with minimal architecture changes, using representation alignment with frozen LMs for effective latent spaces.

entry.title: POETS: Uncertainty-Aware LLM Optimization via Compute-Efficient Policy Ensembles

author.name: Nicolas Menet, Andreas Krause, Abbas Rahimi

entry.summary: Introduces POETS, a framework bridging uncertainty quantification and policy optimization for LLMs using policy ensembles for Thompson Sampling. Bypasses the complex process of training uncertainty-aware reward models by directly training policy ensembles to capture epistemic uncertainty.

entry.title: Spectral Surgery: Class-Targeted Post-Hoc Rebalancing via Hessian Spike Perturbation

author.name: Hugo Vigna, Samuel Bontemps

entry.summary: Proposes Spectral Surgery, a post-hoc method that perturbs model weights along Hessian spike eigenvectors to rebalance per-class accuracy without retraining. First to operationally exploit the spike structure of the Hessian spectrum for improving classification.

entry.title: Measuring and Mitigating the Distributional Gap Between Real and Simulated User Behaviors

author.name: Shuhaib Mehri, Philippe Laban, Sumuk Shashidhar, Marwa Abdulhai, Sergey Levine, Michel Galley, Dilek Hakkani-T\"ur

entry.summary: Introduces a method to measure the distributional gap between real and simulated user behaviors in AI conversations, evaluating 24 LLM-based user simulators. Provides first systematic evaluation showing current simulators poorly capture real user diversity.

entry.title: What Matters for Diffusion-Friendly Latent Manifold? Prior-Aligned Autoencoders for Latent Diffusion

author.name: Zhengrong Yue, Taihang Hu, Mengting Chen, Haiyu Zhang, Zihao Pan, Tao Liu, Zikang Wang, Jinsong Lan, Xiaoyong Zhu, Bo Zheng, Yali Wang

entry.summary: Studies what makes latent spaces 'diffusion-friendly' from the perspective of manifold organization, identifying three key properties: coherent spatial structure, local continuity, and global semantics. Proposes Prior-Aligned Autoencoders (PAAE) incorporating these insights.

entry.title: MedVIGIL: Evaluating Trustworthy Medical VLMs Under Broken Visual Evidence

author.name: Hanqi Jiang, Junhao Chen, Yi Pan, Lifeng Chen, Weihang You, Haozhen Gong, Ruiyu Yan, Jinglei Lv, Lin Zhao, Hui Ren, Quanzheng Li, Tianming Liu, Xiang Li

entry.summary: Introduces MedVIGIL, a 300-case evaluation suite for medical VLMs testing trustworthiness under broken visual evidence (false premises, perturbations, ROI corruption). Fully supervised by board-certified radiologists with clinical risk tiers.

entry.title: TAVIS: A Benchmark for Egocentric Active Vision and Anticipatory Gaze in Imitation Learning

author.name: Giacomo Spigler

entry.summary: TAVIS provides the first shared benchmark for active-vision imitation learning on humanoid robots, with tasks testing global search (pan/tilt) and local occlusion handling (wrist cameras) on GR1T2 and Reachy2 embodiments in IsaacLab.

entry.title: DVD: Discrete Voxel Diffusion for 3D Generation and Editing

author.name: Zhengrui Xiang, Jiaqi Wu, Fupeng Sun, Heliang Zheng, Yingzhen Li

entry.summary: DVD introduces discrete diffusion for sparse voxel generation in 3D pipelines, treating voxel occupancy as a native discrete variable to avoid continuous-to-discrete thresholding, with built-in uncertainty estimation for identifying ambiguous regions.

entry.title: SphereVAD: Training-Free Video Anomaly Detection via Geodesic Inference on the Unit Hypersphere

author.name: Chao Huang, Penfei Wei, Wei Wang, Jie Wen, Zhihua Wang, Li Shen, Wenqi Ren, Xiaochun Cao

entry.summary: SphereVAD proposes a training-free, zero-shot video anomaly detection framework using intermediate-layer features of multimodal LLMs with von Mises-Fisher likelihood-ratio geodesic inference on the unit hypersphere.

entry.title: Semiparametric Efficient Test for Interpretable Distributional Treatment Effects

author.name: Houssam Zenati and Arthur Gretton

entry.summary: DR-ME is the first semiparametrically efficient test for interpretable distributional treatment effects, evaluating kernel witnesses at learned outcome locations to return causal-discrepancy coordinates rather than just global rejection decisions.

entry.title: Alignment as Equilibrium Design

author.name: Elad Hazan

entry.summary: Frames AI alignment through the lens of mechanism design and economics, drawing on Gary Becker's 'rational offender' model. Argues that rather than instilling values, alignment should design incentive structures (equilibria) that make misalignment costly, analogous to how legal systems align human behavior.

entry.title: Beyond Confidence: Rethinking Self-Assessments for Performance Prediction in LLMs

author.name: Sree Bhattacharyya, Samarth Khanna, Leona Chen, Lucas Craig, Tharun Dilliraj, James Z. Wang

entry.summary: Drawing on cognitive appraisal theory from psychology, proposes multidimensional self-assessment for LLMs beyond simple confidence. Finds that competence-related appraisal dimensions outperform confidence for predicting model failure across 12 LLMs and 38 tasks.

entry.title: The Limits of AI-Driven Allocation: Optimal Screening under Aleatoric Uncertainty

author.name: Santiago Cortes-Gomez, Mateo Dulce Rubio, Carlos Patino, Bryan Wilder

entry.summary: Studies how algorithmic targeting based on ML risk scores should be optimally combined with traditional screening procedures, showing that aleatoric uncertainty creates irreducible misallocation that screening can help address.

entry.title: EnvSimBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating and Improving LLM-Based Environment Simulation

author.name: Yi Liu, TingFeng Hui, Wei Zhang, Li Sun, Ningxin Su, Jian Wang, Sen Su

entry.summary: EnvSimBench provides the first formal benchmark for evaluating LLMs as environment simulators for agent training, identifying failures like hallucinations, logical inconsistencies, and silent state drift that corrupt reward signals.

entry.title: ReasonEdit: Towards Interpretable Image Editing Evaluation via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Honghua Chen, Zitong Xu, Huiyu Duan, Xinyun Zhang, Xiongkuo Min, Guangtao Zhai

entry.summary: ReasonEdit introduces the first dataset combining 22K edited images with 113K Chain-of-Thought evaluation samples and 1.3M human judgments, plus a reinforcement learning method (REALM) to train interpretable image editing evaluators that provide reasoned explanations.

entry.title: Toward Privileged Foundation Models:LUPI for Accelerated and Improved Learning

author.name: Xueying Ding, Leman Akoglu

entry.summary: Introduces PIQL, the first framework integrating privileged information (available only during training) to accelerate learning and improve generalization in tabular foundation models. Constructs dataset-level statistics and data-generating program encodings as privileged information.

entry.title: Bayesian Sensitivity of Causal Inference Estimators under Evidence-Based Priors

author.name: Nikita Dhawan, Daniel Shen, Leonardo Cotta, Chris J. Maddison

entry.summary: Generalizes the s-value framework for causal inference sensitivity analysis to three common assumptions, arguing that worst-case sensitivity analysis can be uninformative and proposing Bayesian evidence-based priors for more realistic assessment.

entry.title: Proxy3D: Efficient 3D Representations for Vision-Language Models via Semantic Clustering and Alignment

author.name: Jerry Jiang, Haowen Sun, Denis Gudovskiy, Yohei Nakata, Tomoyuki Okuno, Kurt Keutzer, Wenzhao Zheng

entry.summary: Proxy3D proposes compact 3D proxy representations for vision-language models by performing semantic-aware clustering on encoded scene features from video frames, achieving spatial consistency without explicit 3D geometric reconstruction.

entry.title: Causal Unsupervised Semantic Segmentation

author.name: Junho Kim, Byung-Kwan Lee, Yong Man Ro

entry.summary: Introduces CAUSE, a framework for unsupervised semantic segmentation that leverages causal inference (frontdoor adjustment) to determine appropriate clustering granularity without annotations. Uses a concept clusterbook as a mediator between features and predictions.

entry.title: Breaking the Illusion: When Positive Meets Negative in Multimodal Decoding

author.name: Yubo Jiang, Yitong An, Xin Yang, Abudukelimu Wuerkaixi, Xuxin Cheng, Fengying Xie, Zhiguo Jiang, Cao Liu, Ke Zeng, and Haopeng Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces Positive-and-Negative Decoding (PND), a training-free inference framework that reduces object hallucination in VLMs by amplifying visual evidence and penalizing language-prior-dominant generation through dual-path contrast during decoding.

entry.title: On Training in Imagination

author.name: Nadav Timor, Ravid Shwartz-Ziv, Micah Goldblum, Yann LeCun, David Harel

entry.summary: Studies how errors in learned dynamics and reward models affect policy optimization in model-based RL. Derives optimal sample allocation between dynamics and reward samples, and identifies lower Lipschitz constants as a desirable representation property.

entry.title: Beyond Factor Aggregation: Gauge-Aware Low-Rank Server Representations for Federated LoRA

author.name: Jinqian Chen, Chang Liu, and Jihua Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes GLoRA, a gauge-aware server representation for federated LoRA that addresses the gauge-equivalence problem where the same update has infinitely many factorizations, causing semantic mismatch in factor-level aggregation.

entry.title: VITA-QinYu: Expressive Spoken Language Model for Role-Playing and Singing

author.name: Jiacheng Xu, Heting Gao, Liufei Xie, Zhenchuan Yang, Lijiang Li, Yiting Chen, Bin Zhang, Meng Chen, Chaoyu Fu, Weifeng Zhao, Wenjiang Zhou

entry.summary: Presents VITA-QinYu, the first end-to-end spoken language model supporting natural conversation, role-playing, and singing generation. Uses hybrid speech-text paradigm with multi-codebook audio tokens and 15.8K hours of synthesized training data.

entry.title: When Does Critique Improve AI-Assisted Theoretical Physics? SCALAR: Structured Critic--Actor Loop for Agentic Reasoning

author.name: Vasilis Niarchos, Constantinos Papageorgakis, Alexander G. Stapleton, Sokratis Trifinopoulos

entry.summary: Introduces SCALAR, an Actor-Critic-Judge pipeline for AI-assisted theoretical physics reasoning. Studies how multi-turn dialogue improves over single-shot attempts on QFT and string theory problems, varying actor persona, critic strategy, and model family.

entry.title: From Model to Data (M2D): Shifting Complexity from GNNs to Graphs for Transparent Graph Learning

author.name: Debolina Halder Lina and Arlei Silva

entry.summary: Introduces Model-to-Data distillation that transfers GNN model complexity into enriched graph features, enabling simple models to match complex ones. Provides architectural transparency by materializing model behavior in data space.

entry.title: When Descent Is Too Stable: Event-Triggered Hamiltonian Learning to Optimize

author.name: Yi Wang and Chandrajit Bajaj

entry.summary: Introduces SHAPE, a port-Hamiltonian optimizer that treats nonconvex optimization as a control problem, deciding when to descend, exploit, or escape basins. Uses event-triggered dynamics to avoid over-refining uninformative local minima.

entry.title: AdpSplit: Error-Driven Adaptive Splitting for Faster Geometry Discovery in 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Yongjae Lee, Jingxing Li, Abhay Kumar Yadav, Rama Chellappa, and Deliang Fan

entry.summary: Introduces AdpSplit, an error-driven adaptive split operator for 3D Gaussian Splatting that determines child count from pixel-error statistics. Reduces training time while preserving rendering quality.

entry.title: Towards Fairness under Label Bias in Image Segmentation: Impact, Measurement and Mitigation

author.name: Aditya Parikh, Stella Frank, Sneha Das, Aasa Feragen
