entry.summary: Proposes Cubit, a next-generation architecture replacing the attention mechanism with Kernel Ridge Regression (KRR), reinterpreting standard attention as Nadaraya-Watson regression. This offers a theoretically motivated alternative to the core token-mixing mechanism in Transformers.

entry.title: Why Global LLM Leaderboards Are Misleading: Small Portfolios for Heterogeneous Supervised ML

author.name: Jai Moondra, Ayela Chughtai, Bhargavi Lanka, Swati Gupta

entry.summary: Analyzes ~89K comparisons from Arena leaderboard across 116 languages and 52 LLMs, showing that global Bradley-Terry rankings are misleading due to structured heterogeneity across language, task, and time.

entry.title: ViTok-v2: Scaling Native Resolution Auto-Encoders to 5 Billion Parameters

author.name: Philippe Hansen-Estruch, Jiahui Chen, Vivek Ramanujan, Orr Zohar, Yan Ping, Animesh Sinha, Markos Georgopoulos, Edgar Schoenfeld, Ji Hou, Felix Juefei-Xu, Sriram Vishwanath, Ali Thabet

entry.summary: Introduces ViTok-v2, scaling Vision Transformer autoencoders to 5 billion parameters with native resolution support via NaFlex, achieving improved reconstruction without adversarial losses for stable scaling.

entry.title: Irminsul: MLA-Native Position-Independent Caching for Agentic LLM Serving

author.name: Bole Ma, Jan Eitzinger, Harald K\"ostler

entry.summary: Presents Irminsul, a position-independent caching system designed for Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA) architectures used in DeepSeek-V2/V3/R1, Kimi-K2, GLM-5, and Mistral Large 3. Exploits MLA's factored KV structure to enable efficient content-addressed caching for agentic LLM workloads.

entry.title: Measuring Evaluation-Context Divergence in Open-Weight LLMs: A Paired-Prompt Protocol with Pilot Evidence of Alignment-Pipeline-Specific Heterogeneity

author.name: Florian A. D. Burnat, Brittany I. Davidson

entry.summary: Defines 'evaluation-context divergence' - behavioral changes in LLMs when they detect they're being evaluated vs. deployed - and finds statistically significant divergence in instruction-tuned models but not base models.

entry.title: ReaComp: Compiling LLM Reasoning into Symbolic Solvers for Efficient Program Synthesis

author.name: Atharva Naik, Yash Mathur, Prakam, Carolyn Rose, David Mortensen

entry.summary: ReaComp compiles LLM reasoning traces into reusable symbolic program synthesizers that require no LLM calls at test time, achieving 91.3% accuracy on benchmarks while reducing token usage by 78% compared to LLM-based approaches.

entry.title: One Turn Too Late: Response-Aware Defense Against Hidden Malicious Intent in Multi-Turn Dialogue

author.name: Xinjie Shen, Rongzhe Wei, Peizhi Niu, Haoyu Wang, Ruihan Wu, Eli Chien, Bo Li, Pin-Yu Chen, Pan Li

entry.summary: Addresses hidden malicious intent distributed across multiple benign-looking turns in multi-turn dialogue, proposing a defense that detects the earliest turn at which delivering a response would enable harmful action.

entry.title: Efficient Pre-Training with Token Superposition

author.name: Bowen Peng, Th\'eo Gigant, Jeffrey Quesnelle

entry.summary: Proposes Token Superposition Training (TST), combining contiguous tokens into bags with multi-hot cross-entropy during a superposition phase, significantly improving data throughput per FLOPs during LLM pre-training without architecture changes.

entry.title: EMO: Pretraining Mixture of Experts for Emergent Modularity

author.name: Ryan Wang, Akshita Bhagia, Sewon Min

entry.summary: Introduces EMO, an MoE model designed for emergent modularity where expert subsets can be independently deployed for specific domains without severe performance degradation, unlike standard MoEs.

entry.title: Belief Memory: Agent Memory Under Partial Observability

author.name: Junfeng Liao, Qizhou Wang, Jianing Zhu, Bo Du, Rui Yan, Xiuying Chen

entry.summary: Proposes BeliefMem, a memory system for LLM agents that retains multiple candidate conclusions with probabilities rather than committing to single deterministic observations. This addresses self-reinforcing errors in agent memory under partial observability by maintaining uncertainty across stored beliefs.

entry.title: WavCube: Unifying Speech Representation for Understanding and Generation via Semantic-Acoustic Joint Modeling

author.name: Guanrou Yang, Tian Tan, Qian Chen, Zhikang Niu, Yakun Song, Ziyang Ma, Yushen Chen, Zeyu Xie, Tianrui Wang, Yifan Yang, Wenxi Chen, Qi Chen, Wenrui Liu, Shan Yang, Xie Chen

entry.summary: Presents WavCube, a compact continuous speech latent derived from SSL encoders that unifies speech understanding, reconstruction, and generation. Uses a two-stage training scheme with a semantic bottleneck to filter redundancy from SSL features.

entry.title: Steering Visual Generation in Unified Multimodal Models with Understanding Supervision

author.name: Zeyu Liu, Zanlin Ni, Yang Yue, Cheng Da, Huan Yang, Di Zhang, Kun Gai, Gao Huang

entry.summary: Proposes Understanding-Oriented Post-Training (UNO) to restore synergy between understanding and generation in unified multimodal models. Uses understanding tasks (captioning, visual reasoning) as supervisory signals to steer generative representations.

entry.title: AI #167: The Prior Restraint Era Begins

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's comprehensive AI news roundup covering the White House beginning prior restraint on AI model releases (vetoing Mythos access expansion), Anthropic's growth and compute deals including SpaceX's Colossus 1, Musk vs. OpenAI trial testimony, and regulatory developments likened to an FDA model.

entry.title: Retrieval from Within: An Intrinsic Capability of Attention-Based Models

author.name: Elad Hoffer, Yochai Blau, Ron Banner, Daniel Soudry, Boris Ginsburg

entry.summary: Introduces INTRA, a framework where decoder attention queries score and retrieve from pre-encoded evidence chunks stored in the model's own internal representations, unifying retrieval and generation without external retrievers.

entry.title: Agent Island: A Saturation- and Contamination-Resistant Benchmark from Multiagent Games

author.name: Connacher Murphy

entry.summary: Introduces Agent Island, a multiplayer simulation benchmark where LLM agents compete in games of cooperation, conflict, and persuasion. Designed to resist saturation and contamination, uses Bayesian Plackett-Luce ranking. Reports GPT-5.5 dominating in 999 games across 49 models.

entry.title: Uno-Orchestra: Parsimonious Agent Routing via Selective Delegation

author.name: Zhiqing Cui, Haotong Xie, Jiahao Yuan, Cheng Yang, Hanqing Wang, Yuxin Wu, Yifan Wu, Siru Zhong, Tao Yu, Yifu Guo, Siyu Zhang, Xinlei Yu, Qibing Ren, Usman Naseem

entry.summary: Introduces Uno-Orchestra, a unified orchestration policy for LLM multi-agent systems that jointly learns task decomposition, worker dispatch, and budget allocation from RL trajectories. Achieves 77.0% macro pass@1 across 13 benchmarks, 16% above strongest baseline.

entry.title: Experiment-as-Code Labs: A Declarative Stack for AI-Driven Scientific Discovery

author.name: Zhenning Yang, Yuhan Chen, Patrick Tser Jern Kon, Tongyuan Miao, Hongyi Lin, Venkat Viswanathan, Danai Koutra, Ang Chen

entry.summary: Proposes 'Experiment-as-Code Labs,' a declarative programming stack to bridge AI agents with automated laboratory equipment for scientific discovery. Aims to enable AI agents to control and explore in real-world labs, not just digital environments.

entry.title: Automatically Finding and Validating Unexpected Side-Effects of Interventions on Language Models

author.name: Quintin Pope, Ajay Hayagreeve Balaji, Jacques Thibodeau, Xiaoli Fern

entry.summary: Presents an automated pipeline for auditing behavioral impacts of interventions on LLMs by comparing generations across aligned prompts and producing statistically validated natural-language hypotheses about behavioral differences.

entry.title: Scaling Pretrained Representations Enables Label-Free Out-of-Distribution Detection Without Fine-Tuning

author.name: Brett Barkley, Preston Culbertson, David Fridovich-Keil

entry.summary: Demonstrates that frozen pretrained representations already encode sufficient geometric structure for accurate label-free out-of-distribution detection, without requiring class-conditional modeling or fine-tuning.

entry.title: RVPO: Risk-Sensitive Alignment via Variance Regularization

author.name: Ivan Montero, Tomasz Jurczyk, Bhuwan Dhingra

entry.summary: Proposes RVPO, a risk-sensitive RLHF framework that penalizes inter-reward variance during advantage aggregation, preventing high-magnitude success in one objective from masking critical failures in others.

entry.title: Mean Mode Screaming: Mean--Variance Split Residuals for 1000-Layer Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Pengqi Lu

entry.summary: Identifies 'Mean Mode Screaming' (MMS) as a structural vulnerability in very deep (1000-layer) Diffusion Transformers, where mean-dominated collapse homogenizes token representations. Proposes mean-variance split residual connections to fix this.

entry.title: Crafting Reversible SFT Behaviors in Large Language Models

author.name: Yuping Lin, Pengfei He, Yue Xing, Yingqian Cui, Jiayuan Ding, Subhabrata Mukherjee, Hui Liu, Zhen Xiang

entry.summary: Proposes methods to deliberately compress SFT-induced behaviors into sparse, mechanistically necessary subnetworks ('carriers') that can be selectively controlled at inference time without weight modification.

entry.title: Nonsense Helps: Prompt Space Perturbation Broadens Reasoning Exploration

author.name: Langlin Huang, Chengsong Huang, Jinyuan Li, Donghong Cai, Yuyi Yang, Jiaxin Huang

entry.summary: Proposes LoPE (Lorem Perturbation for Exploration), adding nonsense tokens to prompts during GRPO training to broaden reasoning exploration when all sampled rollouts fail, addressing the zero-advantage problem.

entry.title: Beyond Steering Vector: Flow-based Activation Steering for Inference-Time Intervention

author.name: Zehao Jin, Ruixuan Deng, Junran Wang, Xinjie Shen, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes FLAS (Flow-based Activation Steering), which learns a continuous velocity field to transport activations for controlling LLM behavior at inference time, addressing limitations of fixed single-step steering methods.

entry.title: Hallucination as an Anomaly: Dynamic Intervention via Probabilistic Circuits

author.name: Erik Nielsen, Elia Cunegatti, Marcus Vukojevic, Giovanni Iacca

entry.summary: Proposes PCNET, which uses Probabilistic Circuits to detect hallucinations as geometric anomalies on a factual manifold in the LLM residual stream, enabling selective correction only of hallucinated tokens rather than all tokens.

entry.title: Teaching Thinking Models to Reason with Tools: A Full-Pipeline Recipe for Tool-Integrated Reasoning

author.name: Qianjia Cheng, Yuchen Zhang, Zhilin Wang, Yuxin Zuo, Shunkai Zhang, Yuchen Fan, Yu Qiao, Bowen Zhou, Ning Ding, Yu Cheng, Yun Luo, Ganqu Cui

entry.summary: Presents a comprehensive recipe for teaching thinking models tool-integrated reasoning (TIR) without sacrificing no-tool reasoning ability, finding that tool-enabled evaluation can degrade performance even when models rarely make tool calls.

entry.title: Long Context Pre-Training with Lighthouse Attention

author.name: Bowen Peng, Subho Ghosh, Jeffrey Quesnelle

entry.summary: Proposes Lighthouse Attention, a training-only hierarchical attention algorithm that wraps around standard SDPA to enable subquadratic pre-training at extreme sequence lengths, with gradient-free selection that can be removed after training.

entry.title: Improving the Efficiency of Language Agent Teams with Adaptive Task Graphs

author.name: Elizabeth Mieczkowski, Alexander Ku, Tiwalayo Eisape, Dilip Arumugam, John Matters, Katherine M. Collins, Ilia Sucholutsky, Thomas L. Griffiths

entry.summary: Introduces LATTE, a framework for coordinating LLM agent teams using adaptive task graphs inspired by distributed systems. Balances structured coordination (reducing errors) with adaptability, allowing teams to collaboratively construct and maintain shared task graphs.

entry.title: MUSE: Resolving Manifold Misalignment in Visual Tokenization via Topological Orthogonality

author.name: Panqi Yang, Haodong Jing, Jiahao Chao, Tingyan Xiang, Li Lin, Yao Hu, Yang Luo, Yongqiang Ma

entry.summary: Proposes MUSE for visual tokenization that resolves the trade-off between pixel reconstruction and semantic abstraction by using topological orthogonality to decouple optimization gradients within Transformers.

entry.title: Parallel Prefix Verification for Speculative Generation

author.name: Yuncheng Yao, Yuxuan Xia, Shengjie Wang, Danyang Zhuo

entry.summary: Introduces PARSE, a speculative generation framework that accelerates LLM inference by parallelizing prefix verification at the semantic level rather than token level. Enables semantic-level verification without sequential checks, increasing acceptance granularity.

entry.title: How Does Thinking Mode Change LLM Moral Judgments? A Controlled Instant-vs-Thinking Comparison Across Five Frontier Models

author.name: Sai Sourabh Madur

entry.summary: Evaluates whether enabling reasoning mode changes moral judgments in 5 frontier LLMs (Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT 5.5, Gemini 3 Flash, DeepSeek V3.1, Qwen3.5 397B). Finds aggregate agreement is stable but reasoning narrows cross-model disagreement on disputed scenarios and reduces demographic bias.

entry.title: TSCG: Deterministic Tool-Schema Compilation for Agentic LLM Deployments

author.name: Furkan Sakizli

entry.summary: Introduces TSCG, a deterministic tool-schema compiler that converts JSON schemas to token-efficient structured text for small LLMs (4B-14B), dramatically improving tool-use success rates (Phi-4 14B from 0% to 84.4%) without fine-tuning.

entry.title: Coral: Cost-Efficient Multi-LLM Serving over Heterogeneous Cloud GPUs

author.name: Yixuan Mei, Zikun Li, Zixuan Chen, Shiqi Pan, Mengdi Wu, Xupeng Miao, Zhihao Jia, K. V. Rashmi

entry.summary: Introduces Coral, a system for cost-efficient multi-LLM serving across heterogeneous cloud GPUs. It jointly optimizes resource allocation and serving strategy for multiple model replicas, adapting to shifting throughput demands and resource availability through a two-stage decomposition.

entry.title: Towards Robust LLM Post-Training: Automatic Failure Management for Reinforcement Fine-Tuning

author.name: Lingzhe Zhang, Tong Jia, Yunpeng Zhai, Liancheng Fang, Kening Zheng, Hongyi Liu, Xiaosong Huang, Philip S. Yu, Ying Li

entry.summary: Addresses the fragility of reinforcement fine-tuning (RFT) for LLMs by developing automatic failure management at the training-process level. Provides systematic categorization of RFT failures and proposes automated detection and correction mechanisms.

entry.title: On the (In-)Security of the Shuffling Defense in the Transformer Secure Inference

author.name: Zhengyi Li, Yakai Wang, Kang Yang, Yu Yu, Jiaping Gui, Yu Feng, Ning Liu, Minyi Guo, Jingwen Leng

entry.summary: Demonstrates that the shuffling defense used in secure transformer inference is insecure, showing that adversaries can extract model weights from randomly permuted activations despite the defense.

entry.title: Misaligned by Reward: Socially Undesirable Preferences in LLMs

author.name: Gayane Ghazaryan, Esra D\"onmez

entry.summary: Extends reward model benchmarking to socially consequential domains (bias, safety, morality, ethical reasoning) by converting social evaluation datasets into pairwise preferences, revealing that reward models often prefer socially undesirable outputs.

entry.title: Local Intrinsic Dimension Unveils Hallucinations in Diffusion Models

author.name: Bartlomiej Sobieski, Matthew Tivnan, Dawid P{\l}udowski, Micha{\l} Jan W{\l}odarczyk, Pengfei Jin, Przemyslaw Biecek, Quanzheng Li

entry.summary: Proposes using local intrinsic dimension (LID) to detect structural hallucinations in diffusion models (e.g., extra fingers), showing these correspond to manifold instabilities and high-LID regions that can be identified and mitigated during generation.

entry.title: Superposition Is Not Necessary: A Mechanistic Interpretability Analysis of Transformer Representations for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Alper Y{\i}ld{\i}r{\i}m

entry.summary: Applies sparse autoencoders to probe PatchTST for time series forecasting, finding that transformers don't engage superposition for time series data - explaining why simple linear models remain competitive.

entry.title: Are Flat Minima an Illusion?

author.name: Michael Timothy Bennett

entry.summary: Argues that flat minima in neural networks are illusory since reparameterization can change loss landscape geometry without affecting predictions. Proposes 'weakness' (volume of compatible completions) as the true reparameterization-invariant driver of generalization.

entry.title: Rethinking Data Curation in LLM Training: Online Reweighting Offers Better Generalization than Offline Methods

author.name: Wanru Zhao, Yihong Chen, Yuzhi Tang, Wentao Ma, Shengchao Hu, Shell Xu Hu, Alex Iacob, Abhinav Mehrotra, Nicholas D. Lane

entry.summary: Proposes ADAPT, an online data reweighting method for LLM pretraining that dynamically adjusts sample importance during training, showing better generalization than offline data curation methods like selection and mixing.

entry.title: When Can Voting Help, Hurt, or Change Course? Exact Structure of Binary Test-Time Aggregation

author.name: Yi Liu

entry.summary: Shows that majority voting behavior under exchangeable repeated predictions is fundamentally more complex than classical fixed-competence theory suggests, with latent mixtures generating nonmonotone voting curves.

entry.title: MDN: Parallelizing Stepwise Momentum for Delta Linear Attention

author.name: Yulong Huang, Xiang Liu, Hongxiang Huang, Xiaopeng Lin, Zunchang Liu, Xiaowen Chu, Zeke Xie, Bojun Cheng

entry.summary: Develops a chunkwise parallel algorithm for linear attention with stepwise momentum by reordering update coefficients, improving upon plain SGD-based linear attention (Mamba2, GDN) while maintaining efficiency.

entry.title: Beyond Uniform Credit Assignment: Selective Eligibility Traces for RLVR

author.name: Chaoli Mou, Zhan Zhuang, Xinning Chen, Yu Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes Selective Eligibility Traces (S-trace) for RLVR that implements sparse credit assignment to distinguish critical reasoning steps, addressing the uniform credit assignment limitation of GRPO.

entry.title: Requests of a Feather Must Flock Together: Batch Size vs. Prefix Homogeneity in LLM Inference

author.name: Saksham Rathi, Preeti, Mythili Vutukuru

entry.summary: Shows that in prefix-sharing LLM workloads, smaller prefix-homogeneous batches can achieve higher decode throughput than larger heterogeneous batches due to better KV cache locality.

entry.title: Unifying Goal-Conditioned RL and Unsupervised Skill Learning via Control-Maximization

author.name: Alireza Modirshanechi, Benjamin Eysenbach, Peter Dayan, Eric Schulz

entry.summary: Unifies goal-conditioned RL and mutual information skill learning (MISL) as instances of control-maximization, providing theoretical explanation for why skills learned through MISL support goal-reaching. Includes credible authors (Eysenbach, Dayan, Schulz).

entry.title: Pro-KLShampoo: Projected KL-Shampoo with Whitening Recovered by Orthogonalization

author.name: Ruotong Sun, Ermin Wei

entry.summary: Proposes Pro-KLShampoo that unifies Kronecker-factored preconditioning (KL-Shampoo) with gradient orthogonalization (Muon), observing that Kronecker preconditioner eigenspectra have spike-and-flat structure amenable to low-rank projection.

entry.title: E = T*H/(O+B): A Dimensionless Control Parameter for Mixture-of-Experts Ecology

author.name: Qingjun Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces E = T*H/(O+B), a single dimensionless control parameter that predicts MoE expert collapse, showing E >= 0.5 guarantees zero dead experts across vision and language experiments, removing need for handcrafted balance losses.

entry.title: SoftSAE: Dynamic Top-K Selection for Adaptive Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Jakub St\k{e}pie\'n, Marcin Mazur, Jacek Tabor, Przemys{\l}aw Spurek

entry.summary: Introduces SoftSAE, sparse autoencoders with dynamic top-K selection that adapts sparsity per input based on data complexity, addressing the limitation of fixed-K in mechanistic interpretability of LLMs and ViTs.

entry.title: When and Why SignSGD Outperforms SGD: A Theoretical Study Based on $\ell_1$-norm Lower Bounds

author.name: Hongyi Tao, Dingzhi Yu, Lijun Zhang

entry.summary: Provides theoretical analysis of when SignSGD outperforms SGD by establishing l1-norm lower bounds under l∞-smoothness conditions, explaining the empirical success of sign-based optimizers like SignSGD and Muon in training large models.

entry.title: Optimizer-Model Consistency: Full Finetuning with the Same Optimizer as Pretraining Forgets Less

author.name: Yuxing Liu, Jianyu Wang, Tong Zhang

entry.summary: Shows that full fine-tuning LLMs with the same optimizer used in pretraining achieves better learning-forgetting tradeoffs than other optimizers or LoRA, terming this 'optimizer-model consistency'.

entry.title: CITE: Anytime-Valid Statistical Inference in LLM Self-Consistency

author.name: Hirofumi Ota, Naoto Iwase, Yuki Ichihara, Junpei Komiyama, Masaaki Imaizumi

entry.summary: Proposes CITE, an algorithm for anytime-valid statistical certification that a target answer is the unique mode of an LLM's response distribution during self-consistency sampling, with provable false certification control under arbitrary stopping rules.

entry.title: Quantum-enhanced Large Language Models on Quantum Hardware via Cayley Unitary Adapters

author.name: Borja Aizpurua, Sukhbinder Singh, Augustine Kshetrimayum, Saeed S. Jahromi, Roman Orus

entry.summary: Demonstrates quantum-enhanced LLM adaptation by running Cayley-parameterized unitary adapters on a 156-qubit IBM Quantum System Two processor, improving Llama 3.1 8B perplexity by 1.4% with only 6,000 additional parameters.

entry.title: TIDE: Every Layer Knows the Token Beneath the Context

author.name: Ajay Jaiswal, Lauren Hannah, Han-Byul Kim, Duc Hoang, Mehrdad Farajtabar, Minsik Cho

entry.summary: Proposes TIDE, which re-injects token identity information at every transformer layer via EmbeddingMemory, addressing the rare token problem and contextual collapse that arise from single-injection of token embeddings.

entry.title: UniSD: Towards a Unified Self-Distillation Framework for Large Language Models

author.name: Yiqiao Jin, Yiyang Wang, Lucheng Fu, Yijia Xiao, Yinyi Luo, Haoxin Liu, B. Aditya Prakash, Josiah Hester, Jindong Wang, Srijan Kumar

entry.summary: Proposes UniSD, a unified framework for self-distillation in LLMs that systematically studies and integrates mechanisms like multi-teacher agreement, EMA stabilization, and representation alignment without requiring external teacher models.

entry.title: XL-SafetyBench: A Country-Grounded Cross-Cultural Benchmark for LLM Safety and Cultural Sensitivity

author.name: Dasol Choi, Eugenia Kim, Jaewon Noh, Sang Seo, Eunmi Kim, Myunggyo Oh, Yunjin Park, Brigitta Jesica Kartono, Josef Pichlmeier, Helena Berndt, Sai Krishna Mendu, Glenn Johannes Tungka, \"Ozlem G\"ok\c{c}e, Suresh Gehlot, Katherine Pratt, Amanda Minnich, Haon Park

entry.summary: Introduces XL-SafetyBench with 5,500 test cases across 10 country-language pairs, distinguishing between universal jailbreak harms and culturally embedded sensitivities through native-speaker annotation.

entry.title: UniPrefill: Universal Long-Context Prefill Acceleration via Block-wise Dynamic Sparsification

author.name: Qihang Fan, Huaibo Huang, Zhiying Wu, Bingning Wang, Ran He

entry.summary: Proposes UniPrefill, a block-wise dynamic sparsification method for accelerating long-context prefill that works across different attention architectures (full, linear/full hybrids, sliding window/full hybrids), unlike existing sparse attention approaches.

entry.title: Continuous Latent Diffusion Language Model

author.name: Hongcan Guo, Qinyu Zhao, Yian Zhao, Shen Nie, Rui Zhu, Qiushan Guo, Feng Wang, Tao Yang, Hengshuang Zhao, Guoqiang Wei, Yan Zeng

entry.summary: Proposes Cola DLM, a hierarchical latent diffusion language model that decomposes text generation into latent-space semantic modeling with a block-causal DiT and conditional decoding, offering an alternative to autoregressive generation.

entry.title: The Granularity Axis: A Micro-to-Macro Latent Direction for Social Roles in Language Models

author.name: Chonghan Qin, Xiachong Feng, Ziyun Song, Xiaocheng Feng, Jing Xiong, Lingpeng Kong

entry.summary: Discovers that LLMs encode social role granularity (micro-level individual to macro-level institutional) as the dominant geometric axis in their representation space. In Qwen3-8B, this 'Granularity Axis' aligns with PC1 at cosine 0.972 and explains 52.6% of variance.

entry.title: LAMP: Localization Aware Multi-camera People Tracking in Metric 3D World

author.name: Nan Yang, Julian Straub, Fan Zhang, Richard Newcombe, Jakob Engel, Lingni Ma

entry.summary: Proposes LAMP for 3D human motion tracking from egocentric multi-camera headsets by disentangling observer and target motion. Converts 2D keypoints from all cameras into unified 3D representations using known device pose and calibration.

entry.title: CXR-ContraBench: Benchmarking Negated-Option Attraction in Medical VLMs

author.name: Zhengru Fang, Yanan Ma, Yu Guo, Senkang Hu, Yixian Zhang, Hangcheng Cao, Wenbo Ding, Yuguang Fang

entry.summary: Introduces CXR-ContraBench to study 'negated-option attraction' in medical VLMs where models select negated answers (e.g., 'No consolidation') despite visible evidence. Reveals a polarity reversal failure mode with clinical safety implications.

entry.title: On-Orbit Real-Time Wildfire Detection Under On-Board Constraints

author.name: Matthias R\"otzer, Veronika P\"ortge, Martin Ickerott, Jayendra Praveen Kumar Chorapalli, Dimitri Scheftelowitsch, Max Bereczky, Dmitry Rashkovetsky, Sai Manoj Appalla, Julia Gottfriedsen

entry.summary: Presents a deployed on-orbit wildfire detection system running on a nine-satellite constellation with NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX, operating under sub-megabyte model footprint and sub-150ms inference constraints for real-time fire alerts.

entry.title: Stabilizing LLM Supervised Fine-Tuning via Explicit Distributional Control

author.name: Xinyu Wang, Changzhi Sun, Yuanbin Wu, Xiaoling Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Anchored Learning, a framework to control distributional drift during LLM fine-tuning using a dynamically evolving moving anchor that interpolates between the current model and a frozen reference, transforming global fine-tuning into local trust-region steps.

entry.title: Anticipating Innovation Using Large Language Models

author.name: Enrico Maria Fenoaltea, Filippo Santoro, Giordano De Marzo, Segun Taofeek Aroyehun, Andrea Tacchella

entry.summary: Introduces TechToken, a transformer model treating patent technology codes as vocabulary tokens to predict future technological combinations, showing predictive signals are detectable decades in advance as collective language shifts.

entry.title: WARP: A Benchmark for Primal-Dual Warm-Starting of Interior-Point Solvers

author.name: Dhruv Suri, Helgi Hilmarsson, Shourya Bose

entry.summary: Demonstrates that previously reported ML warm-starting gains for interior-point solvers in AC Optimal Power Flow are artifacts of an inappropriate baseline (flat start vs. actual default midpoint). Shows primal-only warm-starts fail against the correct baseline.

entry.title: The Cost of Context: Mitigating Textual Bias in Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Hoin Jung, Xiaoqian Wang

entry.summary: Identifies and formalizes 'recorruption' in multimodal RAG where accurate retrieved context causes models to abandon correct predictions. Traces this to attentional collapse - visual blindness and positional bias.

entry.title: Teaching LLMs Program Semantics via Symbolic Execution Traces

author.name: Jonas Bayer, Stefan Zetzsche, Olivier Bouissou, Remi Delmas, Michael Tautschnig, Soonho Kong

entry.summary: Introduces an evaluation framework of 500 C verification tasks and shows that training on symbolic execution traces from the Soteria engine improves LLM violation detection by over 17% on Qwen3-8B.

entry.title: Log-Likelihood, Simpson's Paradox, and the Detection of Machine-Generated Text

author.name: Tom Kempton, Viktor Drobnyi, Maeve Madigan, Stuart Burrell

entry.summary: Demonstrates that naively averaging token-level log-likelihood scores for machine-generated text detection causes Simpson's paradox, destroying strong local signals. Proposes conditioning on hidden state regions to correct this.

entry.title: Milestone-Guided Policy Learning for Long-Horizon Language Agents

author.name: Zixuan Wang, Yuchen Yan, Hongxing Li, Teng Pan, Dingming Li, Ruiqing Zhang, Weiming Lu, Jun Xiao, Yueting Zhuang, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: Introduces BEACON, a milestone-guided policy learning framework for long-horizon language agents that partitions trajectories at milestone boundaries for better credit assignment and applies temporal reward shaping within segments.

entry.title: Don't Lose Focus: Activation Steering via Key-Orthogonal Projections

author.name: Haoyan Luo, Mateo Espinosa Zarlenga, Mateja Jamnik

entry.summary: Proposes SKOP (Steering via Key-Orthogonal Projections), an activation steering method that constrains harmful attention rerouting by preserving attention on focus tokens while allowing redistribution among less critical tokens.

entry.title: AgentTrust: Runtime Safety Evaluation and Interception for AI Agent Tool Use

author.name: Chenglin Yang

entry.summary: Presents AgentTrust, a runtime safety layer that intercepts agent tool calls before execution and returns structured verdicts (allow/warn/block/review). Combines shell deobfuscation, safety suggestion, and structured evaluation for real-time agent safety.

entry.title: Budgeted LoRA: Distillation as Structured Compute Allocation for Efficient Inference

author.name: Mohammed Sabry, Anya Belz

entry.summary: Proposes Budgeted LoRA, a distillation framework that treats model compression as structured compute allocation, introducing a global compute budget that redistributes capacity across layers rather than using a fixed student architecture. Aims to produce models efficient at both training and inference time.

entry.title: Sparse Tokens Suffice: Jailbreaking Audio Language Models via Token-Aware Gradient Optimization

author.name: Zheng Fang, Xiaosen Wang, Shenyi Zhang, Shaokang Wang, Zhijin Ge

entry.summary: Proposes TAGO, a sparse jailbreak attack on audio language models that exploits non-uniform gradient energy across audio tokens, optimizing perturbations only on high-gradient-energy token-aligned regions for more efficient attacks.

entry.title: Accelerating LMO-Based Optimization via Implicit Gradient Transport

author.name: Won-Jun Jang, Si-Hyeon Lee

entry.summary: Proposes LMO-IGT, a class of stochastic LMO-based optimization methods leveraging implicit gradient transport for variance reduction without additional gradient evaluations. Provides unified framework for methods like Lion and Muon.

entry.title: Revealing Modular Gradient Noise Imbalance in LLMs: Calibrating Adam via Signal-to-Noise Ratio

author.name: Ziqing Wen, Zhouyang Liu, Jiahuan Wang, Ping Luo, Li Shen, Dongsheng Li, Tao Sun

entry.summary: Reveals that different modules in LLMs have heterogeneous gradient noise levels and proposes SNR-calibrated Adam that provides module-level adaptivity, improving convergence without manual tuning.

entry.title: Towards Steering without Sacrifice: Principled Training of Steering Vectors for Prompt-only Interventions

author.name: Yuntai Bao, Qinfeng Li, Xinyan Yu, Xuhong Zhang, Ge Su, Wenqi Zhang, Liu Yan, Haiqin Weng, Jianwei Yin

entry.summary: Proposes principled training of steering vectors for LLMs with joint optimization of steering factors and directions, and introduces prompt-only SVs that avoid excessive intervention during generation.

entry.title: Layer Collapse in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Alexander Conzelmann, Albert Catalan-Tatjer, Shiwei Liu

entry.summary: Identifies 'layer collapse' in diffusion language models (LLaDA-8B): early layers show collapsed activation patterns with critical super-outliers whose removal causes degenerate outputs. Shows redundancy patterns are reversed compared to autoregressive models.

entry.title: Towards Reliable LLM Evaluation: Correcting the Winner's Curse in Adaptive Benchmarking

author.name: Yang Xu, Jiefu Zhang, Haixiang Sun, Zihan Zhou, Tianyu Cao, Vaneet Aggarwal

entry.summary: Proposes SIREN, a selection-aware reporting protocol that corrects for winner's curse bias in adaptive LLM benchmarking, providing valid statistical inference when benchmark items are reused during tuning.

entry.title: Logic-Regularized Verifier Elicits Reasoning from LLMs

author.name: Xinyu Wang, Changzhi Sun, Lian Cheng, Yuanbin Wu, Dell Zhang, Xiaoling Wang, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: Proposes LOVER, an unsupervised verifier regularized by logical rules (negation consistency, intra/inter-group consistency) that enhances LLM reasoning without requiring labeled training data.

entry.title: Beyond Negative Rollouts: Positive-Only Policy Optimization with Implicit Negative Gradients

author.name: Mingwei Xu, Hao Fang

entry.summary: Proposes Positive-Only Policy Optimization (POPO), which eliminates negative rollouts from GRPO-style training by deriving implicit negative gradients, arguing that penalizing sampled negatives provides poor signal under sparse binary rewards.

entry.title: Patch-Effect Graph Kernels for LLM Interpretability

author.name: Ruben Fernandez-Boullon, David N. Olivieri

entry.summary: Proposes representing activation-patching profiles as patch-effect graphs and applying graph kernels to analyze them, reframing mechanistic interpretability as a graph machine learning problem. Demonstrates on GPT-2 Small that graph kernels can quantify circuit similarities.

entry.title: TriRelVLA: Triadic Relational Structure for Generalizable Embodied Manipulation

author.name: Hanyu Zhou, Chuanhao Ma, Gim Hee Lee

entry.summary: Proposes TriRelVLA, a vision-language-action model that uses triadic relational structure (object-hand-task) for generalizable embodied manipulation. Addresses the limitation that implicit visual representations entangle appearance with action-relevant relations.

entry.title: When Context Hurts: The Crossover Effect of Knowledge Transfer on Multi-Agent Design Exploration

author.name: Saranyan Vigraham

entry.summary: Demonstrates a 'crossover effect' in multi-agent software design: the same context artifact can improve design exploration on some tasks (up to 20x) while degrading it on others (up to 46% reduction). Finds baseline exploration without context predicts direction with r=-0.82.

entry.title: LongSeeker: Elastic Context Orchestration for Long-Horizon Search Agents

author.name: Yijun Lu, Rui Ye, Yuwen Du, Jiajun Wang, Songhua Liu, Siheng Chen

entry.summary: Proposes LongSeeker with Context-ReAct, an elastic context orchestration paradigm for long-horizon search agents that provides five atomic operations (Skip, Compress, Rollback, Snippet, Delete) for adaptive context management during reasoning.

entry.title: Toward Human-AI Complementarity Across Diverse Tasks

author.name: Yuzheng Xu, Annya Dahmani, Matthew D. Blanchard, Niclas Dern, Edy Nastase, Francesca Bianco, Maja Pavlovic, Sukanya Krishna, Eric Modesitt, Miranda Anna Christ, Arth Singh, Gaia Molinaro, Sikata Bela Sengupta, Jaji Pamarthi, Arjun Menon, Rishub Jain

entry.summary: Investigates human-AI complementarity across diverse tasks (knowledge, factuality, reasoning, deception detection). Finds only modest gains from hybridization (+0.4pp over AI alone) with a small complementarity region (8.9%).

entry.title: Validity-Calibrated Reasoning Distillation

author.name: Khouloud Saadi, Di Wang

entry.summary: Proposes validity-calibrated reasoning distillation that treats distillation as local learning-signal allocation rather than path alignment. Instead of token-level imitation, compares student reasoning paths against validity criteria at each step.

entry.title: Layerwise LQR for Geometry-Aware Optimization of Deep Networks

author.name: Simon Dufort-Labb\'e, Pierre-Luc Bacon, Razvan Pascanu, Simon Lacoste-Julien, Aristide Baratin

entry.summary: Introduces Layerwise LQR (LLQR), framing deep network optimization as a Linear Quadratic Regulator problem. Shows exact equivalence between steepest-descent steps under various metrics and finite-horizon LQR, enabling geometry-aware optimization.

entry.title: Memory as a Markov Matrix: Sample Efficient Knowledge Expansion via Token-to-Dictionary Mapping

author.name: Kaustubh Pethkar, Ziyang Xiong, Zuofeng Shang, Yingcong Li

entry.summary: Proposes modeling LLM memory as a Markov transition matrix to enable sample-efficient knowledge injection without parameter updates. This approach avoids catastrophic forgetting by treating knowledge incorporation as modifying transition probabilities rather than updating weights.

entry.title: FLUID: Continuous-Time Hyperconnected Sparse Transformer for Sink-Free Learning

author.name: Waleed Razzaq, Yun-Bo Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes FLUID, a continuous-time Transformer that replaces standard attention with Liquid Attention Network (LAN), reformulating attention logits as solutions to linear ODEs modulated by input-dependent gates. Provides stability guarantees and addresses attention sink issues.

entry.title: CCL-D: A High-Precision Diagnostic System for Slow and Hang Anomalies in Large-Scale Model Training

author.name: Yida Gu, Fakang Wang, Jianhao Fu, Zhenhang Sun, Qianyu Zhang, Hairui Zhao, Xingchen Liu, Yang Tian, Wenjing Huang, Zedong Liu, Yifan Chen, Jinwu Yang, Yueyuan Zhou, Qian Zhao, Haoxu Li, Tao Wang, Feng Yu, Zhan Wang, Guangming Tan, Dingwen Tao

entry.summary: Introduces CCL-D, a diagnostic system for detecting and localizing slow/hang anomalies in collective communication libraries during large-scale distributed training. Combines real-time probes with intelligent decision analysis for fast root cause identification.

entry.title: RLearner-LLM: Balancing Logical Grounding and Fluency in Large Language Models via Hybrid Direct Preference Optimization

author.name: Qiming Bao, Juho Leinonen, Paul Denny, Michael J. Witbrock

entry.summary: Proposes Hybrid-DPO combining NLI signals with verifier LLM scores to address the verbosity bias in standard DPO that rewards fluency over logical correctness. Achieves improved logical alignment across multiple domains and architectures.

entry.title: Storage Is Not Memory: A Retrieval-Centered Architecture for Agent Recall

author.name: Joshua Adler, Guy Zehavi

entry.summary: Proposes True Memory, a six-layer retrieval-centered agent memory architecture that preserves events verbatim and operates as a single SQLite file. Achieves 93% accuracy on LoCoMo, competitive with state-of-the-art systems, using only CPU.

entry.title: Skill Neologisms: Towards Skill-based Continual Learning

author.name: Antonin Berthon, Nicolas Astorga, Mihaela van der Schaar

entry.summary: Explores 'skill neologisms' - soft tokens integrated into LLM vocabulary and optimized for specific skills - as a way to extend model capabilities without weight updates, avoiding catastrophic forgetting while enabling skill composition.

entry.title: SoK: Robustness in Large Language Models against Jailbreak Attacks

author.name: Feiyue Xu, Hongsheng Hu, Chaoxiang He, Sheng Hang, Hanqing Hu, Xiuming Liu, Yubo Zhao, Zhengyan Zhou, Bin Benjamin Zhu, Shi-Feng Sun, Dawu Gu, Shuo Wang

entry.summary: Presents a systematic taxonomy of jailbreak attacks and defenses for LLMs and introduces 'Security Cube', a multi-dimensional evaluation framework that goes beyond simple attack success rate metrics.

entry.title: On the Wasserstein Gradient Flow Interpretation of Drifting Models

author.name: Arthur Gretton, Li Kevin Wenliang, Alexandre Galashov, James Thornton, Valentin De Bortoli, Arnaud Doucet

entry.summary: Analyzes Generative Modeling via Drifting (GMD) through the lens of Wasserstein Gradient Flows, showing connections to KL divergence minimization with Parzen smoothing and characterizing fixed-point convergence. Authors include Arthur Gretton.

entry.title: The First Token Knows: Single-Decode Confidence for Hallucination Detection

author.name: Mina Gabriel

entry.summary: Shows that first-token confidence (normalized entropy of top-K logits at the first answer token) matches or exceeds semantic self-consistency for hallucination detection while requiring only a single greedy decode.

entry.title: Sparse Prefix Caching for Hybrid and Recurrent LLM Serving

author.name: Mikhail Shirokikh, Sergey Nikolenko

entry.summary: Proposes sparse prefix caching for hybrid/recurrent LLM serving that exploits the asymmetry of SSM layers (single stored state vs. full KV cache), formalized as an optimal checkpoint placement problem.

entry.title: MidSteer: Optimal Affine Framework for Steering Generative Models

author.name: Tatiana Gaintseva, Andrew Stepanov, Ziquan Liu, Martin Benning, Gregory Slabaugh, Jiankang Deng, Ismail Elezi

entry.summary: Formalizes the theory of concept steering in generative models, proving standard steering is a special case of LEACE (affine concept erasure) and proposing LEACE-Switch for optimal concept switching with theoretical guarantees.

entry.title: Internalizing Outcome Supervision into Process Supervision: A New Paradigm for Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning

author.name: Fei Ding, Yongkang Zhang, Runhao Liu, Yuhao Liao, Zijian Zeng, Sibo wang, Huiming Yang

entry.summary: Proposes a framework that internalizes outcome supervision into process supervision for RL reasoning, providing fine-grained learning signals for intermediate steps without external process reward models.

entry.title: Feature Starvation as Geometric Instability in Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Faris Chaudhry, Keisuke Yano, Anthea Monod

entry.summary: Argues that feature starvation in sparse autoencoders is a fundamental geometric pathology of overcomplete dictionaries rather than an empirical artifact, and introduces differential-geometric regularizers to address it.

entry.title: OpenG2G: A Simulation Platform for AI Datacenter-Grid Runtime Coordination

author.name: Jae-Won Chung, Zhirui Liang, Yanyong Mao, Jiasi Chen, Mosharaf Chowdhury, Vladimir Dvorkin

entry.summary: Introduces OpenG2G, a simulation platform for studying coordination between AI datacenters and the electricity grid. Addresses the challenge of large datacenter power demands causing grid reliability issues and interconnection delays.

entry.title: Energy Generative Modeling: A Lyapunov-based Energy Matching Perspective

author.name: Yixuan Wang, Wenqian Xue, Warren E. Dixon

entry.summary: Unifies training and sampling in energy-based generative models within a single framework using density transport on Wasserstein space cast as a nonlinear control problem, with KL divergence as Lyapunov function.

entry.title: CRAFT: Forgetting-Aware Intervention-Based Adaptation for Continual Learning

author.name: Md Anwar Hossen, Fatema Siddika, Juan Pablo Munoz, Tanya Roosta, Ali Jannesari

entry.summary: Proposes CRAFT, a continual learning framework for LLMs that learns low-rank interventions on hidden representations instead of updating model weights, with KL-based routing, regularization, and merging.

entry.title: Full-Spectrum Graph Neural Network: Expressive and Scalable

author.name: Xiaohan Wang, Deyu Bo, Longlong Li, Kelin Xia

entry.summary: Proposes Full-Spectrum GNN (FSpecGNN) that lifts spectral graph filtering from node domain to node-pair domain with bivariate filters over eigenvalue pairs, provably exceeding 1-WL expressivity.

entry.title: QuadraSHAP: Stable and Scalable Shapley Values for Product Games via Gauss-Legendre Quadrature

author.name: Majid Mohammadi, Grigory Reznikov, Pavel Sinitcyn, Krikamol Muandet, Siu Lun Chau

entry.summary: Shows that Shapley values for product games admit exact one-dimensional integral representations, yielding a Gauss-Legendre quadrature scheme that is provably exact with ⌈d/2⌉ nodes for d features.

entry.title: Near-Policy: Accelerating On-Policy Distillation via Asynchronous Generation and Selective Packing

author.name: Miao Rang, Zhenni Bi, Hang Zhou, Kai Han, Xuechun Wang, An Xiao, Xinghao Chen, Yunhe Wang, Hanting Chen

entry.summary: Proposes Near-Policy Distillation (NPD) that decouples student generation from training via asynchronous processing, enabling SFT with sequence packing while managing policy lag through sparse updates and filtering.

entry.title: Optimal Transport for LLM Reward Modeling from Noisy Preference

author.name: Licheng Pan, Haochen Yang, Haoxuan Li, Yunsheng Lu, Yongqi Tong, Yinuo Wang, Shijian Wang, Zhixuan Chu, Lei Shen, Yuan Lu, Hao Wang

entry.summary: Proposes SelectiveRM for robust reward modeling using optimal transport, with Joint Consistency Discrepancy and Mass Relaxation to handle noisy preference labels without overfitting.

entry.title: Towards Generation-Efficient Uncertainty Estimation in Large Language Models

author.name: Mingcheng Zhu, Yu Liu, Tingting Zhu

entry.summary: Investigates whether effective uncertainty estimation in LLMs can be achieved with partial generation or input-only information, developing a unified framework for early uncertainty estimation.

entry.title: Understanding diffusion models requires rethinking (again) generalization

author.name: Pierre Marion, Yu-Han Wu

entry.summary: Position paper arguing that understanding generalization in diffusion models requires fundamentally new theoretical frameworks, since memorization and generalization are incompatible in generative models (memorized models produce copies, not novel data). Surveys existing explanations and identifies gaps.

entry.title: Memory Inception: Latent-Space KV Cache Manipulation for Steering LLMs

author.name: Andy Zeyi Liu, Michael Zhang, Ilana Greenberg, Adam Alnasser, Lucas Baker, John Sous

entry.summary: Introduces Memory Inception (MI), a training-free method for steering LLMs by inserting text-derived key-value banks at selected layers, combining the control strength of prompting with the compactness of activation steering.

entry.title: SMolLM: Small Language Models Learn Small Molecular Grammar

author.name: Akhil Jindal, Harang Ju

entry.summary: Trains SMolLM, a 53K-parameter weight-shared transformer achieving 95% SMILES validity on ZINC-250K, outperforming 10x larger GPTs. Mechanistic analysis reveals the model resolves chemical constraints in fixed order across passes.

entry.title: Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation: Bridging Exploitation and Imitation at the Token Level

author.name: Nan Jia, Haojin Yang, Xing Ma, Jiesong Lian, Shuailiang Zhang, Weipeng Zhang, Ke Zeng, Xunliang Cai, Zequn Sun

entry.summary: Proposes Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation (AOPD) that replaces negative reinforcement with localized divergence minimization in non-positive advantage regions while preserving positive reinforcement, improving mathematical reasoning.

entry.title: SparseForge: Efficient Semi-Structured LLM Sparsification via Annealing of Hessian-Guided Soft-Mask

author.name: Liu Hanzuo, Chaofan Lin, Weixuan Sun, Yulong Wang, Key, Rayying, Mingyu Gao

entry.summary: Proposes SparseForge for post-training semi-structured (2:4) sparsification of LLMs using Hessian-aware importance estimation with progressive annealing of soft masks, achieving efficient sparse recovery without large-scale retraining.

entry.title: Is One Layer Enough? Understanding Inference Dynamics in Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Amir Rezaei Balef, Mykhailo Koshil, Katharina Eggensperger

entry.summary: Presents the first large-scale mechanistic study of layerwise dynamics in 6 tabular foundation models, revealing substantial depth redundancy. A proof-of-concept looped single-layer model achieves comparable performance using only 20% of parameters.

entry.title: BRICKS: Compositional Neural Markov Kernels for Zero-Shot Radiation-Matter Simulation

author.name: Richard Hildebrandt, Evangelos Kourlitis, Baran Hashemi, Manuel B\"unstorf, Thierry Meyer, Nikola Boskov, Michael Kagan, Dan Rosenbaum, Sanmay Ganguly, Lukas Heinrich

entry.summary: Introduces BRICKS, compositional neural surrogates for radiation-matter interactions using next-particle prediction kernels based on Riemannian Flow Matching on product manifolds. Enables zero-shot simulation of unseen material distributions.

entry.title: How Many Iterations to Jailbreak? Dynamic Budget Allocation for Multi-Turn LLM Evaluation

author.name: Shai Feldman, Yaniv Romano

entry.summary: Introduces DAPRO, a dynamic budget allocation framework for multi-turn LLM evaluation that provides theoretically valid lower predictive bounds on iterations needed to trigger events like jailbreaks, improving over static allocation.

entry.title: Maximizing Rollout Informativeness under a Fixed Budget: A Submodular View of Tree Search for Tool-Use Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yuelin Hu, Zhenbo Yu, Zhengxue Cheng, Wei Liu, Li Song

entry.summary: Formalizes Rollout Informativeness under Fixed Budget for tool-use agentic RL, proving that naive sampling suffers collapse for hard prompts, and recasting state selection as submodular maximization with 1-1/e guarantee.

entry.title: Understanding Annotator Safety Policy with Interpretability

author.name: Alex Oesterling, Donghao Ren, Yannick Assogba, Dominik Moritz, Sunnie S. Y. Kim, Leon Gatys, Fred Hohman

entry.summary: Studies annotator disagreement in AI safety labeling, distinguishing operational failures, policy ambiguity, and value pluralism using interpretability methods applied to annotator models.

entry.title: Spectral Lens: Activation and Gradient Spectra as Diagnostics of LLM Optimization

author.name: Andy Zeyi Liu, Elliot Paquette, John Sous

entry.summary: Introduces spectral diagnostics (activation covariance and per-sample gradient SVD spectra) for understanding LLM training dynamics. Reveals that batch size acts as a latent determinant of representation geometry and that early activation covariance tails predict downstream token efficiency.

entry.title: Autoregressive Visual Generation Needs a Prologue

author.name: Bowen Zheng, Weijian Luo, Guang Yang, Colin Zhang, Tianyang Hu

entry.summary: Proposes Prologue, which generates a small set of 'prologue tokens' prepended to visual token sequences for autoregressive image generation, decoupling generation optimization from reconstruction quality. Reduces gFID from 21.01 to 10.75 on ImageNet 256×256.

entry.title: Rethinking Adapter Placement: A Dominant Adaptation Module Perspective

author.name: Suoxin Zhang, Run He, Di Fang, Xiang Tan, Kaixuan Chen, Huiping Zhuang

entry.summary: Proposes PAGE (Projected Adapter Gradient Energy) to identify optimal placement for LoRA adapters, finding that a single shallow FFN down-projection layer concentrates most of the trainable gradient energy, leading to 'Dominant Adaptation Module' discovery.

entry.title: LatentRAG: Latent Reasoning and Retrieval for Efficient Agentic RAG

author.name: Yijia Zheng, Marcel Worring

entry.summary: Proposes LatentRAG, which shifts both reasoning and retrieval in agentic RAG from discrete language space to continuous latent space, reducing latency from autoregressive generation of intermediate thoughts and subqueries.

entry.title: FedAttr: Towards Privacy-preserving Client-Level Attribution in Federated LLM Fine-tuning

author.name: Su Zhang, Junfeng Guo, Heng Huang

entry.summary: Addresses the challenge of identifying which client in federated learning contributed watermarked data, despite secure aggregation hiding individual updates. Proposes FedAttr for privacy-preserving client-level attribution during federated LLM fine-tuning.

entry.title: Are We Making Progress in Multimodal Domain Generalization? A Comprehensive Benchmark Study

author.name: Hao Dong, Hongzhao Li, Shupan Li, Muhammad Haris Khan, Eleni Chatzi, Olga Fink

entry.summary: Introduces MMDG-Bench, the first unified benchmark for multimodal domain generalization that covers action recognition and beyond, including input corruptions, missing modalities, and model trustworthiness, questioning whether reported gains reflect genuine progress.

entry.title: Negative Before Positive: Asymmetric Valence Processing in Large Language Models

author.name: Sohan Venkatesh

entry.summary: Uses activation patching and steering to discover that LLMs process negative and positive emotional valence at different network depths—negative in early layers, positive in mid-to-late layers—demonstrating dedicated internal structure for emotion processing.

entry.title: Estimating the Black-box LLM Uncertainty with Distribution-Aligned Adversarial Distillation

author.name: Huizi Cui, Huan Ma, Qilin Wang, Yuhang Gao, Changqing Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes DisAAD for estimating uncertainty of black-box LLMs via a lightweight proxy model trained with adversarial distillation to learn the output distribution, avoiding expensive multiple sampling.

entry.title: Litespark Inference on Consumer CPUs: Custom SIMD Kernels for Ternary Neural Networks

author.name: Nii Osae Osae Dade, Tony Morri, Moinul Hossain Rahat, Sayandip Pal

entry.summary: Develops custom SIMD kernels for ternary neural networks that replace matrix multiplication with addition/subtraction operations, enabling LLM inference on consumer CPUs without GPUs.

entry.title: Cited but Not Verified: Parsing and Evaluating Source Attribution in LLM Deep Research Agents

author.name: Hailey Onweller, Elias Lumer, Austin Huber, Pia Ramchandani, Vamse Kumar Subbiah, Corey Feld

entry.summary: Introduces a source attribution evaluation framework using AST parsing to extract and verify inline citations in LLM-generated reports at scale, closing the loop by retrieving actual cited content for verification.

entry.title: StraTA: Incentivizing Agentic Reinforcement Learning with Strategic Trajectory Abstraction

author.name: Xiangyuan Xue, Yifan Zhou, Zidong Wang, Shengji Tang, Philip Torr, Wanli Ouyang, Lei Bai, Zhenfei Yin

entry.summary: Introduces StraTA, which adds explicit trajectory-level strategy to agentic RL by sampling compact strategies from initial states, conditioning actions on strategies, and training both jointly with hierarchical GRPO.

entry.title: ReFlect: An Effective Harness System for Complex Long-Horizon LLM Reasoning

author.name: Fan Huang

entry.summary: Introduces ReFlect, a deterministic wrapper system for LLM reasoning that provides standalone error detection and recovery logic for long-horizon tasks. Shows that standard prompt-level self-critique fails (flags no issues in 90/100 cases) while their external harness approach improves error recovery.

entry.title: On Time, Within Budget: Constraint-Driven Online Resource Allocation for Agentic Workflows

author.name: Xinglin Wang, Zishen Liu, Shaoxiong Feng, Peiwen Yuan, Yiwei Li, Jiayi Shi, Yueqi Zhang, Chuyi Tan, Ji Zhang, Boyuan Pan, Yao Hu, Kan Li

entry.summary: Studies constraint-driven online resource allocation for agentic workflows where tasks must be completed within specific budgets and deadlines. Shifts focus from average efficiency to maximizing probability of workflow completion under explicit constraints.

entry.title: iTRIALSPACE: Programmable Virtual Lesion Trials for Controlled Evaluation of Lung CT Models

author.name: Fakrul Islam Tushar, Umme Hafsa Momy, Joseph Y. Lo, Geoffrey D. Rubin

entry.summary: Introduces iTRIALSPACE, a programmable evaluation framework for lung CT models that creates controlled virtual lesion trials using ControlNet-conditioned CT synthesis. Enables systematic evaluation across 54 nodule attributes from 13,140 annotated nodules.

entry.title: VideoRouter: Query-Adaptive Dual Routing for Efficient Long-Video Understanding

author.name: Kuanwei Lin, Wenhao Zhang, Ge Li

entry.summary: Presents VideoRouter, a query-adaptive dual-router framework for efficient long-video understanding that allocates visual tokens based on where evidence is distributed temporally. Uses semantic and image routers for budget-aware evidence allocation.

entry.title: Think, then Score: Decoupled Reasoning and Scoring for Video Reward Modeling

author.name: Yuan Wang, Ouxiang Li, Yulong Xu, Borui Liao, Jiajun Liang, Jinghan Li, Meng Wang, Xintao Wang, Pengfei Wang, Kuien Liu, Xiang Wang

entry.summary: Proposes decoupled reasoning and scoring for video reward models, separating Chain-of-Thought reasoning from reward prediction. Aims to combine interpretability of generative RMs with accuracy of discriminative RMs.

entry.title: Whole-body CT attenuation and volume charts from routine clinical scans via evidence-grounded LLM report filtering

author.name: Christian Wachinger, Bernhard Renger, Christopher Sp\"ath, Jan Kirschke, Marcus Makowski

entry.summary: Uses an LLM ensemble to filter pathological findings from 350,000+ CT radiology reports, enabling construction of healthy reference distributions for organ volume and tissue attenuation across age and sex.

entry.title: Metonymy in vision models undermines attention-based interpretability

author.name: Ananthu Aniraj, Cassio F. Dantas, Dino Ienco, Massimiliano Mancini, Diego Marcos

entry.summary: Demonstrates that modern vision models exhibit 'metonymy' - the latent representation of an object part encodes information about distant parts, violating the locality assumption that underpins attention-based interpretability methods.

entry.title: MedHorizon: Towards Long-context Medical Video Understanding in the Wild

author.name: Bodong Du, Bowen Liu, Yang Yu, Xinpeng Ding, Zhiheng Wu, Shuning Wang, Shuo Nie, Naiming Liu, Qifeng Chen, Yangqiu Song, Xiaomeng Li

entry.summary: MedHorizon is a benchmark for long-context medical video understanding preserving 759 hours of full-length clinical procedures with 1,253 evidence-grounded questions requiring temporal localization before reasoning.

entry.title: Large Vision-Language Models Get Lost in Attention

author.name: Gongli Xi, Ye Tian, Mengyu Yang, Huahui Yi, Liang Lin, Xiaoshuai Hao, Kun Wang, Wendong Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a unified information-theoretic and geometric framework to analyze attention and MLP modules in LVLMs, revealing that attention preserves subspaces while MLPs inject new information, providing theoretical grounding for optimization.

entry.title: OA-WAM: Object-Addressable World Action Model for Robust Robot Manipulation

author.name: Yushan Liu, Peibo Sun, Shoujie Li, Yifan Xie, Lingfeng Zhang, Xintao Chao, Shiyuan Dong, Fang Chen, Xiao-Ping Zhang, Wenbo Ding

entry.summary: Proposes OA-WAM, which decomposes world action model predictions into object-addressable slot states (robot slot + N object slots) with persistent address vectors and time-varying content vectors, enabling robust object-referenced manipulation under scene shifts.

entry.title: Structural Correspondence and Universal Approximation in Diagonal plus Low-Rank Neural Networks

author.name: Ying Chen, Aoxi Li, Jihun Kim, Javad Lavaei

entry.summary: Studies the expressive power of diagonal plus low-rank neural networks, showing that purely low-rank layers collapse for function approximation but diagonal+low-rank structure achieves universal approximation with parameter efficiency.

entry.title: Do Neural Operators Forget Geometry? The Forgetting Hypothesis in Deep Operator Learning

author.name: Yanming Xia, Angelica I. Aviles-Rivero

entry.summary: Formalizes the Geometric Forgetting Hypothesis: neural operators progressively lose access to domain geometry with depth due to Markovian structure, and proposes geometric residual injection to counteract it.

entry.title: MANTRA: Synthesizing SMT-Validated Compliance Benchmarks for Tool-Using LLM Agents

author.name: Ashwani Anand, Ivi Chatzi, Ritam Raha, Anne-Kathrin Schmuck

entry.summary: Presents MANTRA, a framework for automatically synthesizing SMT-validated compliance benchmarks from natural-language manuals and tool schemas to evaluate tool-using LLM agents.

entry.title: CAR: Query-Guided Confidence-Aware Reranking for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Zhipeng Song, Yizhi Zhou, Xiangyu Kong, Jiulong Jiao, Xuezhou Ye, Chunqi Gao, Xueqing Shi, Yuhang Zhou, Heng Qi

entry.summary: Proposes CAR, a training-free reranking framework for RAG that uses generator confidence change as a document usefulness signal, promoting documents that increase answer confidence and demoting those that decrease it.

entry.title: Adaptive Q-Chunking for Offline-to-Online Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Nandiraju Gireesh, Yuanliang Ju, He Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Adaptive Q-Chunking (AQC) for offline-to-online RL that dynamically selects action chunk sizes based on state context, using advantage comparison to resolve discount-scale mismatch between different chunk lengths.

entry.title: Matrix-Decoupled Concentration for Autoregressive Sequences: Dimension-Free Guarantees for Sparse Long-Context Rewards

author.name: Pei-Sen Li

entry.summary: Establishes sharp McDiarmid-type concentration bounds for autoregressive LLM sequences that avoid the O(N) variance inflation of classical methods for sparse terminal rewards.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Simplicial Message Passing

author.name: Elena Xinyi Wang, Bastian Rieck

entry.summary: Introduces Geometric Simplicial Weisfeiler-Lehman (GSWL) test that incorporates vertex coordinates into simplicial complex color refinement, enabling geometry-aware message passing beyond standard WL.

entry.title: Taming the Entropy Cliff: Variable Codebook Size Quantization for Autoregressive Visual Generation

author.name: Bowen Zheng, Weijian Luo, Guang Yang, Colin Zhang, Tianyang Hu

entry.summary: Proposes variable codebook sizes across token positions for visual tokenizers, identifying the 'Entropy Cliff' phenomenon where conditional entropy drops to near-zero after the first few positions, making large fixed codebooks wasteful.

entry.title: A$^2$TGPO: Agentic Turn-Group Policy Optimization with Adaptive Turn-level Clipping

author.name: Dingwei Chen, Zefang Zong, Zhipeng Ma, Leo Luo, Yang Li, Chengming Li, Peng Chen, Jie Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes A²TGPO for agentic LLM RL that uses turn-group policy optimization with adaptive clipping and Information Gain signals for better credit assignment in multi-turn tool-calling interactions.

entry.title: EgoEMG: A Multimodal Egocentric Dataset with Bilateral EMG and Vision for Hand Pose Estimation

author.name: Ziheng Xi, Jiayi Yu, Yitao Wang, Yanbo Duan, Jianjiang Feng, Jie Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces EgoEMG, the first dataset synchronizing bilateral wrist EMG with egocentric video for bimanual hand pose estimation, covering 41 participants performing 60 gestures with comprehensive sensor suite.

entry.title: Render, Don't Decode: Weight-Space World Models with Latent Structural Disentanglement

author.name: Roussel Desmond Nzoyem, Mauro Comi

entry.summary: NOVA represents world model states as weights of implicit neural representations (INRs), enabling analytical rendering without decoder networks while providing compactness, portability, and zero-shot super-resolution.

entry.title: Temporal Reasoning Is Not the Bottleneck: A Probabilistic Inconsistency Framework for Neuro-Symbolic QA

author.name: Tran Quang Liem

entry.summary: Challenges the prevailing narrative that temporal reasoning is the fundamental bottleneck in LLMs, arguing instead that the failure lies in unstructured text-to-event representation. Introduces a neuro-symbolic QA framework with a Probabilistic Inconsistency Signal that decouples perceptual errors from reasoning failures.

entry.title: Executable World Models for ARC-AGI-3 in the Era of Coding Agents

author.name: Sergey Rodionov

entry.summary: Evaluates a coding-agent system for ARC-AGI-3 that maintains an executable Python world model, verifies against observations, refactors toward simpler abstractions (MDL-like bias), and plans through the model. Reports results on 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games.

entry.title: FASQ: Flexible Accelerated Subspace Quantization for Calibration-Free LLM Compression

author.name: Ye Qiao, Yian Wang, Zhiheng Chen, Hyoukjun Kwon, Sitao Huang

entry.summary: Presents FASQ, a calibration-free LLM compression framework using product quantization that provides continuous compression ratios (27-49% model size) beyond fixed bit-width schemes. Surpasses 4-bit GPTQ and AWQ on Llama-3-8B.

entry.title: LLMs Uncertainty Quantification via Adaptive Conformal Semantic Entropy

author.name: Hamed Karimi, Vaishali Meyappan, Reza Samavi

entry.summary: Proposes Adaptive Conformal Semantic Entropy (ACSE) for LLM uncertainty quantification, adaptively measuring semantic dispersion by clustering semantic entropy of diverse responses to the same prompt.

entry.title: Worst-Case Discovery and Runtime Protection for RL-Based Network Controllers

author.name: Hongyu H\`e, Minhao Jin, Maria Apostolaki

entry.summary: Presents ReGuard, a framework that discovers worst-case scenarios for RL-based network controllers and protects them at inference time without retraining. Uses bilevel regret-maximization to find failure cases and provides certified lower bounds on worst-case performance.

entry.title: Average Attention Transformers and Arithmetic Circuits

author.name: Lena Ehrmuth, Laura Strieker

entry.summary: Analyzes the computational power of average attention transformers, showing they can simulate arithmetic circuits given as input, establishing connections between transformer expressiveness and circuit complexity classes.

entry.title: Evolving Idea Graphs with Learnable Edits-and-Commits for Multi-Agent Scientific Ideation

author.name: Jiangwen Dong, Bo Li, Wanyu Lin

entry.summary: Introduces Evolving Idea Graphs (EIG), a graph-based multi-agent framework for scientific ideation where nodes capture claims and edges encode relations, with learnable edit-and-commit operations for iterative refinement.

entry.title: When Does Gene Regulatory Network Inference Break? A Controlled Diagnostic Study of Causal and Correlational Methods on Single-Cell Data

author.name: Miguel Fernandez-de-Retana, Ruben Sanchez-Corcuera, Unai Zulaika, Aritz Bilbao-Jayo, Aitor Almeida

entry.summary: Introduces a controlled diagnostic framework to understand when and why causal methods fail compared to correlation-based baselines for gene regulatory network inference from single-cell data, isolating seven biologically motivated pathologies.

entry.title: Why Geometric Continuity Emerges in Deep Neural Networks: Residual Connections and Rotational Symmetry Breaking

author.name: Kyungwon Jeong, Won-Gi Paeng, Honggyo Suh

entry.summary: Explains why weight matrices in deep networks exhibit geometric continuity (similar singular vectors across layers) through two mechanisms: residual connections creating gradient coherence and symmetry-breaking nonlinearities constraining layers to a shared coordinate frame.

entry.title: Piper: Efficient Large-Scale MoE Training via Resource Modeling and Pipelined Hybrid Parallelism

author.name: Sajal Dash, Feiyi Wang

entry.summary: Develops Piper, a system for efficient large-scale MoE training that addresses memory, communication, and workload imbalance challenges through mathematical resource modeling and pipelined hybrid parallelism on HPC platforms.

entry.title: Continual Knowledge Updating in LLM Systems: Learning Through Multi-Timescale Memory Dynamics

author.name: Andreas Pattichis, Constantine Dovrolis

entry.summary: Proposes Memini, a bio-inspired external memory system for LLMs using coupled multi-timescale dynamics (fast/slow variables based on Benna-Fusi synaptic consolidation) that enables episodic sensitivity, gradual consolidation, and selective forgetting.

entry.title: SAT: Sequential Agent Tuning for Coordinator Free Plug and Play Multi-LLM Training with Monotonic Improvement Guarantees

author.name: Yi Xie, Yangyang Xu, Yi Fan, Bo Liu

entry.summary: Introduces Sequential Agent Tuning (SAT), a coordinator-free training paradigm for teams of smaller LLMs that uses block-coordinate updates with monotonic improvement guarantees, avoiding distribution shift issues of joint training.

entry.title: Structural Instability of Feature Composition

author.name: Yunpeng Zhou

entry.summary: Analyzes the instability of compositional steering with Sparse Autoencoders through a geometric framework, deriving a compositional-collapse threshold and characterizing conditions where simultaneously activating multiple features breaks down.

entry.title: Information Theoretic Adversarial Training of Large Language Models

author.name: Yiwei Zhang, Jeremiah Birrell, Reza Ebrahimi, Rouzbeh Behnia, Jason Pacheco, Elisa Bertino

entry.summary: Proposes WARDEN, a distributionally robust adversarial training framework for LLMs that dynamically reweights adversarial examples using information-theoretic principles to improve robustness against jailbreaks.

entry.title: GRALIS: A Unified Canonical Framework for Linear Attribution Methods via Riesz Representation

author.name: Raimondo Fanale

entry.summary: Presents GRALIS, a unified mathematical framework using Riesz Representation Theorem to prove that SHAP, IG, LIME and linearized GradCAM all admit a canonical representation, enabling formal comparison and simultaneous guarantees.

entry.title: Shortcut Solutions Learned by Transformers Impair Continual Compositional Reasoning

author.name: William T. Redman, Erik C. Johnson, Brian Robinson

entry.summary: Investigates how Transformers develop shortcut solutions that impair their ability to continually learn compositional reasoning tasks. Extends the LEGO framework to a continual learning setting to systematically study representation reuse across related tasks.

entry.title: Towards Scalable One-Step Generative Modeling for Autoregressive Dynamical System Forecasting

author.name: Tianyue Yang, Xiao Xue

entry.summary: Proposes MeLISA, a latent-free autoregressive generative surrogate for physical dynamics forecasting built on pixel-space MeanFlow, designed for one-step generation that preserves long-term statistical structure.

entry.title: Optimal Contextual Pricing under Agnostic Non-Lipschitz Demand

author.name: Jianyu Xu, Yu-Xiang Wang

entry.summary: Achieves optimal O(T^{2/3}) regret for contextual dynamic pricing with non-Lipschitz demand curves, improving over previous O(T^{3/4}) results and matching known lower bounds.

entry.title: A Measure-Theoretic Finite-Sample Theory for Adaptive-Data Fitted Q-Iteration

author.name: Manuel Haussmann, Mustafa Mert \c{C}elikok, Melih Kandemir

entry.summary: Bridges the gap between theoretical RL foundations and practical deep RL by combining measure-theoretic MDP analysis, deterministic error propagation, and PAC generalization bounds for fitted Q-iteration.

entry.title: Multi-agent decision making: A Blackwell's informativeness approach

author.name: Zheng Zhang, Cuong C. Nguyen, Kevin Wells, Gustavo Carneiro

entry.summary: Applies Blackwell's informativeness framework to analyze multi-agent LLM decision making, proving that voting and debate are no more informative than pooled Bayesian posterior maximization.

entry.title: One Algorithm, Two Goals: Dual Scoring for Parameter and Data Selection in LLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: Xinrui Chen, Liu Yang, Ou Wu

entry.summary: Casts parameter and data selection in LLM fine-tuning as bilevel optimization problems sharing a common scoring rule, showing parameter importance and data utility are row-wise and column-wise aggregations of a single gradient interaction matrix.

entry.title: Topological Signatures of Grokking

author.name: Yifan Tang, Qiquan Wang, In\'es Garc\'ia-Redondo, Anthea Monod

entry.summary: Studies grokking through persistent homology, identifying a topological signature (sharp increase in H1 persistence) that coincides with grokking on modular arithmetic tasks and reflects emergence of cyclic structure.

entry.title: Memory Efficient Full-gradient Attacks (MEFA) Framework for Adversarial Defense Evaluations

author.name: Yuan Du, Mitchel Hill, HanQin Cai

entry.summary: Shows that gradient checkpointing enables exact full-gradient attacks through long diffusion purification trajectories, providing more rigorous robustness evaluation of stochastic purification defenses than approximate backpropagation.

entry.title: MinMax Recurrent Neural Cascades

author.name: Alessandro Ronca

entry.summary: Shows that MinMax algebra provides recurrence that is expressively powerful (all regular languages), efficiently parallelizable (log-time), and free from vanishing/exploding gradients, forming MinMax Recurrent Neural Cascades.

entry.title: Efficient Serving for Dynamic Agent Workflows with Prediction-based KV-Cache Management

author.name: Haoyu Zheng, Fangcheng Fu, Jia Wu, Binhang Yuan, Yongqiang Zhang, Hao Wang, Yuanyuan Zhu, Xiao Yan, Jiawei Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes PBKV for efficient LLM agent workflow serving that predicts agent invocation sequences in dynamic workflows and manages KV-Cache reuse accordingly, addressing limitations of static workflow assumptions.

entry.title: PACZero: PAC-Private Fine-Tuning of Language Models via Sign Quantization

author.name: Murat Bilgehan Ertan, Xiaochen Zhu, Phuong Ha Nguyen, Marten van Dijk, Srinivas Devadas

entry.summary: Introduces PACZero, a PAC-private zeroth-order mechanism for fine-tuning LLMs that achieves zero mutual information privacy while maintaining usable utility. This achieves MIA resistance that differential privacy only matches at epsilon=0.

entry.title: Diffusion-Based Posterior Sampling: A Feynman-Kac Analysis of Bias and Stability

author.name: Matias G. Delgadino, Sebastien Motsch, Advait Parulekar, William Porteous, Sanjay Shakkottai

entry.summary: Provides theoretical characterization of bias in diffusion-based posterior samplers using Feynman-Kac analysis. Identifies which posterior geometries concentrate bias and derives explicit path expectation corrections.

entry.title: Weight-Decay Turns Transformer Loss Landscapes Villani: Functional-Analytic Foundations for Optimization and Generalization

author.name: Abhijit Das, Sayantan Dutta

entry.summary: Provides the first rigorous functional-analytic proof that the standard Transformer loss with weight decay satisfies Villani's criteria for coercive energy functions, deriving exponential convergence guarantees for Langevin training.

entry.title: When No Benchmark Exists: Validating Comparative LLM Safety Scoring Without Ground-Truth Labels

author.name: Sushant Gautam, Finn Schwall, Annika Willoch Olstad, Fernando Vallecillos Ruiz, Birk Torpmann-Hagen, Sunniva Maria Stordal Bj{\o}rklund, Leon Moonen, Klas Pettersen, Michael A. Riegler

entry.summary: Formalizes 'benchmarkless comparative safety scoring' for LLMs when no labeled safety benchmark exists for the target language/sector. Proposes an instrumental-validity chain using controlled contrasts and variance analysis.

entry.title: DexSim2Real: Foundation Model-Guided Sim-to-Real Transfer for Generalizable Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Zijian Zeng, Fei Ding, Huiming Yang, Xianwei Li, Yuhao Liao

entry.summary: Presents DexSim2Real, a framework using vision-language foundation models to bridge sim-to-real transfer for dexterous manipulation, combining FM-guided domain randomization with visual realism criticism.

entry.title: Architecture Matters: Comparing RAG Systems under Knowledge Base Poisoning

author.name: Samuel Korn

entry.summary: Evaluates four RAG architectures (vanilla, agentic, MADAM-RAG, recursive LMs) under adversarial knowledge base poisoning, finding that architecture significantly affects robustness to attacks.

entry.title: DBMSolver: A Training-free Diffusion Bridge Sampler for High-Quality Image-to-Image Translation

author.name: Sankarshana Venugopal (Seoul National University), Mohammad Mostafavi (Seoul National University), Jonghyun Choi (Seoul National University)

entry.summary: Introduces DBMSolver, a training-free sampler for Diffusion Bridge Models that uses exponential integrators to reduce function evaluations by up to 5x while improving quality (53% FID reduction) for image-to-image translation tasks.

entry.title: Gaming the Metric, Not the Harm: Certifying Safety Audits against Strategic Platform Manipulation

author.name: Florian A. D. Burnat, Brittany I. Davidson

entry.summary: Formalizes how online safety platforms can game audit metrics by routing through semantically equivalent content variants, and proves that any metric scoring variants directly is manipulable. Proposes class-level aggregation as a defense.

entry.title: Beyond the Independence Assumption: Finite-Sample Guarantees for Deep Q-Learning under $\tau$-Mixing

author.name: Leon Halgryn (University of Twente), Sophie Langer (Ruhr-Universit\"at Bochum), Janusz M. Meylahn (University of Twente), E. Moritz Hahn (University of Twente)

entry.summary: Extends DQN finite-sample analysis to dependent data by modeling replay buffer minibatches as τ-mixing processes, providing the first risk bounds for deep Q-learning that don't assume independence.

entry.title: ReActor: Reinforcement Learning for Physics-Aware Motion Retargeting

author.name: David M\"uller, Agon Serifi, Sammy Christen, Ruben Grandia, Espen Knoop, Moritz B\"acher

entry.summary: Proposes a bilevel optimization framework (ReActor) that jointly adapts human reference motions to robot morphology while training a tracking policy via RL. It eliminates manual tuning by using approximate gradients and sparse semantic correspondences, addressing physical inconsistencies like foot sliding and self-collisions.

entry.title: Superintelligent Retrieval Agent: The Next Frontier of Information Retrieval

author.name: Zeyu Yang, Qi Ma, Jason Chen, Anshumali Shrivastava

entry.summary: Introduces SIRA (SuperIntelligent Retrieval Agent), which compresses multi-round exploratory search into single corpus-discriminative retrieval actions by building strong priors about terminology and evidence locations in large knowledge bases.

entry.title: A Few Good Clauses: Comparing LLMs vs Domain-Trained Small Language Models on Structured Contract Extraction

author.name: Nicole Lincoln, Nick Whitehouse, Jaron Mar, Rivindu Perera

entry.summary: Demonstrates that a domain-trained small language model (Olava Extract) can outperform frontier LLMs on structured contract extraction with 78-97% lower inference cost and higher precision, reducing hallucinations in legal workflows.

entry.title: SEQUOR: A Multi-Turn Benchmark for Realistic Constraint Following

author.name: Beatriz Canaverde, Duarte M. Alves, Jos\'e Pombal, Giuseppe Attanasio, Andr\'e F. T. Martins

entry.summary: Introduces SEQUOR, a benchmark for evaluating constraint adherence in long multi-turn conversations, showing that instruction-following accuracy drops over 11% as conversations grow longer, even for single constraints.
